## 03. Non-Deterministic Metrics: `pass@k` vs. `pass^k`
Because LLM generation is stochastic, running the exact same prompt and tool sequence $k$ times can produce different trajectories and outcomes. Picking the wrong multi-trial metric can make a brittle system look production-ready on paper while failing constantly for real users.

### Mathematical & Operational Contrast

Let $p \in [0, 1]$ be the single-trial probability that an agent or model completes a task correctly on one independent run, and let $k$ be the number of independent trials.

$$\text{pass}@k = 1 - (1 - p)^k \qquad \text{vs.} \qquad \text{pass}^k = p^k$$

| Metric | Formula (for single-run success $p$) | Meaning | Curve as $k$ Increases | When to Use | When It Is Dangerous |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **`pass@k`** *(At-Least-One Success)* | $1 - (1 - p)^k$ *(unbiased estimator over $n \ge k$ samples)* | Chance of seeing **one or more successes** across $k$ independent runs. | **Rises toward 100%** (masks underlying flakiness) | Code generation with a compiler/unit-test verifier; swarm tournament prototyping where a deterministic filter picks the single working output. | **Customer-facing chat or autonomous agents:** users only see 1 run, and side-effecting tools cannot be casually run 5 times hoping one works. |
| **`pass^k`** *(Every-Run Consistency)* | $p^k$ | Chance that **every single run across $k$ trials** succeeds without failure. | **Decays exponentially toward 0%** (exposes variance) | **Customer-facing agents**, unattended background automation, regulated workflows, and mutating tool pipelines where every invocation must be reliable. | Over-optimizing `pass^k` on purely creative brainstorming tasks where diversity across samples is desirable. |

### The Exponential Decay of Consistency (`pass^k` Table)

Notice how a single-run accuracy of $p = 0.90$ looks impressive on `pass@5` ($99.999\%$) while collapsing to $59.0\%$ on `pass^5` and $34.9\%$ on `pass^10`:

| Single-Run Accuracy ($p$) | `pass@1` / `pass^1` | `pass@5` ($1 - (1-p)^5$) | `pass^5` ($p^5$) | `pass^10` ($p^{10}$) | Operational Interpretation |
| :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :--- |
| **0.70 (70%)** | 70.0% | 99.8% | **16.8%** | **2.8%** | Usable for 5-sample code synthesis with unit tests; **unusable** for live automation. |
| **0.85 (85%)** | 85.0% | 99.99% | **44.4%** | **19.7%** | Fails more than half the time over 5 consecutive runs. |
| **0.90 (90%)** | 90.0% | 99.999% | **59.0%** | **34.9%** | Still fails **41% of 5-run consistency suites**. |
| **0.95 (95%)** | 95.0% | >99.999% | **77.4%** | **59.9%** | Minimum baseline before adding deterministic guardrails. |
| **0.99 (99%)** | 99.0% | >99.999% | **95.1%** | **90.4%** | Production-grade step reliability (achieved via code gates + schema constraints). |

### Compounding Multi-Step Accuracy Across Sequential Agent Steps

The exact same multiplicative law governs a single execution of a **multi-step sequential workflow**. If an agent must complete $M$ sequential steps (e.g., Classify Intent → Formulate Query → Select Tool → Parse Payload → Synthesize Final Answer) and each step has independent success probability $p_i$, end-to-end workflow success is the product of every step:

$$P(\text{Workflow Success}) = \prod_{i=1}^{M} p_i \quad \text{(or } p^M \text{ if each step has accuracy } p\text{)}$$

- **Example:** A 6-step autonomous workflow where every individual step scores **92%** in isolation ($p = 0.92$) has an end-to-end first-pass success rate of $0.92^6 \approx \mathbf{60.6\%}$—meaning nearly **4 out of 10 production runs fail**.
- **Architectural remedies to beat compounding decay:**
  1. **Replace probabilistic steps with deterministic workflow nodes:** If steps 2 and 4 can be written as standard code, ADK workflow edges, or strict schema validators ($p = 1.00$), a 6-step pipeline shrinks to 3 probabilistic hops ($0.92^3 \approx 77.9\%$).
  2. **Insert programmatic verification gates between steps:** Catch and auto-correct malformed tool arguments or schema errors at step $i$ before passing corrupt state to step $i+1$.
  3. **Bound step count:** Keep autonomous loops shallow and route predefined sequences through deterministic workflow orchestrators (`SequentialAgent`) rather than LLM routers.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Exam & production rule:** Whenever a scenario involves an unattended workflow, customer-facing support agent, or financial/database tool execution, evaluate readiness using **`pass^k`** (every trial succeeds) and **end-to-end trajectory completion**, never `pass@k`. Use `pass@k` only when a downstream deterministic verifier (such as a test suite or compiler) can automatically filter $k$ candidates before side effects occur.

---

## 04. The 4-Level Agent Test Pyramid & Integration Seams
Testing an agentic system exclusively through end-to-end live conversations is slow, expensive, and non-diagnostic; testing it exclusively through isolated unit tests misses catastrophic multi-step handoff failures. Production teams structure verification as a **4-Level Agent Test Pyramid**.

```
            /\          LEVEL 4: Live Canary & Online Monitors
           /L4\         (Async sampled rubrics, shadow runs — Continuous)
          /────\
         /  L3  \       LEVEL 3: Trajectory, Seam & Simulation Tests
        /────────\      (2-Step Sim + fault injection — Pre-Release)
       /    L2    \     LEVEL 2: Single-Step Component Evals
      /────────────\    (Isolated router/RAG golden slices — Per PR)
     /      L1      \   LEVEL 1: Deterministic Unit & Replay Tests
    /________________\  (Schemas, callbacks, conformance — Every Commit)
```

### The 4 Levels in Detail

| Level | Scope & Target | What Is Mocked vs. Live | Execution Cadence & Cost | What It Catches |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Level 1: Deterministic Unit & Replay Tests** | Tool JSON schemas, Pydantic validators, prompt template rendering, PII scrubbers, retry state machines, `adk conformance test --mode=replay` | **LLM is 100% mocked / replayed** from recorded fixtures. Pure code execution. | Every save / pre-commit hook · **Milliseconds to <5s · $0** | Broken schema definitions, template `KeyError` bugs, callback regressions, broken `state_delta` routing. |
| **Level 2: Single-Step Component Evals** | A single LLM call in isolation: intent router, entity extractor, query rewriter, or RAG answer generator | **Live LLM call** against a frozen, curated golden input + fixed context snapshot. | Every PR touching prompts/models · **Seconds to minutes · Low cost** | Prompt regressions, classification drift, hallucination on specific golden slices, schema compliance drops. |
| **Level 3: Trajectory & Seam Integration Tests** | Multi-turn agent loop across 2–8 steps: tool selection, argument passing, error recovery, subagent handoffs | **Live LLM + Environment Simulation / sandboxed test doubles** (including injected `503`, `429`, and empty-result fixtures). | Pre-release gate / nightly build · **Minutes · Moderate cost** | **Integration seam failures**, infinite tool loops, silent error swallowing, oversized tool payloads, state loss during compaction. |
| **Level 4: Live Canary & Online Monitors** | Real production traffic across the full deployed stack | **100% live** (canary slice, shadow pipeline, or 1–5% sampled **Online Evaluation Monitors**). | Continuous in production · **Budgeted % of prod spend** | Input/data drift, unpredicted user phrasing, latency spikes, real third-party API schema changes. |

### Why Integration Seams Hide Silent Bugs

An **integration seam** is the boundary where the output of Component A becomes the input of Component B (for example: *Query Rewriter → Hybrid Retriever*, *Tool Execution Output → Agent Context*, or *Planner Subagent → Executor Subagent*).

**Compound Error Cascades across Multi-Step Pipelines:** Every individual component can score **>95% in isolated component evaluations** while the end-to-end system fails on **>40% of real tasks** because independent step probabilities compound multiplicatively ($0.95^5 \approx 77\%$) and isolated evaluations feed idealized, clean inputs to each stage rather than handling noisy upstream artifacts.

| Seam Failure Pattern | How Component A Behaves ("Passes L2") | How Component B Breaks Across the Seam | Architectural Fix |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Format & Schema Drift** | Extractor outputs dates as `"Oct 26, 2026"` or wraps JSON in ```` ```json ```` markdown fences (passes loose L2 check). | Downstream SQL/API tool expects strict ISO-8601 `2026-10-26` or raw JSON and throws a validation/parse error. | Enforce **strict structured outputs** (`output_schema` / JSON Schema) at the seam and validate with a Level 1/3 contract test. |
| **Unbounded Tool Output & Silent Truncation** | Search tool dumps a 40,000-token raw log into context (diluting model attention), or middleware naively slices the first 4,000 chars. | Either attention degrades across turns (**context rot**) or the stack trace at the bottom is cut off, causing a confident *"No errors found"*. | Truncate structurally (head + tail + error lines, or return pagination metadata `truncated: true, next_cursor: "..."`). |
| **State Loss During Context Compaction** | Sliding-window summarizer compresses 12 prior turns into a 3-sentence prose paragraph. | Summarizer drops an exact UUID, config flag, or constraint read in Turn 2 that Turn 14 needs to execute a tool safely. | Persist exact IDs, constraints, and slot values in structured **Session `state`** (`session.state`), never solely in summarized prose. |
| **Swallowed Tool Failures (Empty vs. Error)** | Tool wrapper catches a database timeout (`504`) and returns `[]` or `""` so the pipeline doesn't crash. | The model interprets `[]` as ground truth (*"You have zero open orders"*) instead of a transient system outage. | Never conflate empty results with failures; return explicit structured error flags (`is_error: true`, error code, retryability). |
| **Distribution Shift Between Stages** | Query rewriter expands short user queries into 80-word boolean strings that were never in the retriever's golden set. | Dense embedding model loses specificity on 80-word keyword-stuffed queries, dropping top-5 recall by 30%. | Evaluate *Query Rewriter + Retriever* together as a coupled pair in Level 3 seam tests using end-to-end Recall@K. |

---

## 05. Observability, Distributed Tracing & Drift Detection
In a production agentic workflow, a single user message can fan out into Model Armor screening, hybrid vector retrieval, cross-encoder reranking, multi-turn `gemini-4-argon` or Claude reasoning calls, MCP tool executions, and A2A sub-agent delegations. Without standardized **distributed tracing**, diagnosing a 19-second stall, a reasoning loop, or a hallucination is guesswork.

### OpenTelemetry `gen_ai.*` Semantic Conventions & Agent Observability

Instrument every workflow with **OpenTelemetry (OTel) Semantic Conventions for Generative AI** (`gen_ai.*` attributes across `invoke_agent`, `chat`, and `execute_tool` spans) so traces render uniformly across **Google Cloud Trace**, **Agent Registry Observability**, and vendor-neutral APMs:

```
Trace (trace_id="tr_9f8a...", session_id="sess_42", is_agentic=true)
 ├─ Span 1: model_armor.screen_input  [14 ms | verdict=ALLOW]
 ├─ Span 2: retrieval.agent_search    [82 ms | top_k=20, rerank_n=5]
 ├─ Span 3: gen_ai.chat (Turn 1)      [1,180 ms | ttft=310 ms | tool_calls]
 │   └─ model="gemini-3.8-flash", in=4820, cached=4200, think=190, out=95
 ├─ Span 4: gen_ai.execute_tool       [640 ms | mcp:order | retry=1]
 └─ Span 5: gen_ai.chat (Turn 2)      [910 ms | ttft=240 ms | stop]
```

### Automatic Cloud Monitoring Metrics vs. OpenTelemetry `gen_ai.*` & Log-Based Metrics

Infrastructure and publisher-model telemetry arrive out of the box in **Cloud Monitoring (`GA`)** with zero code changes, whereas agent-level tool, session, loop-depth, and policy signals require **ADK OpenTelemetry semantic conventions** (`OTEL_SEMCONV_STABILITY_OPT_IN='gen_ai_latest_experimental'`) or **Cloud Logging log-based metrics**:

| Telemetry boundary | Specific metric types / attributes | Setup & cardinality rule |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Automatic Cloud Monitoring (`GA`, zero code changes)** | • **Cloud Run:** `run.googleapis.com/request_count`, `run.googleapis.com/request_latencies`, `run.googleapis.com/container/billable_instance_time`, `cpu/utilizations`, `memory/utilizations`.<br>• **GKE:** `kubernetes.io/container/*` (CPU, memory, storage, `restart_count`).<br>• **Agent Runtime & Agent Gateway:** request throughput, RPC/HTTP status errors, container CPU/memory usage, and `p50`/`p95`/`p99` runtime/gateway latency.<br>• **Model Platform Online Serving:** `aiplatform.googleapis.com/publisher/online_serving/token_count` and `aiplatform.googleapis.com/publisher/online_serving/model_invocation_latencies`. | Emitted automatically by Google Cloud control planes; tracks aggregate endpoint health and total project TPM/RPM, **not** which tool or session caused a spike. |
| **OTel GenAI (`gen_ai.*`) & Log-Based Metrics *(explicit opt-in)*** | • **Per-tool error rate:** `gen_ai.operation.name="execute_tool"` + `gen_ai.tool.name` + `status=ERROR` (`error.type`).<br>• **Per-session token spend:** `gen_ai.conversation.id` + `gen_ai.usage.input_tokens` / `gen_ai.usage.output_tokens` (counting `thinking_tokens` + A2A/subagent fan-out).<br>• **Reasoning loop depth:** child span count (`call_llm` + `execute_tool`) per root `trace_id`.<br>• **Policy & guardrail denials:** Agent Gateway request logs (`resource.type="networkservices.googleapis.com/Gateway"` with `jsonPayload.authzPolicyInfo.policies.result="DENIED"` / `httpRequest.status=403`), IAP Data Access audit logs (`protoPayload.serviceName="iap.googleapis.com"` with `protoPayload.authorizationInfo.granted=false` on `iap.resources.egressViaIAP`), and Model Armor blocks (`SanitizeOperationLogEntry`). | Enable ADK OTel (`--otel_to_cloud`, `GOOGLE_CLOUD_AGENT_ENGINE_ENABLE_TELEMETRY=true`, `AdkApp(..., enable_tracing=True)`, or `get_gcp_exporters(enable_cloud_tracing=True)` on Cloud Run/GKE; GKE also needs an Agent Registry entry for Topology). **Cardinality rule:** **never** attach `session_id`, `user_id`, or `trace_id` as a Cloud Monitoring metric label! |

The writer identity (usually the runtime service account) needs `roles/telemetry.tracesWriter`, `roles/logging.logWriter` and `roles/monitoring.metricWriter`. The ADK instrumentation guide's recommended environment for content-safe tracing:

```bash
GOOGLE_CLOUD_AGENT_ENGINE_ENABLE_TELEMETRY=true                # Agent Runtime only
OTEL_SEMCONV_STABILITY_OPT_IN=gen_ai_latest_experimental       # latest gen_ai conventions
OTEL_INSTRUMENTATION_GENAI_CAPTURE_MESSAGE_CONTENT=EVENT_ONLY  # messages as events, never "true"
ADK_CAPTURE_MESSAGE_CONTENT_IN_SPANS=false                     # no prompt text or PII in span attributes
```

- **High-cardinality metric label trap:** attaching unbounded `session_id` (`gen_ai.conversation.id`), `user_id`, or `trace_id` as a **Cloud Monitoring metric label** explodes active time-series cardinality, exhausts custom metric quotas, and spikes observability billing. Group Cloud Monitoring metrics only by bounded labels (`gen_ai.tool.name`, `model`, `status`), and query per-session or per-user breakdowns in **Cloud Logging Log Analytics**, **BigQuery log sinks**, or **Cloud Trace**.
- **Turning tracing on is a data decision:** once built-in instrumentation is enabled, text prompts and agent responses are sent to your project. Review it with the data owner, not only the SRE team.
- **Spans hold metadata, not conversations:** Agent Platform keeps latency, status codes and structure in spans and routes prompts and responses to Cloud Storage (recommended: no truncation, multimodal payloads, lifecycle rules) or Cloud Logging (text only, size limits). Because the two stores are separate, IAM can grant `roles/cloudtrace.user` for debugging without granting read access to conversation content.
- **`EVENT_ONLY`, never `true`:** with the latest `gen_ai` conventions, `OTEL_INSTRUMENTATION_GENAI_CAPTURE_MESSAGE_CONTENT=true` is an invalid configuration and no log or trace data is collected at all.
- **Media offload:** for images and large documents, set `OTEL_INSTRUMENTATION_GENAI_COMPLETION_HOOK=upload`, `OTEL_INSTRUMENTATION_GENAI_UPLOAD_FORMAT=jsonl` and `OTEL_INSTRUMENTATION_GENAI_UPLOAD_BASE_PATH=gs://...` so payloads land in a bucket instead of inside spans.
- **Online monitors depend on captured content:** they read `gen_ai.input.messages`, `gen_ai.output.messages`, `gen_ai.system_instructions` and `gen_ai.tool.definitions` from the inference event. Switching content capture off also switches off online evaluation, so address PII by redacting upstream (**Sensitive Data Protection** de-identification templates, **Model Armor**) and by restricting the log bucket (`roles/logging.privateLogViewer`) or Cloud Storage bucket.
- **Dual-Attribution Agentic Audit Logging (`is_agentic=true`):** When an agent acts on behalf of a human user, Cloud Audit Logs and execution logs tag events with `is_agentic=true` and record **both** (1) the cryptographic SPIFFE **Agent Identity** (`principal://...` / `spiffe://...`) and (2) the initiating **human user principal**, which removes "confused deputy" blind spots in forensics.

### Reading one agent turn in a trace

The agent's Traces tab offers a Session view (multi-turn conversations with session token totals and evaluation scores), a Trace view (one end-to-end request) and a Span view (individual model calls, API requests and tool executions). Open one trace for a single turn and walk it top-down:

| Order | Span to inspect | Healthy pattern | Investigate when |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1 | **Root `invoke_agent`** | One trace per user turn; total duration roughly equals the sum of child spans | A gap before the first child (cold start or blocking initialization), or one turn split across several traces (context propagation broken) |
| 2 | **LLM spans (`call_llm` wrapping `generate_content {model}`)** | A small, stable number of calls per turn; input tokens grow modestly turn over turn; each call ends in a final answer or a well-formed tool call | Input tokens climbing every turn (history bloat), output cut off at the token limit, repeated retries after `429` |
| 3 | **Tool spans (`execute_tool`; MCP calls carry `mcp.method.name = tools/call` and `gen_ai.tool.name`)** | Independent tools overlap in time; compact results; no `error.type` | Same tool with the same arguments three or more times in a row, `error.type` set, or a serial waterfall of multi-second calls |
| 4 | **Sub-agent handoffs (nested `invoke_agent` spans)** | A shallow parent-to-specialist tree that matches the intended design and the Topology tab's edges | A to B to A ping-pong, unexpected specialists, or depth that grows with every turn |
| 5 | **Retrieval spans (search and RAG tools appear as `execute_tool`)** | Fast, non-empty results whose content shows up in the final answer | Zero or irrelevant results followed by a confident answer (hallucination risk) |
| 6 | **Guardrail spans (Model Armor, Preview)** | Screening adds little latency and allows benign traffic | An empty or refused answer that a Model Armor interception explains, which rules out a retrieval miss |
| 7 | **Evaluation tab on the trace** | Online monitor scores and rationales agree with what you just read | Low scores on a trace that looks clean (check the rubric) or high scores on a broken one (check the autorater) |

### Troubleshooting Production Agent Issues via Telemetry Views

Agent Registry's Observability tab (Overview, Evaluation, Models, Tools, Usage, Logs) plus the agent's Traces and Topology tabs map production symptoms to root causes. The Models view isolates p95 latency, errors, quota failures and tokens per model; the Tools view shows p95 latency, call counts and error rates per tool, plus how often a turn called no tool at all.

| Symptom | Likely cause | Where to look | Fix |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Tool latency spike** (turn `p95` jumps while LLM time stays flat) | Unpooled database connections, cross-region hops, or independent reads executed one after another | Tools view `p95` per tool; Traces waterfall with long or serial `execute_tool` spans | Co-locate runtime and data, use **MCP Toolbox** connection pooling, fan out independent reads (`ParallelAgent`), set per-tool timeouts, cache hot lookups |
| **Reasoning or tool-call loops** | Ambiguous tool errors (an empty string instead of actionable feedback) or cyclic sub-agent routing | Traces: 8 or more consecutive `call_llm` and `execute_tool` pairs with identical or oscillating arguments; Topology for A to B to A edges | Return structured error hints (`ReflectAndRetryToolPlugin`), cap iterations (`max_llm_calls`, `max_iterations`), break cycles with deterministic state flags (per-cause fixes in the runaway loop triage table below) |
| **Ignored tools ("no-tool interactions")** | Vague or overlapping tool descriptions, so the model answers from parametric memory | Tools view no-tool rate alongside rising `HALLUCINATION` scores on domain questions | Sharpen tool descriptions and schemas; add `trajectory_in_order_match` CI gates |
| **Prefill or thinking bottleneck** | `thinking_level="HIGH"` on routine hops, or volatile text at the top of the prompt defeating prefix caching | Models and Traces views: `thinking_tokens` dominating generation time, high TTFT with `cached_tokens = 0` | Route simple steps to `gemini-3.5-flash-lite` (`minimal`) or `gemini-3.8-flash` (`low`); move volatile state after `static_instruction` |
| **Rising token cost** | Unbounded conversation history, large tool payloads, many tool schemas sent on every turn | Overview token usage (input vs. output); per-span input tokens growing turn over turn | ADK context compaction (token-based or sliding window), context caching, pruned tool results, tools and skills loaded on demand |
| **Hallucinated answers** | Empty or weak grounding, or the agent answering despite an empty retrieval | Evaluation view hallucination rate; retrieval span output compared with the final response | Ground on Agent Search or RAG Engine, add reranking, instruct the agent to abstain when retrieval returns nothing |
| **Retrieval misses** | Dense-only search missing exact codes and acronyms, or chunks stripped of their section headings | Retrieval `execute_tool` spans returning irrelevant or zero results | Hybrid (dense plus keyword) retrieval, chunking that keeps ancestor headings, reranking, corpus refresh |
| **Quality drift after a model or prompt change** | New model version or prompt edit changes tool selection, formatting or refusal behavior | Evaluation dashboard trends across agent versions; Automatic Loss Analysis clusters for the new version | Roll back to the prior pinned version, add failing traces to the golden set, re-run the optimizer before re-promoting (see `#feedback-flywheel`) |
| **`429` / quota errors** | Burst traffic or runaway loops exhausting model quota (`RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED`) | Models view quota failures; Cloud Logging entries with `429` | Full-jitter backoff (see `#resilience-stack`), loop caps, concurrency limits, Provisioned Throughput for predictable capacity |
| **Cold starts** | No idle instance when a request arrives; heavy imports and client setup at startup | Gap before the first child span on the first turn; instance count rising during spikes | Raise `min_instances` (Agent Runtime) or `--min-instances` (Cloud Run) to cover baseline load, lazy-load heavy libraries, slim images; for async ADK agents on Agent Runtime start `container_concurrency` at a multiple of 9 (for example 36) and watch memory |
| **Traces tab or online monitor empty** | Telemetry never enabled, or content capture disabled | Cloud Trace for `gen_ai.*` attributes; Logs Explorer filtered on `resource.labels.online_evaluator` | Apply the opt-in settings above; confirm monitor filters with Initial Inspection |

### Runaway loop triage

The loop row above names the shared symptom. Five different causes produce it, and each one needs its own fix. The common rule: a loop must never end on model judgment alone. An iteration cap, a terminal route or a budget has to end it.

| Loop cause | Trace signal | Deterministic fix |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **`LoopAgent` with no exit path** | The same child agent spans repeat in the same order until something external stops the run; `LoopAgent` never decides to stop by itself | Set `max_iterations` on every `LoopAgent` and give the checker an exit tool that sets `tool_context.actions.escalate = True` (a custom agent can instead yield an event with `EventActions(escalate=True)`) |
| **Graph back-edge with no terminal branch** | Two graph nodes alternate in the trace and the run ends only on a timeout or budget | Keep an iteration counter in state and have the router node emit a terminal route (for example `DONE`) once the counter reaches its cap; point `DEFAULT_ROUTE`, which fires when no other route on that node matches, at a terminal or fallback node rather than at the back-edge |
| **Tool error retried forever** | `execute_tool` spans with `error.type` set, each followed by an LLM call that reissues the same tool with the same arguments | `ReflectAndRetryToolPlugin(max_retries=...)` caps retries per tool (default 3, tracked per invocation) and returns structured guidance to the model; for errors that cannot self-heal (`401`, `403`, `404`), a `before_tool_callback` that counts calls per tool-and-arguments key returns a dict once the limit is hit, which skips the tool and hands the model a "do not retry" result |
| **A2A ping-pong delegation** | Nested spans alternate between two remote agents inside one distributed trace; Topology shows edges in both directions | Keep delegation acyclic (a specialist never delegates back to its caller), carry a hop or depth counter in the delegated task and refuse past a fixed depth, and give each task a deadline and token budget |
| **Over-strict critic** | Every run uses the full `max_iterations` even on drafts a reviewer would accept; the escalate event never appears | Calibrate the critic rubric against golden examples labeled acceptable, and when the cap is hit return the best draft flagged as partial or hand off to a human instead of failing silently |

* **Minimal exit wiring:** give the critic an exit tool that sets `tool_context.actions.escalate = True` when the draft passes, and always construct the loop with a hard cap, for example `LoopAgent(name="refine", sub_agents=[critic, refiner], max_iterations=5)`, so the loop stops even if escalation never fires.

* **Agent Anomaly Detection (Preview, allowlisted):** an Agent Platform service that analyzes ADK OpenTelemetry traces and logs out of band, so it adds no latency to the agent. Its agentic cascading failures category (OWASP ASI08) covers infinite execution loops and oscillating retries, and a separate resource exhaustion category covers runaway token or compute use. Findings appear in Security Command Center and detection metrics in Cloud Monitoring. It requires ADK for Python 2.1.0 or later on Agent Runtime, Cloud Run or GKE, with tracing on and prompt and response content captured.
* **Detection is not prevention:** anomaly findings arrive after the loop has already spent tokens, so the caps and terminal routes in the table stay mandatory.
* **Anti-pattern (raising the cap):** bumping `max_iterations` or `max_llm_calls` so the agent "has room to finish" leaves the missing exit signal in place and makes each runaway cost more.
* **Anti-pattern (default route as back-edge):** mapping `DEFAULT_ROUTE` to the loop's back-edge means any unexpected route value, including a typo, re-enters the cycle.

### SLIs, SLOs & Two Distinct Forms of Production Drift

Production AI systems track **four SLI dimensions**: **Responsiveness** (`p95 TTFT`, `p95` turn latency), **Pipeline Reliability** (`429`/`5xx` rate, tool `is_error` rate, fallback rate, unexpected `max_tokens`/`refusal` stop reasons), **Economic Efficiency** (cache hit ratio $>75\%$, cost per resolved task, `p95` turns/session), and **Semantic Quality** (sampled **Online Evaluation Monitor** pass rates $\ge 96\%$ and human escalation rate).

Even with zero code deploys, quality degrades over time through two distinct drift mechanisms with opposite fixes:

| Drift Type | Root Cause | Symptoms in Telemetry | Engineering Remediation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **1. Input / Data Drift** *(World Changes)* | Real user queries, new product SKUs, updated regulations, or changed third-party API payloads diverge from your static golden set and RAG corpus. | Model ID and prompt hash are unchanged and infra SLIs are green, yet **retrieval similarity scores drop**, out-of-domain queries rise, and Online Monitor faithfulness declines gradually. | **1.** Monitor query embedding distribution shift & retrieval score histograms.<br>**2.** Refresh the RAG / Agent Search corpus.<br>**3.** Feed SDP-scrubbed failing traces into the **LM Feedback Flywheel** to expand the golden evalset. |
| **2. Model / Provider Drift** *(System Changes)* | Calling a moving model alias (e.g., `-latest`), an unannounced provider routing update, or an unvalidated prompt/tool-schema edit. | Sudden step-change shift in output length, `refusal` rate, JSON parse errors, or tool-calling aggressiveness across all topics simultaneously. | **1.** **Pin exact immutable model snapshot IDs** and Agent Registry versions.<br>**2.** Run automated Level 2/3 eval gates before any model cutover (using **Data-Driven Prompt Optimizer** when migrating model families).<br>**3.** Maintain instant config rollback to the prior pinned ID. |

### 5-Target Alerting Policy Matrix & Multi-Window SLO Burn-Rate Alerts

Configure operational alerts across five high-signal agent boundaries while guarding against time-series cardinality blowups and judge-token billing spikes:

| Alert Target | Telemetry Source & Aggregation | Example Condition (Directional) | Critical Guardrail / Anti-Pattern |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **1. Tool Call Error Rate** | OTel `execute_tool` spans (`error.type`) or log-based counter grouped by `gen_ai.tool.name` | `> 5%` error ratio over a rolling 5-minute window per `gen_ai.tool.name` | **Never** attach high-cardinality `session_id` or `user_id` labels to the Cloud Monitoring metric descriptor. |
| **2. `p95` Tool & Turn Latency** | `run.googleapis.com/request_latencies`, `model_invocation_latencies`, or tool duration histograms with **`ALIGN_PERCENTILE_95`** | `ALIGN_PERCENTILE_95` exceeds latency SLO (e.g., `8 s` interactive chat) for 10 minutes | **Never alert on arithmetic mean latency**, which masks heavy-tail reasoning and retry stalls behind fast cache hits. |
| **3. Runaway Loop Depth** | Child span count per `trace_id` (`steps_per_turn > max_iterations - 1`) + **Agent Anomaly Detection (`Preview`, OWASP ASI08)** in SCC | Spike in turns hitting `max_iterations - 1` or any ASI08 cascading-failure finding | Out-of-band anomaly detection fires *after* tokens burn; always pair with an in-band hard `max_iterations` / `max_llm_calls` cap. |
| **4. Token Spend per Session** | Cumulative `input_tokens + output_tokens + thinking_tokens` per `gen_ai.conversation.id` via **Log Analytics / BigQuery sink** | `p99` tokens/session exceeds `2×` trailing 7-day baseline (counting subagent fan-out) | Compute per-session `p99` in Log Analytics or BigQuery, never as a per-session Cloud Monitoring time series. |
| **5. Online Monitor Quality Drop** | `aiplatform.googleapis.com/online_evaluator/scores` filtered by `metric.labels.evaluation_metric_name` | Rolling 30-min mean score `< 0.85` (or `< 0.80` default template) on `HALLUCINATION` / `TOOL_USE_QUALITY` | Apply **cost-control trace sampling filters** (`duration > 5s` or **`5%` random sample** + max samples/run); **never sample 100%** of high-QPS traffic (5–31 judge calls/trace, e.g., 31 calls on `SAFETY` `safety_v3`!). |

*(Also watch sustained `429` quota failures in the Models view and `>50%` jumps in the Tools view "no-tool interaction" rate.)*

**Multi-Window SLO Error-Budget Burn-Rate Alerts:** Static 5-minute threshold alerts either page on-call engineers for harmless 30-second upstream blips or fail to fire during a slow `0.3%` error leak that silently exhausts a 30-day `99.9%` SLO. Pair a **1-hour `10×` fast-burn alert** (pages immediately on acute outages) with a **24-hour `2×` slow-burn alert** (creates a ticket on gradual error-budget leaks) using Cloud Monitoring's native SLO selector:

```text
select_slo_burn_rate("projects/<proj>/services/<svc>/serviceLevelObjectives/<slo>", "3600s") > 10.0
select_slo_burn_rate("projects/<proj>/services/<svc>/serviceLevelObjectives/<slo>", "86400s") > 2.0
```

> [!NOTE]
> *Directional thresholds:* numeric cutoffs (`5%`, `8 s`, `0.85`, `10.0`, `2.0`) are SRE baselines, not fixed platform limits. Calibrate thresholds against your service's error budget and two to four weeks of production traces.

### Online monitors and quality alerts: catching drift

Offline evals prove a release was good on the day it shipped. **Online Monitors** keep scoring production traffic afterwards, and **quality alerts** turn a falling score into a page, so both drift types from the table above surface without a manual spot check.

1. **Instrument for evaluation:** enable Cloud Trace export and content capture as events (`OTEL_SEMCONV_STABILITY_OPT_IN=gen_ai_latest_experimental`, `OTEL_INSTRUMENTATION_GENAI_CAPTURE_MESSAGE_CONTENT=EVENT_ONLY`) so each trace carries `gen_ai.agent.name`, `gen_ai.conversation.id` and the inference messages.
2. **Create a monitor:** on the Online monitors tab of the Evaluation page, pick the agent, evaluate all traces or a filtered slice (for example by duration or token usage), choose metrics such as safety, task success, tool use quality or hallucination, then set a sampling percentage and a maximum samples per run to cap judge cost.
3. **Scheduled scoring loop:** roughly every 10 minutes the monitor queries sampled traces from Cloud Trace and Cloud Logging, scores them with the Agent Platform evaluation service, writes results to Cloud Logging and exports numeric scores to Cloud Monitoring.
4. **Alert on the scores:** from the monitor's menu, choose **Create alerting policy** to get one template per configured metric, or use **Recommended Alerts** on the agent's Evaluation dashboard (an aggregate low-score template plus per-metric templates such as task success and tool use quality). Route incidents to Slack, email or Pub/Sub; each incident carries the monitor's labels so responders land on the traces that caused it.
5. **Triage the drop:** compare score trends across agent versions on the Evaluation dashboard, open the Evaluation tab of low-scoring traces for rubric verdicts and rationales, then run **Automatic Loss Analysis** to classify rubric failures into loss patterns and semantic clusters.
6. **Classify and fix:** a step change aligned with a deploy or model switch points to model or prompt drift (roll back, then fix through the flywheel). A gradual decline with no deploy points to input drift (refresh the corpus, expand the golden set). Either way, the clustered failures feed the closed loop in `#feedback-flywheel`.

- **Access control:** online evaluation runs under the project-level service agent (P4SA), and anyone allowed to create an `OnlineEvaluator` can attach it to any agent in the project. Restrict that permission to authorized administrators.
- **Silent monitor:** when a monitor is active but shows no results, confirm live traces contain `gen_ai.*` attributes, re-check filters with Initial Inspection, and search Logs Explorer for `resource.labels.online_evaluator` error entries.

---

## 06. LM Feedback Flywheel, Failure Clustering & Agent Optimizer
Drift detection tells you *that* quality moved; the **LM Feedback Flywheel** and **Agent Optimizer** ensure every production failure class is discovered automatically, grouped by root cause, fixed programmatically without "prompt whack-a-mole," and permanently guarded against in CI/CD.

```
Live Traffic + Cloud Trace (gen_ai.* spans)
  ├─► Explicit & Implicit UX Signals (thumbs-down, re-query, HITL)
  └─► Online Evaluation Monitors (1%–5% async reference-free rubrics)
               │
               ▼
  [ Cloud Logging / BigQuery Sink + SDP PII De-Identification ]
               │
               ▼
  [ Failure Cluster Analysis (Automatic Loss Analysis) ]
    • Groups low-scoring traces into ranked root-cause clusters
        ┌──────┴───────────────────────────────┐
        ▼                                      ▼
[ Evalset Expansion ]             [ Programmatic Optimization ]
 • Replay tool fixtures            • Zero-Shot Optimizer (no data)
 • Keep held-out split             • Data-Driven / Agent Optimizer
 • Gate PRs (`agents-cli eval`)      (`instruction` | `demo` | `both`)
```

### Step-by-Step Closed-Loop Feedback Flywheel

1. **Capture Multi-Source Signals:** Collect explicit user feedback (thumbs-down, bug reports), implicit behavioral friction (immediate re-prompting, session abandonment, human escalation), and automated **Online Evaluation Monitors (`OnlineEvaluator`)** that continuously sample 1–5% of live Cloud Trace spans and score them asynchronously with reference-free autoraters (`HALLUCINATION`, `TOOL_USE_QUALITY`, `GENERAL_QUALITY`).
   - *IAM Governance Rule:* Online monitors execute under a platform service agent that reads trace payloads and spends judge tokens—restrict monitor creation/modification IAM permissions to authorized AgentOps engineers.
2. **Scrub Before Storage:** Export flagged `trace_id` records to BigQuery via Cloud Logging sinks after passing payloads through **Sensitive Data Protection (SDP)** de-identification templates (`ReplaceWithInfoTypeConfig` or `CryptoDeterministicConfig` surrogates) so promoted `evalset` cases and **Example Store** few-shot pairs never leak customer PII or credentials into Git repos or prompts.
3. **Triage via Failure Cluster Analysis (Automatic Loss Analysis):** Instead of playing whack-a-mole on isolated support tickets, invoke **`client.evals.generate_loss_clusters()`** (or `agents-cli eval analyze`) over low-scoring online traces and failed simulation runs. An analyzer LLM clusters raw failures into actionable root-cause buckets (e.g., *"Cluster #1 (34% of failures): `book_flight` receives relative dates like 'next Friday' instead of ISO-8601"*, *"Cluster #2 (19%): premature final answer before reading page 2 of search results"*) ranked by $\text{Frequency} \times \text{Severity}$.
4. **Reproduce & Codify Outcomes (Not Brittle Transcripts):** Convert representative traces from top clusters into reproducible `evalset` cases (`user_content`, `session_input`, `intermediate_data.tool_uses` / `reference_trajectory`) and **Example Store** exemplars. Assert **outcomes and required safety milestones** (`trajectory_in_order_match`) rather than exact word-for-word transcripts so valid alternative reasoning paths still pass.
5. **Protect Generalization with a Held-Out Split & Watch Saturation:** Keep a **held-out validation slice** (`train` vs. `validation`) invisible to both engineers and automated prompt optimizers (`adk optimize` / `optimize-agent`) during tuning to prevent prompt memorization/overfitting, and continuously refresh suites that saturate near 100%.

### Programmatic Prompt Optimization (`Agent Optimizer` / Prompt Optimizer)

Manually rewriting a 4,000-token system prompt to fix Failure Cluster #1—or migrating prompts from an older model to **`gemini-3.8-flash`**, **`gemini-4-argon`**, or a smaller **`Gemma 4`** deployment—often introduces regressions on previously working behaviors. Agent Platform provides two automated optimization engines:

| Optimizer Engine | Inputs Required | Optimization Modes & Mechanism | When to Choose |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Zero-Shot Optimizer**<br>(`client.prompt_optimizer.optimize_prompt`) | **Only the raw prompt / system instruction** (zero labeled examples or eval dataset required). | `optimization_mode="zero_shot"`: Analyzes prompt structure against model best practices and immediately returns `suggested_prompt` plus `applicable_guidelines` (e.g., adding missing role boundaries, fixing ambiguous constraints, removing redundant instructions). | Cold-start prototyping, cleaning up ad-hoc developer prompts in seconds, or preparing an initial baseline before collecting golden data. |
| **Data-Driven Optimizer & `Agent Optimizer`**<br>(`adk optimize` / `agents-cli eval optimize` / GEPA job) | System instructions + prompt template + **labeled/scored `train` dataset** (plus held-out `validation` split) + **Gen AI Evaluation metrics** + **target model ID**. | Runs an iterative closed-loop `optimize-agent` job (`evaluate → analyze failure clusters → mutate prompt/demos → re-evaluate on target model`) across three selectable modes:<br>• **`instruction`**: Rewrites system instructions only.<br>• **`demonstration`**: Selects optimal few-shot examples from candidates (or populates **Example Store**).<br>• **`instruction_and_demo`**: Jointly optimizes instructions and few-shot demonstrations. | **1.** Fixing ranked **Failure Clusters** without regressing existing evals.<br>**2.** **Model migrations** (adapting prompts to `gemini-4-argon` or distilling a frontier prompt down to `gemini-3.5-flash-lite` / `Gemma 4` for cost/latency savings). |

## 07. Deployment Runtime Selection: Agent Runtime vs. Cloud Run vs. GKE
Selecting the wrong compute runtime in Google Cloud creates immediate architectural friction—either starving a stateful agent of memory, breaking MCP server hosting, or saddling a small team with unnecessary Kubernetes node management. Apply **Rule 0 (Managed by Default)**: start at the most managed runtime that satisfies your language, protocol, accelerator, and isolation constraints.

### Google Cloud Agentic Runtime Decision Matrix

| Architectural Dimension | **Agent Runtime** *(formerly Agent Engine)* | **Cloud Run** *(Services & Jobs)* | **Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE)** | **Managed Agents API** *(Preview)* |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Primary Workload Fit** | Stateful Python/ADK, LangGraph, CrewAI, or A2A orchestrators (`reasoningEngines`) needing turnkey agent ops | **Custom Streamable HTTP MCP servers** (`--functional-type=mcp-server`), polyglot agents (TS, Java, Go, Python), webhook/Pub/Sub event-driven agents | **Self-hosted open-weight models (`Gemma 4`, `Llama`) on GPUs/TPUs**, dense multi-agent meshes, strict kernel-isolated multi-tenant sandboxes | Declarative autonomous coding, research, and file-processing agents (`Agents API` + `Interactions API`) |
| **Operational Overhead** | **Lowest** (fully managed agent container lifecycle) | **Low** (serverless container-to-URL, scales to zero) | **Highest** (cluster, node pools, networking, controller upgrades) | **Zero** (Google runs the loop and no-egress Linux container) |
| **State & Memory Model** | **Built-in:** Native **Agent Platform Sessions**, **Memory Bank**, **Example Store**, and **Code Execution** sandbox | **Stateless / Ephemeral RAM:** Local memory vanishes on scale-in; must attach external **Sessions** (`agentengine://`), **Memorystore**, **Firestore**, or **Cloud SQL** | StatefulSets, **Agent Substrate** (`<1s` auto-snapshot/restore of memory & files on GKE Standard), or external managed DBs | Server-side state chained via `previous_interaction_id` and `environment_id` (`global` endpoint) |
| **Scaling & Duration** | Managed autoscaling up to **`1,000` instances** (**`100` in VPC-SC**); `min_instances` for zero cold start; up to **`6,000` revisions** (`traffic-split` bypassed if Agent Gateway routes); multi-day async workflows | Scales `0 → 1,000` rapidly; HTTP timeout up to **60 minutes**; Cloud Run Jobs up to **24h** for batch backfills | Granular HPA/VPA, custom queue metrics, GPU time-slicing, Spot VMs, **Committed Use Discounts (CUDs)** | Synchronous streaming or `background=True` multi-hour async execution |
| **Hosts Custom MCP Servers?** | **No** (consumes MCP/A2A, does not host standalone MCP servers) | **Yes — Primary serverless choice** for Streamable HTTP `/mcp` servers | **Yes** — High-density, stateful, or private in-cluster MCP fleets | **No** (supports server-side tools only) |
| **Custom GPUs / Self-Hosted Models?** | **No** (calls managed model APIs or private GKE/Model Garden endpoints over PSC) | **Limited** (serverless L4 / RTX PRO 6000 GPUs for lightweight bursts) | **Yes — Primary choice** for vLLM/TGI serving of **Gemma 4** on GPUs/TPUs *(never proprietary Gemini weights!)* | **No** |
| **Code Sandbox Isolation** | Managed **Code Execution** micro-container (`<1s` startup, 100 MB I/O, up to 14-day TTL) & **Computer Use** (`Preview`) | Call external Agent Platform Code Execution sandbox API | **Agent Sandbox on GKE** (`SandboxTemplate` + `SandboxWarmPool` pre-warmed **gVisor** pods; blocks `hostNetwork`/`hostPath`) | Built-in isolated Linux container (outbound network disabled by default) |

### Runtime dimensions in detail

The matrix above names the best fit. The table below compares the three general-purpose runtimes on the dimensions that usually decide an architecture review.

| Dimension | **Agent Runtime** | **Cloud Run** | **GKE** |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Managed agent primitives** | Sessions, Memory Bank, Code Execution sandbox and Agent Identity available to the deployed agent; bidirectional streaming (`Gemini Live API`) supported | None built in; call Agent Platform Sessions or Memory Bank through the SDK, or bring Firestore, Memorystore, Spanner or Cloud SQL | None built in; wire state yourself or use Agent Sandbox and Agent Substrate |
| **Scale-to-zero** | `min_instances` defaults to 1, so one warm instance stays up | Scales to zero when idle unless you set minimum instances | Pods scale with HPA and nodes with the cluster autoscaler; the cluster itself stays provisioned |
| **Cold start and concurrency** | Raise `min_instances` to absorb baseline load; `container_concurrency` defaults to 9 (one per agent process), and async ADK agents should start at a multiple of 9 such as 36 (too high risks OOM); `max_instances` caps at `1,000` (`100` in VPC-SC) | Default 80 concurrent requests per instance for console deploys (80 × vCPU with gcloud or Terraform), configurable up to 1,000; minimum instances and startup CPU boost cut cold starts | Warm pods have no cold start; new pods pay image pull and readiness time, which you tune |
| **Accelerators** | None exposed; calls hosted models | NVIDIA L4 (24 GB) and NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (96 GB) GPUs, with scale to zero; L4 needs at least 4 CPU and 16 GiB memory | Full GPU and Cloud TPU node pools for self-hosted models |
| **Runtime contract** | Custom containers listen on `0.0.0.0:8080`; `/api/reasoning_engine` (unary `query`) and `/api/stream_reasoning_engine` (`streamQuery`) are optional but required for SDK use, and the streaming one for the console playground; `AdkApp` is the reference implementation | Any container that serves on `$PORT` (HTTP, gRPC, WebSockets) | Standard Kubernetes Pod spec: sidecars, DaemonSets, StatefulSets |
| **Sandboxing untrusted code** | Managed Code Execution sandbox | Per-instance sandboxed execution environment; call the managed Code Execution sandbox for model-written code | GKE Sandbox (gVisor) and Agent Sandbox with warm pools |
| **Networking** | Private Service Connect interface (`networkAttachment`, `/28` min subnet) + `AgentConnectivityTemplate` (`vpcEgress: ALL_TRAFFIC`, DNS `restricted.googleapis.com` `199.36.153.4/30` under VPC-SC) | Direct VPC egress, internal ingress, VPC Service Controls, IAP | Native VPC subnets, private clusters, `NetworkPolicy`, service mesh |
| **Identity** | Agent Identity (GA) per agent, or a service account | Per-service service account or Agent Identity; IAP for callers | Workload Identity Federation for GKE maps Kubernetes service accounts to IAM principals |
| **Ops burden** | Lowest: packaging, revisions and telemetry hooks managed | Low: no nodes, you own the container | Highest: cluster upgrades, node pools, networking, controllers |
| **Billing shape** | Compute and memory of running instances, including the warm baseline; see Agent Platform pricing | Request-based or instance-based billing; GPUs billed per GPU second | Cluster fee plus nodes (Standard) or requested Pod resources (Autopilot) |

> [!NOTE]
> *Directional cold-start figures:* the Agent Runtime scaling guide shows one benchmark (300 concurrent requests, default `min_instances=1`) averaging about 4.7 seconds on a cold run versus about 0.4 seconds warm, and roughly 1.4 seconds once `min_instances=10`. Cloud Run documents about 5 seconds to start a GPU instance with drivers preinstalled. Treat these as examples and load test your own agent.

#### Choose this runtime when

* **Stateful ADK orchestrator that needs sessions, memory and per-agent identity with little glue code:** choose Agent Runtime.
* **Real-time voice or video agent that streams in both directions:** Agent Runtime bidirectional streaming fits, but it is Preview; confirm the launch stage is acceptable or host a WebSocket service on Cloud Run.
* **Custom Streamable HTTP MCP server or webhook tool that idles most of the day:** choose Cloud Run for scale to zero and IAP in front of the endpoint.
* **Polyglot agent or web front end packaged as a standard container:** choose Cloud Run.
* **Bursty small open model inference without running a cluster:** choose Cloud Run with an L4 or RTX PRO 6000 GPU.
* **Large self-hosted open-weight models on multi-GPU or TPU nodes inside a private VPC:** choose GKE.
* **Model-written or user-supplied code that must run with kernel isolation next to your workloads:** choose GKE with GKE Sandbox or Agent Sandbox; for short stateless snippets, the managed Code Execution sandbox is enough.
* **Workload that needs sidecars, DaemonSets or StatefulSet caches in one namespace:** choose GKE.

- **Anti-pattern:** picking GKE for a single stateless agent "for flexibility". You inherit cluster upgrades and on-call load with no capability you need.
- **Anti-pattern:** raising `container_concurrency` on Agent Runtime for a synchronous agent. The default of 9 assumes blocking code; only async agents benefit, and memory limits still apply.

### GKE Sub-Architecture Choice: Agent Substrate vs. Agent Sandbox

When requirements mandate GKE, distinguish its two specialized agent orchestration architectures:
- **Agent Substrate on GKE (Actor-Based, GKE Standard):** Best for high-density stateful agents that frequently go idle between user turns. Active agents multiplex over a shared pool of warm Pods; idle agents automatically checkpoint memory and filesystem state to storage and restore in **`< 1 second`**, maximizing node utilization.
- **Agent Sandbox on GKE (Pod-Based, GKE Autopilot or Standard):** Best when each agent or untrusted code execution requires a dedicated Kubernetes Pod (`Sandbox` / `SandboxClaim` CRDs, `SandboxWarmPool` for sub-second startup), full `PodSpec` sidecars, hardware accelerators (GPUs/TPUs), and mandatory **gVisor** kernel isolation enforced via Validating Admission Policy.

### Runtime Capacity, Quota & Configuration Traps

* ***"Region temporarily at capacity"* vs. `429 RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED`:**
   - Seeing **`"Region temporarily at capacity"`** when deploying an Agent Runtime instance means **physical regional compute pool exhaustion**, *not* an IAM error or project quota cap—filing a quota increase ticket will not resolve it. Deploy to an alternate supported region, right-size vCPU/memory, or retry off-peak.
   - Seeing **`429 RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED`** during Gemini API inference indicates shared Standard PayGo contention or TPM/RPM limits. Route stateless requests to the **`global` endpoint**, apply full-jitter backoff, enable **Priority PayGo** for bursty interactive paths, or purchase **Provisioned Throughput (GSUs)** for predictable baseline load. *(Remember: Provisioned Throughput does **not** cover Batch Prediction or internal calls made by other managed services like Agent Search, even when using the same model.)*
* **Reserved Environment Variables on Agent Runtime:** Never override `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT` or `PORT`, and never define custom variables starting with the reserved `GOOGLE_CLOUD_AGENT_ENGINE*` prefix (except documented platform toggles like `GOOGLE_CLOUD_AGENT_ENGINE_ENABLE_TELEMETRY=true`).
* **Agent Registry Auto-Registration Rules:** Agents on **Agent Runtime**, **Gemini Enterprise**, official Google MCP servers, annotated **GKE** workloads, and **Cloud Run** services deployed with `--functional-type=agent` + `--identity-type=agent-identity` auto-register in **Agent Registry**; unflagged Cloud Run services and external/on-prem MCP servers must be registered via the writable `Service` resource.

---

## 08. Production Resilience Stack & Fault Isolation
LLM APIs and external tools operate under tight token-per-minute (TPM) and request-per-minute (RPM) quotas, variable compute load, and occasional regional brownouts. Production resilience requires a **4-layer defense stack** where each control lives at a distinct architectural boundary.

```
Incoming User / Workflow Request
       ▼
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ LAYER 1: Call-Site Retry (Exponential Backoff + Full Jitter)           │
│ • 429/5xx/529 only; honor Retry-After; mutating tools need idempotency │
└──────┬─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
       │ Retries exhausted or upstream error rate spikes
       ▼
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ LAYER 2: Service-Boundary Circuit Breaker (Closed ─► Open ─► Half-Open)│
│ • Trips across worker pool; fails fast (<1 ms) to prevent starvation   │
└──────┬─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
       │ Circuit OPEN
       ▼
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ LAYER 3: Orchestration Fallbacks (Region/global ─► Cross-tier ─► Cache)│
└──────┬─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
       │ Fallbacks exhausted or policy/confidence trigger
       ▼
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ LAYER 4: Graceful Degradation & Structured Human Escalation            │
│ • Persist state, trace_id & attempted tools; route to operator queue   │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### Layer 1: Exponential Backoff with Full Jitter & Idempotency

When an upstream model endpoint returns `429 Too Many Requests` or `529 Overloaded`, naive fixed-interval retries synchronize across all concurrent workers—creating a **retry storm (thundering herd)** that guarantees the next wave fails too.

1. **Honor `Retry-After` first:** If the response includes a `retry-after` or `retry-after-ms` header, sleep for at least that server-specified duration.
2. **Use Exponential Backoff with Full Jitter** when no header is present:
   $$t_{\text{sleep}} = \text{Uniform}\!\left(0,\; \min\left(T_{\text{cap}},\; T_{\text{base}} \cdot 2^{\text{attempt}}\right)\right)$$
   Randomizing the wait across $[0, \text{cap}]$ desynchronizes concurrent callers.
3. **Single Retry Owner:** Official SDKs (`google-genai`, `anthropic`) retry transient errors (`408`, `409`, `429`, `>=500`) **twice by default**. Never wrap an SDK call that has default retries enabled inside your own 4-attempt loop (multiplying to $3 \times 4 = 12$ hits per request). Either configure `HttpRetryOptions` / `max_retries` on the SDK client or set `max_retries=0` and manage retries in one wrapper.
4. **Never retry terminal errors or content decisions:** Fail fast on `400` (bad schema, invalid `thinking_level`), `401`/`403` (auth), `404` (bad model ID), `413` (payload too large), **workspace spend-cap `429`s** (which lack `retry-after`), and `HTTP 200` with `stop_reason: "refusal"` / safety block.
5. **Idempotency Keys on Mutating Tools:** Retrying a mutating tool (`charge_credit_card`, `issue_refund`, `create_jira_ticket`) after a `504 Gateway Timeout` risks duplicate execution if the first request committed server-side. Every mutating tool must pass a deterministic **`idempotency_key`** (`sha256(session_id + turn_index + tool_name + canonical_args)`) deduplicated in Memorystore/Redis or the downstream API.

### Layers 2–4: Circuit Breakers, Validated Fallbacks & Context-Rich Escalation

- **Layer 2 — Circuit Breakers (`Closed → Open → Half-Open`):** Per-request retries during a 10-minute outage hold thousands of sockets open, starving web workers. A shared service-boundary circuit breaker trips **`Open`** once error rates breach threshold (failing fast in `<1 ms` into Layer 3), then probes recovery via **`Half-Open`** after a cooldown window.
- **Layer 3 — Orchestration Fallbacks:** Fail over first to the same model via the **`global` endpoint** or a secondary region; if falling back across model tiers/families (e.g., `gemini-4-argon` → `gemini-3.8-flash` or `Claude Opus` → `Sonnet`), maintain a **fallback-specific prompt/parameter configuration** (adjusted via **Data-Driven Prompt Optimizer** and validated on your Level 2/3 golden suite) so unsupported parameters (like `thinking_budget` vs. `thinking_level`) do not cause secondary `400` crashes.
- **Layer 4 — Structured Human Escalation:** When fallbacks exhaust or `max_turns` / policy boundaries trigger, hand off a structured bundle (`trace_id`, session history, verified customer entities, tools already invoked + outputs, and escalation reason) so the human specialist never asks the customer to repeat themselves.

---

## 09. Safe Rollouts: Shadow Mode vs. 4-Element A/B Testing
Passing an offline golden dataset and simulation suite (Levels 1–3) is necessary but never sufficient for high-volume production changes. Real user traffic contains live concurrency, cache warmth, and long-tail phrasing that static suites miss. Promote changes through a **4-Stage Progressive Delivery Pipeline**:

```
[1. Offline & Sim] ─► [2. Shadow Mode (Dark Launch)] ─► [3. Canary 1%–5%]
 (Golden + 2-Step)     (Async fork; mock writes!)        (Sticky + SLO gate)
                                                               │
                                                               ▼
                       [4. Controlled A/B Test] (Sticky split + fixed N)
```

### Shadow Mode (Dark Launch) vs. Canary vs. A/B Testing

| Rollout Stage | Who Sees Candidate Output? | Side-Effecting Tools Allowed? | What It Validates Best | Blind Spots / Limitations |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Offline & Simulation** | Eval harness only | Mocked / **Environment Simulation** | Regressions on known golden cases, multi-turn persona stress tests, fault-injection handling | Cannot test real production concurrency, live cache hit ratios, or organic user reactions. |
| **Shadow Mode** *(Dark Launch)* | **Nobody** (logged async; user receives baseline response) | **Read-only tools only** (mutating tools MUST be stubbed/sandboxed!) | Real-world `p95`/`p99` latency, crash rates, token spend, cache hit rate, first-turn tool selection, and async autorater parity | **Cannot measure multi-turn user reaction** (user replies to baseline Turn 1, creating counterfactual divergence on Turn 2+) or business conversion. |
| **Canary Release** | **1%–5% of live traffic** (sticky by session) | Live tools (with circuit breakers & auto-rollback) | Production stability, quota saturation, and catastrophic UX failures under real closed-loop dialogue | Small slice lacks statistical power to prove subtle (2%–3%) resolution or conversion gains. |
| **Controlled A/B Test** | **Randomized split** (e.g., 50/50 or 80/20 sticky by user/account) | Full live stack | Causal impact on primary business/quality outcomes + non-inferiority against cost and latency guardrails | Requires pre-committed sample size $N$ and business-cycle duration; exposes treatment cohort to candidate. |

> [!WARNING]
> **Critical Shadow Mode Safety Rule:** In shadow mode, live requests are duplicated asynchronously to the candidate agent. If the candidate calls **mutating tools** (`refund_order`, `update_crm`, `send_email`), running unsandboxed shadow mode executes real side effects twice or corrupts production data! Enforce a **read-only tool sandbox** in shadow mode.

### Rigorous Controlled Experimentation & A/B Testing

An A/B experiment must lock in **all four elements before launch**:
1. **Explicit Falsifiable Hypothesis & Sticky Randomization Unit:** Randomize at the **user, account, or session level** (`hash(user_id + experiment_salt) % 100`), **never per HTTP turn** (which mixes models mid-conversation, destroys prefix caching, and ruins causal attribution).
2. **Single-Variable Isolation:** Change **one variable per treatment arm** (e.g., prompt revision OR model tier, not prompt + model + retriever + UI simultaneously).
3. **Primary Outcome Metric + Guardrail Metrics (Non-Inferiority Bounds):** Pair one primary success metric (e.g., *Verified Resolution Rate without Escalation*) with strict guardrails that must not degrade: `p95` TTFT/turn latency, **token cost per resolved task**, unhelpful refusal rate, tool error rate, and `HALLUCINATION` monitor score.
4. **Pre-Committed Sample Size $N$ & Statistical Stopping Rule:** Fix $\alpha = 0.05$, power $1 - \beta = 0.80$, MDE, and minimum full weekly cycle beforehand. **Never stop early the first day $p < 0.05$ ("peeking" / p-hacking)** unless using formal sequential testing boundaries (Always-Valid p-values / O'Brien-Fleming alpha-spending).

---

## 10. Token Economics, Heavy-Tail Sizing & 4-Step Enterprise ROI
More enterprise AI pilots fail at the FinOps gate than at the accuracy gate. A prototype that costs \$0.02 per query on clean developer tests can easily cost \$0.85 per resolved ticket in production once heavy-tail context growth, ~15× multi-agent fan-out, online judge sampling, and human review labor are included.

### Heavy-Tail Token Distributions (`p95`/`p99` vs. `p50`)

LLM token consumption follows a **heavily right-skewed (log-normal / Pareto) distribution**:
- **Why `p50` (median) sizing fails:** While the median session might be 2 turns consuming 3,000 tokens (\$0.01), the top 5%–10% (`p95`–`p99`) involve 15-turn debugging loops, 50-page PDFs, large MCP JSON payloads, `thinking_level="HIGH"` reasoning traces, and retries—consuming 150,000 to 500,000+ tokens per session.
- Without context compaction and prefix caching, resending history across $N$ turns bills **quadratically** ($O(N^2)$):
  $$\text{Cumulative Input Tokens across } N \text{ turns} \approx N \cdot S_{\text{static}} + \sum_{t=1}^{N} (N - t + 1) \cdot \Delta_{\text{turn } t}$$
- **FinOps Sizing Rule:** Model TPM quotas and monthly budgets using the **distribution mean or `p95`/`p99`-weighted buckets**, never `p50 × volume`, and enforce hard caps (`max_turns`, `max_tokens`, observation pruning) to clip runaway tails.

### High-Impact Cost-Bending Levers (Multi-Agent ~15× Multiplier)

Autonomous multi-agent systems consume **~15× more tokens** than single-turn chat (~4× more than single-agent tool loops) due to parallel subagent context initialization, multi-hop reasoning, and coordinator synthesis. Bend the cost curve with six architectural levers:

| Cost-Optimization Lever | Mechanism | Typical Savings Impact | Critical Exam & Production Nuance |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **1. Tiered Semantic Model Routing** | Route simple classification/guardrails to **`gemini-3.5-flash-lite`** (`Haiku`), workhorse tool loops to **`gemini-3.8-flash`** (`Sonnet`), and complex synthesis to **`gemini-4-argon`** (`Opus`). | **50% – 80%** token spend reduction | Validate each routed tier against your Level 2/3 golden set (and tune prompts with **Data-Driven Optimizer**). |
| **2. Prefix-Aligned Context Caching** | **Implicit caching** (automatic on `gemini-4-argon` at $\ge 4,096$ tokens and `3.x` at $\ge 4,096$ to $6,144$ tokens, **zero storage fee**, ~90–95% read discount) vs. **Explicit caching** (`cachedContents` / `cache_control` with TTL storage/write cost where supported). | **Up to 80% – 95%** on repeated input prefixes + lower TTFT | Cache creation bills at standard input price on Gemini; **explicit `cachedContents` pays TTL storage fees while implicit caching has zero storage cost** (`gemini-4-argon` supports implicit only). Keep static instructions/tools at byte 0! |
| **3. Thinking / Effort Right-Sizing** | Use `thinking_level="minimal"` on `3.5-flash-lite` or `"low"`/`"medium"` on `3.8-flash` & `4-argon` (and `effort: "low"` on Claude) for routine hops, since thinking tokens bill at **output token rates**. | **30% – 60%** output token reduction | Reserve `thinking_level="high"` for ambiguous planning, root-cause analysis, or complex math/code synthesis. |
| **4. Async Batch / Flex Inference** | Run nightly 10,000-case offline evalsets, bulk backfills, and large autorater jobs via **Batch Prediction / Flex PayGo / Message Batches API** ($\le 24\text{h}$ SLA). | **~50% price reduction** on input & output tokens | **Provisioned Throughput (GSUs) does NOT cover batch prediction**—use Batch/Flex for offline workloads and GSUs for steady real-time traffic. |
| **5. Observation Masking & Session Compaction** | Prune verbose MCP JSON/HTML fields after extraction (`after_tool_callback`), run tabular filtering inside the **Code Execution sandbox**, and compact older session turns. | **40% – 70%** reduction in multi-turn $O(N^2)$ growth | Store critical IDs/constraints in structured `session.state` before compacting prose to prevent **state erasure**. |
| **6. Idle Infra Hygiene** | Tune `min_instances`, suspend idle Cloud Workstations (`idleAction=SUSPEND`), and undeploy unused **Vector Search 1.0** index endpoints. | Eliminates 24/7 fixed hourly burn at zero QPS | Deployed Vector Search 1.0 endpoints bill continuously per node-hour even when serving zero queries. |

### Unit Economics & Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) Ledger

Calculate **Net Monthly Benefit** across all four steps—ignoring **Step 4 (Human-Review & Exception Tax)** is the #1 cause of negative-ROI production launches:

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ STEP 1: Baseline Human Task Cost                                        │
│   Baseline_Cost = Monthly_Volume × Hours_Per_Task × Loaded_Labor_Rate   │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ STEP 2: Gross Labor Value Captured                                      │
│   Gross_Savings = Baseline_Cost × Automation_Rate × Time_Saved_Fraction │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ STEP 3: Total AI Operating Cost (Tail-Adjusted)                         │
│   AI_OpEx = LLM_Tokens (p95-weighted + retries + Online Monitor sample) │
│           + Runtime/Retrieval Hosting + Amortized Eng Maintenance       │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ STEP 4: Mandatory Human-Review & Exception Tax (The Hidden Killer)      │
│   Review_Tax = (Flagged_Rate × Volume × Audit_Hours × Reviewer_Rate)    │
│              + (Error_Rate × Volume × Rework_Hours × Specialist_Rate)   │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ NET MONTHLY BENEFIT = Gross_Savings − AI_OpEx − Review_Tax              │
│ NET ROI (%)         = (Net_Monthly_Benefit / Total_Investment) × 100    │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

- **Worked Sanity Check:** On $50,000\text{ claims/month}$ at $\$12/\text{claim}$ baseline ($\$600\text{k}$), 80% automation yields **$\$480\text{k}$ Gross Savings** (Step 2) against **$\$30\text{k}$ AI OpEx** (Step 3). If compliance requires a 6-minute ($\$6$) audit on all $40,000$ automated claims ($\$240\text{k}$) plus 20-minute ($\$30$) specialist rework on $2,500$ subtle errors ($\$75\text{k}$), **Step 4 Review Tax = $\$315\text{k}$**, cutting Net Benefit from $\$450\text{k}$ down to **$\$135\text{k}/\text{month}$**. If audit time approaches baseline manual time (e.g., 14 min vs. 12 min), Net ROI turns **negative**—fixable only by raising `pass^k` precision, adding $0 Tier 1 deterministic gates, and calibrating confidence routing so humans audit only genuinely uncertain slices.

### Architectural Readiness & Launch-Gate Triage

| Launch-Gate Verdict | Engineering & Economic Criteria | Canonical Scenario | Architectural Action |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **1. Production-Ready (Go)** | Accuracy, `p95` latency, unit economics, and governance bounds all fit current models and data. | Internal IT helpdesk agent grounded on Agent Search with 4s streaming TTFT and ticket fallback. | Proceed to Level 1–3 eval harness + staged canary rollout. |
| **2. Conditional Go (Guardrails Required)** | Core task works, but synchronous latency or unreviewed autonomy conflicts with latency budgets or risk posture. | 50-page contract redlining requested in `< 1s` with 100% autonomous legal sign-off. | Re-architect around **async background execution** (`background=True`, 30–60s) + **mandatory human approval gate (HITL)**. |
| **3. No-Go (Use Deterministic Automation)** | Requires 100.00% zero-defect determinism without review, `< 5 ms` control loops, or $10\times$ negative unit economics. | High-frequency `< 5 ms` trading execution or unreviewed autonomous clinical dosing from raw handwriting. | **Keep LLMs off the critical path**; use deterministic rules/classical ML, or limit AI strictly to assistive drafting with HITL. |

## 11. Production Failure Modes & Diagnostic Matrix

### Production Failure Mode Diagnostic Matrix

| Observed Production Symptom | Root Cause | Correct Engineering Remediation | Trap / Wrong Fix to Avoid |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Compliance agent scores 97% on `FINAL_RESPONSE_QUALITY` yet issues refunds without checking eligibility** | **"Right answer, wrong path"** blind spot in outcome-only grading | Pair outcome autoraters with **`trajectory_in_order_match` / `trajectory_exact_match`** (`trajectory_single_tool_use`) and a forbidden-tool `CustomMetric` | Raising the `FINAL_RESPONSE_QUALITY` threshold from 0.90 to 0.99 |
| **Online Evaluation Monitor rejects `trajectory_exact_match` or causes a 6×–31× judge LLM billing spike on live traffic** | Live traffic has **no ground-truth reference trajectory**, and 100% sampling triggers **5–31 judge calls/trace** (`TOOL_USE_QUALITY` ~5× Flash + 1× Pro; `SAFETY` `safety_v3` **31× Flash**) | Score **reference-free rubrics** (`HALLUCINATION`, `TOOL_USE_QUALITY`, `FINAL_RESPONSE_QUALITY`) with **trace sampling filters** (`5%` sample or `duration > 5s`) + max samples/run | Trying to attach `trajectory_exact_match` online or enabling 100% online rubric evaluation on high-QPS traffic |
| **Cloud Monitoring hits custom metric cardinality limits and spikes observability spend after tracking per-session tokens** | Unbounded **`session_id` (`gen_ai.conversation.id`) or `user_id`** attached as a Cloud Monitoring metric label | Strip high-cardinality IDs from Monitoring labels (group only by bounded `gen_ai.tool.name`, `model`, `status`); compute `p99` tokens/session in **Log Analytics / BigQuery log sink** | Hashing `session_id` into another unbounded Cloud Monitoring label |
| **On-call engineers get paged on 30-second `503` blips while a slow `0.3%` error leak silently burns the monthly 99.9% SLO** | Alerting on single-window static error counts or arithmetic mean latency | Use **multi-window SLO burn-rate alerts** (`select_slo_burn_rate(..., "3600s") > 10.0` fast burn + `"86400s" > 2.0` slow burn) and **`ALIGN_PERCENTILE_95`** latency aligners | Lowering a single 5-minute static error-rate threshold until alert fatigue worsens |
| **Team has zero historical chat logs and cannot test multi-turn edge cases or `503` tool outages safely** | Relying solely on static single-turn prompts or live prod backends | Run **2-Step Agent Simulation** (from an **Agent Registry** snapshot) + **Environment Simulation** fault injection | Running load/fault tests directly against live production payment APIs |
| **Manual prompt edits to fix one bug cluster keep breaking three unrelated instructions** | Manual "prompt whack-a-mole" without closed-loop optimization | Cluster traces via **Failure Cluster Analysis**, expand the golden set (with a **held-out split**), and run **Data-Driven Prompt Optimizer / Agent Optimizer** | Appending contradictory ALL-CAPS warnings to the bottom of the system prompt |
| **Deploying a custom Streamable HTTP MCP server onto Agent Runtime fails** | **Agent Runtime** hosts stateful agent orchestrators (`reasoningEngines`), not standalone MCP servers | Host custom Streamable HTTP MCP servers on **Cloud Run** (or **GKE**) and register them in **Agent Registry** | Embedding external MCP server daemons inside `session.state` |
| **Users lose conversation context randomly on a TypeScript/Python agent hosted on Cloud Run** | Storing session history in **ephemeral Cloud Run container RAM** across scale-to-zero recycles | Externalize state to **Agent Platform Sessions** (`agentengine://`), **Memorystore for Redis**, **Firestore**, or **Cloud SQL** | Increasing Cloud Run request timeout to 60 minutes without external state |
| **Architect proposes self-hosting `gemini-4-argon` on GKE GPUs for VPC isolation** | **Proprietary Gemini weights cannot be self-hosted** on customer clusters | Call managed Gemini endpoints inside **VPC Service Controls** (+ Provisioned Throughput if needed), or self-host open-weight **Gemma 4** on GKE | Creating a GKE GPU node pool to pull `gemini-4-argon` container weights |
| **Agent Runtime deployment fails with `"Region temporarily at capacity"`** | **Physical regional compute pool exhaustion** (not a project quota limit) | Deploy to an alternate supported region, reduce per-instance vCPU/RAM, or retry off-peak | Filing an IAM or project quota-increase support ticket and waiting |
| **Every component passes isolated Level 2 evals at >95%, but end-to-end tasks fail 45% of the time** | **Integration seam failure** (schema mismatch, oversized tool payloads, or state loss during compaction) | Add **Level 3 Trajectory & Seam Integration Tests**, strict JSON schemas, and structured `session.state` preservation | Tuning isolated Level 2 prompts further in single-step harnesses |
| **Shadow mode rollout accidentally sends duplicate cancellation emails to real customers** | Shadow pipeline executed **live mutating tools** instead of a read-only sandbox | Intercept/mock all state-mutating tools in shadow mode; allow only read-only retrieval | Running unsandboxed shadow mode on a smaller 5% traffic slice |
| **AI saves 80% of drafting time, yet total department labor cost rises by 12%** | **Step 4 Human-Review & Exception Tax** exceeds Step 2 Gross Savings | Add $0 Tier 1 code validators and calibrate confidence routing so humans audit only uncertain/high-risk slices | Ignoring human audit time in the FinOps ROI spreadsheet |
