## 07. Risks, Limitations & Best Practices (`#section-7`)

### Risks & Anti-Patterns

- **Cargo Cult Coding:** Accepting AI output without understanding it — code passes a happy-path demo, but nobody on the team can debug or extend it.
- **Hidden Technical Debt:** AI generates duplicated, "good enough" imperative glue that silently erodes modularity.
- **Security Blind Spots:** Unchecked AI code frequently introduces SQL injection, SSRF, XSS, insecure deserialization, or hardcoded credentials.
- **Hallucinated APIs & Slopsquatting:** AI invents non-existent SDK methods or imports hallucinated package names that attackers register on PyPI/npm (**slopsquatting**).
- **Context Window Overflow & Rot:** Dumping massive repositories into one chat degrades attention and causes contradictory edits across files.
- **Skill Atrophy:** Uncritical reliance on Full Autopilot erodes engineers' mental models of system failure modes.

### Core Best Practices

- **Always Review:** Read every line of AI-generated diffs before merging — treat AI output as an untrusted draft PR.
- **Test First:** Generate or write executable unit/integration tests alongside specifications before accepting implementation code.
- **Constrain Context:** Scope prompts with explicit architectural boundaries, pinned SDK versions, and file paths.
- **Version Everything:** Commit small, atomic checkpoints so bad agent trajectories can be reverted cleanly.
- **Automated Security Verification:** Run SAST, dependency validation, and PoC-verified remediation (**CodeMender**) on all generated code.
- **Document Intent:** Commit the specification or ADR capturing *why* the design was chosen, not just the resulting code.

> **The "It Works" Trap:** The most dangerous outcome of vibe coding is code that **appears to work perfectly** in a local demo while hiding race conditions, multi-currency rounding bugs, or exploitable injection flaws. Always ask: *"Does it work, or does it only seem to work?"*

### Production Readiness Checklist

- ✅ Every line of AI-generated code has been read and understood by a human reviewer
- ✅ Unit and integration tests cover critical paths and edge cases
- ✅ Security scan (SAST + secret detection) passes with zero injection vectors or hardcoded credentials
- ✅ Dependencies verified — all imported packages and API methods exist at approved, vulnerability-free versions
- ✅ Architecture documented so engineers can maintain and debug the service independently
- ✅ Performance load-tested under expected `p95`/`p99` concurrency (AI optimizes for plausibility, not tail latency)
- ✅ Licensing & IP provenance verified against copyleft policy

---

## 08. Secure Coding Sandboxes: Antigravity, Cloud Workstations & GKE (`#section-8`)

Giving an autonomous coding agent—or a 5-agent swarm—unrestricted shell access on a developer laptop holding production `gcloud` tokens, SSH keys, and `.env` secrets creates catastrophic blast radius: a single prompt injection inside a README or MCP response can exfiltrate credentials, wipe host directories, or corrupt shared Git state. Enterprise agentic development (PAA Section 2.1 / CCAR-F Domain 3) enforces **defense-in-depth sandboxing** across local CLI/IDE terminals, cloud dev environments, and runtime code execution clusters.

```
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ LAYER 1: Agent Process & Worktree Sandbox (Antigravity --sandbox / Claude Seatbelt)    │
│  • Blocks .env reads & arbitrary egress; Workspace="branch" / git worktree per worker  │
├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ LAYER 2: Managed Cloud Dev Environment (Google Cloud Workstations + VPC-SC)            │
│  • No public IP · Private PSC cluster · Zero local source code · idleAction=SUSPEND    │
├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ LAYER 3: Runtime Untrusted Code Execution (Agent Sandbox on GKE / Code Execution)      │
│  • gVisor user-space kernel · SandboxWarmPool (<1s) · Blocks hostNetwork & hostPath    │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### Enterprise Sandbox Comparison Matrix

| Sandbox Surface | Primary Use Case | Isolation Boundary & Network Controls | Key Operational / Exam Rules |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Antigravity Terminal Sandbox & Branch Workspaces** | Interactive IDE / CLI (`agy`) vibe coding & parallel subagent swarms | OS-level process sandbox (`--sandbox` / `enableTerminalSandbox`); blocks `.env` secret reads and outbound network by default (`read_url` domain allowlist); **`Deny > Ask > Allow`** rule precedence. | **Off by default in App UI presets** (even `"Full machine"`—must toggle `Enable Terminal Sandbox` explicitly); **auto-enabled in CLI `auto` mode**. Spawn parallel swarm workers with **`Workspace="branch"`** (isolated Git worktrees) to prevent `.git/index.lock` collisions. |
| **Claude Code Sandboxed Bash + Vertex AI** | Terminal/IDE agentic coding (`claude`) with enterprise cloud governance | macOS Seatbelt / Linux `bubblewrap` filesystem write cage (cwd only) + proxy-enforced domain allowlist; parallel swarms use `claude --worktree` (`-w`). | Set **`CLAUDE_CODE_USE_VERTEX=1`** inside Cloud Workstations to authenticate via Google Cloud IAM (zero static Anthropic API keys), keeping prompts inside regional **VPC-SC** perimeters and **Cloud Audit Logs**. |
| **Google Cloud Workstations** | Standardized, zero-trust enterprise developer & coding-agent cloud IDEs | Dedicated Compute Engine VM inside customer VPC with **zero public IP** (`constraints/compute.vmExternalIpAccess`), **Private Cluster** via **Private Service Connect (PSC)**, and **VPC Service Controls** perimeter blocking data exfiltration. | Configure **`idleAction=SUSPEND`** (not `STOP`/delete) + **keep-alive scripts (`/google/scripts/keep_alive.sh`)** detecting active agent PIDs so long-running agent builds aren't killed mid-task while idle workstations pause vCPU/RAM billing with RAM state preserved! |
| **Agent Sandbox on GKE** *(Pod-Based)* | Executing untrusted AI-generated code, dynamic tool scripts, or isolated multi-tenant coding agents at scale | Dedicated Kubernetes Pod per sandbox (`Sandbox` / `SandboxClaim` / `SandboxTemplate`) isolated by **gVisor (`runsc`)** user-space kernel; **Validating Admission Policy** blocks `hostNetwork`, `hostPID`, and `hostPath`. | Attach a **`SandboxWarmPool`** CRD to pre-warm gVisor pods for **`< 1 second`** claim latency on GKE Autopilot or Standard; supports custom `PodSpec` sidecars and GPUs/TPUs. |
| **Agent Substrate on GKE** *(Actor-Based)* vs. **Managed Code Execution** | High-density stateful agents (*Substrate*) vs. zero-ops Python calculation sandboxes (*Code Execution*) | **Agent Substrate** multiplexes stateful agents on shared warm GKE Standard pods with `<1s` memory/filesystem snapshot-restore; **Agent Platform Code Execution** runs zero-egress micro-containers (`<1s` start, 100 MB I/O, up to 14-day TTL). | Do **not** use actor-based Agent Substrate when untrusted multi-tenant code requires strict per-tenant kernel/Pod isolation—use **Agent Sandbox on GKE** with **gVisor** instead. |

### Critical Enterprise Sandbox Architecture Patterns

1. **Preventing Swarm Git Corruption (`Workspace="branch"` / `git worktree`):** When 4 swarm agents edit files and run `pytest` concurrently inside the *same* working tree, they overwrite each other's uncommitted edits and crash on `.git/index.lock`. Always isolate each worker in its own **Git worktree** (`Workspace="branch"` in Antigravity `invoke_subagent`, or `claude -w <name>` in Claude Code), which shares the underlying `.git` object store without duplicating disk space.
2. **Zero-Exfiltration Contractor & Regulated Coding (`Cloud Workstations + VPC-SC`):** For regulated finance/healthcare teams or external contractors, prohibit source checkouts on unmanaged laptops. Provision **Cloud Workstations** with private gateway ingress, disable browser clipboard/SSH file transfer via IAM & Chrome Enterprise Premium policies, route LLM calls (`Gemini Code Assist`, `Antigravity`, or `Claude Code on Vertex AI`) over **Private Google Access** inside a **VPC-SC** perimeter, and bind workstation service accounts with least-privilege IAM.
3. **Preserving Long-Running Agent Sessions Without 24/7 VM Burn:** Standard Cloud Workstation idle timeouts (`runningTimeout`, default 2 hours) terminate unattended VMs, killing background `/goal` or test-suite runs if no browser keystrokes occur. Combine a custom `/google/scripts/keep_alive.sh` hook (which returns busy while an `agy`/`claude`/build process is active) with **`idleAction=SUSPEND`** so truly idle workstations hibernate to persistent disk (halting compute charges) and resume with open terminals and memory intact.

---

## 09. Autonomous Vulnerability Remediation: CodeMender & Google AI Threat Defense (`#section-9`)

AI-assisted coding increases code output by 5×–10×, creating an acute security bottleneck: traditional SAST scanners bury AppSec engineers under thousands of **unverified false-positive alerts**, while naive "ask an LLM to patch this CVE" scripts hallucinate superficial fixes that break builds or leave the underlying flaw intact. **Google AI Threat Defense** and **CodeMender** (PAA Section 2.2) close this gap with **exploit-verified autonomous remediation**.

### Google AI Threat Defense: The 4-Stage Security Lifecycle

**Google AI Threat Defense** organizes agentic and software security across four continuous stages:

```
┌──────────────────┐    ┌──────────────────────────┐    ┌──────────────────────────┐    ┌──────────────────┐
│  1. PREPARE      │───►│ 2. SCAN & PRIORITIZE     │───►│  3. REMEDIATE            │───►│  4. MONITOR      │
│ • SAIF guardrails│    │ • SAST / Artifact scan   │    │ • CodeMender autonomous  │    │ • Cloud Audit    │
│ • Hardened base  │    │ • Wiz Security Graph     │    │   Find → Verify → Fix    │    │   (is_agentic)   │
│   images & SBOMs │    │   cloud exposure ranking │    │ • Sandbox PoC exploit +  │    │ • Model Armor &  │
│ • Sandbox policy │    │ • SCC attack path score  │    │   human-reviewed PR      │    │   SCC runtime    │
└──────────────────┘    └──────────────────────────┘    └──────────────────────────┘    └──────────────────┘
```

1. **Prepare:** Establish Secure AI Framework (SAIF) policies, locked dependency registries, hardened container base images, VPC-SC perimeters, and sandbox templates before code is deployed.
2. **Scan and Prioritize:** Combine static/artifact scanning with **Security Command Center (SCC)** and the **Wiz Security Graph** to correlate code vulnerabilities against *real cloud runtime exposure* (internet ingress, over-privileged IAM service accounts, reachable sensitive data stores)—prioritizing exploitable attack paths over theoretical findings in dead code.
3. **Remediate:** Dispatch **CodeMender** to autonomously validate exploitability via sandboxed Proof-of-Concept (PoC) execution and synthesize root-cause, regression-tested patches for human PR approval.
4. **Monitor:** Continuously inspect live traffic and agent actions using **Model Armor** (prompt injection / PII / malicious URLs), **Dual-Attribution Cloud Audit Logs (`is_agentic=true`)**, and SCC runtime threat detection.

### Inside CodeMender: Hybrid Architecture & The `Find → Verify → Fix` Loop

**CodeMender** (Public Preview, built by Google DeepMind) uses a **hybrid client-service architecture**:
- **Hosted Multi-Agent Reasoning Service:** Google-hosted Gemini reasoning agents (configurable via `--model` override) that hypothesize root causes, design exploits, synthesize patches, and run independent **LLM-as-judge** patch critiques.
- **Local CLI / Daemon Client (`cm`):** Runs directly inside the developer's workstation, CI runner, or private build container where the codebase and compiler toolchain live, equipped with a **process sandbox enabled by default** and explicit file scoping (`scan.extensions.include` in `config.yaml`; supports **C/C++, C#/.NET, Go, Java, JS/TS, Kotlin, Python, Ruby, Rust, and PHP**).

| CodeMender Step | CLI Command | What Happens Under the Hood | Why Traditional Tools Fail Here |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **1. Find** *(or Import)* | `cm find` **or** `cm report import --file ./findings.json` | Scans scoped source files for memory-safety, injection, auth-bypass, and logic flaws—**OR imports external SAST / Wiz Security Graph JSON reports** via `cm report import --file ./findings.json`. | Exam trap: CodeMender is **NOT limited to vulnerabilities it found itself**—it natively ingests third-party scanner findings to verify and patch them! |
| **2. Verify** *(PoC Exploit)* | `cm verify <FINDING_ID>` | Synthesizes, compiles, and executes a **concrete Proof-of-Concept (PoC) exploit / fuzzing harness inside an isolated sandbox (on by default)** to trigger the vulnerability deterministically. | SAST tools flag syntactic patterns with 40%–70% false-positive rates; `cm verify` proves real-world exploitability before bothering engineers. |
| **3. Fix** *(Root-Cause Patch)* | `cm fix <FINDING_ID> -y` | Traces dataflow/AST root causes, generates an idiomatic multi-file fix, **re-runs the PoC exploit** (asserting it now fails to exploit), runs the full **unit/regression suite**, passes an **LLM-as-judge** style & equivalence critique, and stages a **human-reviewed PR**. | Naive one-shot LLM patches add brittle input blacklists or break callers; CodeMender refuses to propose a patch unless the PoC is neutralized and tests pass. |

```bash
# End-to-end CodeMender workflow in CI / Cloud Workstations
# 1. Import prioritized findings from external SAST / Wiz JSON report (or run `cm find`)
cm report import --file ./findings.json

# 2. Compile & execute sandboxed Proof-of-Concept (PoC) exploits to filter false positives (sandbox on by default)
cm verify FINDING_042

# 3. Synthesize root-cause patches, re-verify PoC neutralization + test suite, and stage PR
cm fix FINDING_042 -y --model gemini-4-argon
```

### Architectural Guardrails for Autonomous Remediation

- **Mandatory Sandbox Execution for `cm verify` & `cm fix`:** Because `cm verify` compiles and executes live exploit payloads (buffer overflows, command injections, deserialization gadgets), always run verification inside CodeMender's **process sandbox** inside an isolated CI container, **Cloud Workstation**, or **Agent Sandbox on GKE (`gVisor`)**—never against live production databases or shared host credentials.
- **Human-in-the-Loop Merge Gate:** CodeMender automates root-cause localization, exploit verification, and patch validation, reducing mean-time-to-remediate (MTTR) from weeks to minutes—but **human maintainers retain final PR merge authority** on production branches, inspecting the attached root-cause explanation and regression PoC test.

---

## 10. Key Takeaways & Self-Assessment (`#section-10`)

### Key Takeaways

- **Vibe Coding** is conversational AI-assisted development (`1 human : 1 agent`), coined by Andrej Karpathy in 2025, operating across a spectrum from **Full Autopilot** (throwaway prototypes) to **Human-Led + AI Assist** (production code).
- **Swarm Prototyping** orchestrates multiple specialized agents in parallel (`Fan-Out/Fan-In`, `Tournament`, `Pipeline`, `Specialization Grid`, `Ensemble`) to explore competing architectures rapidly; isolate workers in **Git worktrees (`Workspace="branch"` / `claude -w`)** to prevent `.git/index` collisions.
- The biggest danger of unverified AI code is the **"It Works" trap** (code that demos cleanly while hiding logic bugs, hallucinated APIs, or injection vulnerabilities). Always review, test, load-test, and scan AI-generated code.
- **Enterprise Sandboxing** layers **Antigravity Terminal Sandbox** (`--sandbox`, off by default in App presets; blocks `.env` & arbitrary egress; `Deny > Ask > Allow`), **Cloud Workstations** (private PSC cluster, zero public IP, VPC-SC, `idleAction=SUSPEND` + `/google/scripts/keep_alive.sh`), and **Agent Sandbox on GKE** (`gVisor` + `SandboxWarmPool` `<1s` startup).
- **CodeMender** operates in Stage 3 (**Remediate**) of **Google AI Threat Defense** (`Prepare → Scan & Prioritize → Remediate → Monitor`), executing **`cm find` / `cm report import` → `cm verify` (sandboxed PoC exploit eliminating false positives) → `cm fix` (PoC-neutralized, regression-tested, LLM-judge-critiqued PR for human review)**.
- Across both vibe coding and autonomous remediation, **the human shifts from typist to architect, reviewer, and final quality gate**.

### Self-Assessment Questions

- **Q1.** Who coined the term "Vibe Coding" and in what year, and what are the three modes on the Vibe Coding spectrum?
  - *Answer:* Coined by **Andrej Karpathy** in early **2025**. The three modes are **Full Autopilot** (throwaway prototypes/hackathons, very high risk), **Collaborative Mode** (features/internal tools/MVPs, moderate risk), and **Human-Led + AI Assist** (production/security-critical/regulated systems, low risk).
- **Q2.** When running a 4-agent Tournament or Specialization Grid swarm locally in Antigravity or Claude Code, why do uncommitted edits and `.git/index.lock` errors occur, and what configuration prevents them?
  - *Answer:* Sharing a single working directory causes concurrent agents to overwrite files and contend on `.git/index.lock`. Isolate every subagent in its own **Git worktree** (`Workspace="branch"` in Antigravity `invoke_subagent` or `claude --worktree` / `-w` in Claude Code), and enable the terminal sandbox (`--sandbox` / `enableTerminalSandbox`, which is off by default in Antigravity App UI presets).
- **Q3.** A bank provisions Cloud Workstations for engineers running long-horizon coding agents. How do they block code exfiltration while preventing idle timeouts from killing active 3-hour agent builds *without* paying 24/7 VM costs when developers go home?
  - *Answer:* Deploy **private Cloud Workstations** (zero public IP, Private Service Connect control plane) inside a **VPC Service Controls (VPC-SC)** perimeter using IAM-authenticated **Gemini Code Assist / Antigravity / Claude Code on Vertex AI (`CLAUDE_CODE_USE_VERTEX=1`)**. Pair `/google/scripts/keep_alive.sh` (detecting active agent PIDs during builds) with **`idleAction=SUSPEND`** so genuinely idle VMs hibernate to disk (halting vCPU/RAM charges) while preserving RAM/terminal state on resume.
- **Q4.** When executing untrusted AI-generated Python/Bash packages on GKE at scale with sub-second startup, why should you choose **Agent Sandbox on GKE** over **Agent Substrate on GKE**?
  - *Answer:* **Agent Substrate** multiplexes trusted stateful actors across shared warm pods on GKE Standard. Untrusted code execution requires strict per-workload kernel isolation via **Agent Sandbox on GKE**, which provisions dedicated **gVisor (`runsc`)** pods (`SandboxTemplate`), blocks `hostNetwork`/`hostPath` via Validating Admission Policy, and achieves `<1s` claim latency using **`SandboxWarmPool`**.
- **Q5.** Security engineers complain that SAST scanners flood their backlog with 65% false positives. How does **CodeMender** integrate with external SAST / Wiz reports inside **Google AI Threat Defense** to solve this?
  - *Answer:* Within Stage 3 (**Remediate**) of AI Threat Defense (`Prepare → Scan & Prioritize → Remediate → Monitor`), engineers ingest external SAST/Wiz SARIF findings via **`cm report import`** (or discover new ones via `cm find`), run **`cm verify`** inside an isolated sandbox to compile and execute a real **Proof-of-Concept (PoC) exploit** (filtering out non-exploitable false positives), and run **`cm fix`** to generate a root-cause patch verified against the PoC, unit tests, and an LLM-as-judge critic before opening a human-reviewed PR.

# Instruction-Driven Development (IDD & SDD): Enterprise Skills, Customizations & Spec-to-Eval Study Guide (v3.0)

> **Author:** Michaël Bettan · **Version:** 3.0 (April 2026 — PAA Section 2: Agentic Software Engineering & CCAR-F Domain 3)

A structured methodology for AI-assisted software engineering — also known as **Specification-Driven Development (SDD)**. Move beyond ad-hoc prompting to a disciplined, reproducible workflow where **instructions, modular `SKILL.md` packages, deterministic hooks, and `agents-cli` evaluation gates** form an executable engineering contract.

---

## 01. The Problem with Ad-Hoc Prompting {#s1}

Most developers using AI coding assistants start in an **ad-hoc, reactive mode**: they open a chat, type a prompt like *"build me a login page,"* accept the output, and move to the next thing. This works for simple tasks but breaks down for anything complex, team-based, or production-grade.

The result? **Inconsistent outputs**, lost context between sessions, no reproducibility, and code that works in isolation but fails when integrated. IDD solves this by treating AI interaction as a *structured engineering process*, not a casual conversation.

### Inconsistency

The same prompt produces different results across sessions, models, or team members. No deterministic outputs.

### Context Loss

AI forgets previous decisions. Each session starts from zero. Architectural coherence degrades over time.

### No Collaboration

Prompts live in one developer's head. No shared understanding, no review process, no handoff protocol.

> **The Ad-Hoc Spiral:** Without structure, each AI interaction accumulates subtle inconsistencies. By the time you notice, your codebase is a patchwork of individually-correct but collectively-incoherent components. This is the **"death by a thousand prompts"** anti-pattern.

---

## 02. What is IDD / SDD? {#s2}

**Instruction-Driven Development (IDD)** — also called **Specification-Driven Development (SDD)** — is a methodology where you write detailed, structured instructions *before* engaging the AI. These instructions serve as the contract between human intent and AI execution.

Think of it as **TDD (Test-Driven Development) but for prompts**: instead of writing tests first then code, you write specifications first then let AI generate the implementation. The spec is the single source of truth — versioned, reviewed, and shared across the team.

### Core Philosophy of IDD

- **Spec First, Code Second:** Write the instruction document before touching the AI — clarify what you want before asking for it
- **Instructions as Artifacts:** Specs are version-controlled, peer-reviewed, and reusable — they're as important as the code itself
- **Deterministic Intent:** The same instruction should produce functionally equivalent results regardless of when, where, or by whom it's executed
- **Separation of Concerns:** Human handles *what* and *why*; AI handles *how*
- **Iterative Refinement:** Specs evolve through feedback loops — each iteration makes instructions more precise and AI output more reliable

> **IDD vs SDD — Same Thing, Different Names:** The community uses both terms interchangeably. **IDD (Instruction-Driven Development)** emphasizes the instructional nature of prompts. **SDD (Specification-Driven Development)** emphasizes the formal specification. In practice, they describe the identical workflow.

---

## 03. The IDD Workflow (Step-by-Step) {#s3}

IDD follows a disciplined, six-phase workflow (`Define → Review → Execute → Validate → Refine → Archive`). Each phase has clear inputs, outputs, and quality gates.

### Detailed Phase Breakdown

1. **Define the Instruction:** Write a structured document containing: project context, functional requirements, non-functional requirements (performance, security), technical constraints (language, framework, patterns), file structure expectations, test requirements, and acceptance criteria.
2. **Review & Validate the Spec:** Have a teammate or second AI review the instruction for ambiguity, missing edge cases, contradictions, and completeness (e.g., via Antigravity `/plan` Artifact review or `/grill-me` design interviews). Fix before executing.
3. **Execute with AI:** Feed the instruction to your AI assistant as primary context alongside relevant existing files. Ask the AI to confirm its plan before generating code.
4. **Validate Output Against Spec:** Check every acceptance criterion. Run generated unit/integration tests and eval sets (`agents-cli eval run`). Verify file structure matches spec and scan for security issues.
5. **Refine the Instruction:** Based on what the AI got right and wrong, update the spec to remove ambiguity and add explicit constraints where the model drifted.
6. **Archive & Reuse:** Commit the instruction alongside the code in the same branch/PR. Promote repeatable workflows into modular `SKILL.md` packages or template libraries.

> **The Golden Rule of IDD:** If your instruction is ambiguous, the AI's output will be unpredictable. The quality of your specification directly determines the quality of the generated code. **Invest time in the spec, save time in debugging.**

---

## 04. Instruction Documents (Spec Anatomy) {#s4}

The instruction document is the heart of IDD — a **structured specification** with six canonical sections:

```markdown
# Instruction: [Feature Name]
## Version: 1.0 | Date: 2026-04-15 | Author: [Name]

## 1. Context
Project: [Project name and brief description]
Current State: [What exists, what's the starting point]
Goal: [What this instruction should produce]

## 2. Functional Requirements
- FR-01: User can register with email and password
- FR-02: System sends verification email on registration
- FR-03: User can login and receive a JWT token

## 3. Non-Functional Requirements
- NFR-01: Response time < 200ms for auth endpoints
- NFR-02: Passwords hashed with bcrypt (cost factor 12)
- NFR-03: Rate limiting: 5 login attempts per minute per IP

## 4. Technical Constraints
- Language: Python 3.12
- Framework: FastAPI
- Database: PostgreSQL via SQLAlchemy
- Auth: JWT with PyJWT
- Testing: pytest with >80% coverage

## 5. File Structure
src/
  auth/
    router.py     # API endpoints
    service.py    # Business logic
    models.py     # SQLAlchemy models
    schemas.py    # Pydantic schemas
  tests/
    test_auth.py  # Unit + integration tests

## 6. Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] All FR items implemented and tested
- [ ] All NFR constraints verified
- [ ] No security vulnerabilities (no hardcoded secrets)
- [ ] Code passes ruff linting with zero warnings
- [ ] README updated with setup instructions
```

- **Context Block:** Gives the AI project awareness — what exists, what's the goal, and what constraints are inherited from previous decisions.
- **Functional Requirements:** Numbered, independently testable statements of what the system must do.
- **Non-Functional Requirements:** Latency, security, scalability, and quality guardrails that prevent shortcuts.
- **Technical Constraints:** Locked-in language versions, frameworks, databases, and testing libraries.
- **File Structure:** Explicit directory and file layout preventing ad-hoc file sprawl.
- **Acceptance Criteria:** Verifiable pass/fail conditions for "done."

---

## 05. IDD vs Vibe Coding vs Traditional {#s5}

| Dimension | Traditional Dev | Vibe Coding | IDD / SDD |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Planning** | Requirements doc / tickets | Mental model + ad-hoc prompts | Structured instruction document + Plan Artifact |
| **Implementation** | Human writes all code | AI generates, human reviews | AI generates from spec, human + CI gates validate |
| **Reproducibility** | High (deterministic) | Low (prompt-dependent) | High (spec + evalset form the contract) |
| **Team Scalability** | High (established processes) | Low (tribal knowledge) | High (shared specs, rules & `SKILL.md` registry) |
| **Speed** | Slow (manual coding) | Very fast (but fragile) | Fast (after upfront spec investment) |
| **Quality Control** | Code review + CI | Varies (often minimal) | Spec review + deterministic hooks + eval CI |
| **Best For** | Critical systems, large teams | Prototypes, solo exploration | Production AI-assisted software engineering |

> **IDD is Vibe Coding's Adult Form:** IDD doesn't replace vibe coding — it **matures** it. Teams explore ideas rapidly with vibe coding, then formalize architecture, constraints, and acceptance tests into IDD specs for production delivery (`Vibe Coding = Prototyping → IDD = Engineering`).

---

## 06. Real-World IDD Patterns {#s6}

### Pattern 1: Layered Specs (`L0 → L3`)

- **L0 — Project Spec:** Overall architecture, tech stack, security invariants (`AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md`)
- **L1 — Module Specs:** One per domain module (`auth`, `billing`, `notifications`)
- **L2 — Feature Specs:** Individual user-facing features within a module
- **L3 — Task Specs:** Atomic coding tasks (add endpoint, migrate schema, fix bug)
- Each lower layer inherits constraints from the layer above without duplicating boilerplate.

### Pattern 2: Spec-Test-Code Loop

1. Write the instruction spec with explicit acceptance criteria and eval cases.
2. Generate tests (and `*.evalset.json` cases for agentic features) from the spec *first*.
3. Generate the implementation until all tests and evaluation rubrics pass.
4. Refine either the spec or implementation whenever edge cases surface.

### Pattern 3: Spec as PR Template

- Every pull request links or embeds the IDD spec that produced the diff.
- Reviewers verify implementation fidelity against the spec, preserving architectural *why* in version history.

### Pattern 4: Instruction Library

- Curate proven templates (`auth-api.md`, `crud-service.md`, `react-form.md`, `data-pipeline.md`) and modular `SKILL.md` bundles so new engineers ship compliant services from day one.

---

## 07. Tools, Templates & Ecosystem {#s7}

### Tools That Support IDD Workflows

- **Google Antigravity (`AGENTS.md`, `GEMINI.md`, `.agents/rules/`, `/plan`, `/grill-me`):** Agent-first IDE & CLI with executable Plan Artifacts, interactive design interviews (`/grill-me`), scoped rules, and native `SKILL.md` discovery
- **Claude Code (`CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/rules/`, Plan Mode):** Hierarchical instruction files (`@path` imports, path-scoped rules), deterministic lifecycle hooks, and `Shift+Tab` read-only Plan Mode
- **`google-agents-cli` (`agents-cli`):** Unified Google Cloud CLI (`uvx google-agents-cli`) for installing official agent skills, scaffolding ADK prototypes, running evaluation gates, deploying to Cloud Run / GKE / Agent Runtime, and publishing to Gemini Enterprise
- **Cursor Rules (`.cursorrules` / `.cursor/rules/*.mdc`):** Project-level instruction files that persist context across IDE sessions
- **Claude Projects (System Prompts):** Persistent workspace-level instructions and reference documents
- **GitHub Copilot Instructions:** Repository-level `.github/copilot-instructions.md` files constraining Copilot code generation
- **Aider Conventions:** `.aider.conf.yml` and convention files encoding repository standards
- **Windsurf Memories:** Persistent cross-session architecture context

### Spec Storage & Quality Checklist

- Store specs in `/specs` or `/docs/idd` using `IDD-{module}-{feature}-v{version}.md` plus `SPEC_INDEX.md`, versioned in the same branch and PR as the code.
- Ensure every requirement is **testable**, free of vague words (*"appropriate," "nice," "fast"*), locked to **specific versions/libraries**, **explicit in file structure**, and **complete on error/edge cases**.
- **Avoid Over-Specification:** Keep spec depth proportional to complexity — a 50-line helper needs a few bullet points, whereas multi-service or regulated features warrant full six-part specs.

---

## 08. Agent Skills (`SKILL.md`), 3-Level Progressive Disclosure & `GCPSkillRegistry` {#s8}

Dumping 40 procedural runbooks or dozens of verbose MCP tool schemas into `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md` causes **context bloat** (also called **tool bloat**): reasoning accuracy drops, latency rises, and prompt-cache costs balloon on unrelated tasks. The open **Agent Skills standard (`agentskills.io`)** solves this through **3-Level Progressive Disclosure**.

### Directory Layout & Discovery Scopes

```text
.agents/skills/deploy-cloud-run/     # Workspace skill (or ~/.config/agents/skills/, .claude/skills/)
├── SKILL.md                         # Required: YAML frontmatter + core workflow (< 5,000 tokens)
├── scripts/                         # Optional: non-interactive CLI helpers (--help, zero TTY prompts)
│   └── verify_service.py
├── references/                      # Optional: deep API/IAM tables read only when needed
│   └── vpc-sc-troubleshooting.md
└── assets/                          # Optional: starter templates & JSON schemas
    └── service.yaml.tmpl
```

### 3-Level Progressive Disclosure Architecture

| Disclosure Level | What Enters Context Window | Token Cost | Trigger Condition |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Level 1 — Discovery (Catalog)** | YAML frontmatter only (`name` optional, **`description` required**) | **~100 tokens / skill** at session startup | Loaded automatically when the session starts |
| **Level 2 — Instructions (Activation)** | Full `SKILL.md` Markdown body | **< 5,000 tokens** recommended | Loaded *only* when user intent semantically matches `description` (or explicit `/skill-name`) |
| **Level 3 — Execution & Deep Reference** | `scripts/`, `references/`, `examples/`, `resources/` | **0 tokens until read/invoked** | Read via file tools or executed as black-box CLI commands strictly on demand |

### Critical Authoring Rules for `SKILL.md`

1. **`description` Is the Sole Semantic Trigger:** At Level 1, the agent *only* sees YAML frontmatter (`name` + `description`). A vague description (*"Helps with cloud stuff"*) never triggers reliably; write keyword-rich trigger conditions (*"Deploy and troubleshoot ADK services on Cloud Run with VPC-SC; trigger when editing service.yaml or debugging 403 ingress errors"*).
2. **Keep `SKILL.md` Under 5,000 Tokens & Scripts Non-Interactive:** Move bulky API tables into `references/` and deterministic validation into `scripts/` exposing `--help` flags and structured JSON/exit codes. **Never** use interactive `input()` / TTY prompts inside skill scripts — autonomous agents run headlessly and will hang.
3. **Skill Design Categories:**
   - **Domain Reference:** Standards, schema contracts, and API specifications referenced without file mutations
   - **CLI & MCP Automation:** Non-interactive command wrappers and parameter presets for linters, build tools, and MCP servers
   - **Template Scaffolding:** Generates boilerplate components and test harnesses from project templates
   - **Quality & Policy Auditing:** Evaluates code changes, configurations, or schemas against architectural and security rubrics
   - **Multi-Phase Execution:** Coordinates multi-stage procedures (such as dependency upgrades, migration verification, or eval runs)
4. **Enterprise Governance via `GCPSkillRegistry`:** Rather than copying `.agents/skills/` across hundreds of repos manually, platform teams publish versioned skills centrally on Google Cloud using **`GCPSkillRegistry`** (`Skill`, `SkillRevision`, and `Publisher` resources), enforcing IAM access control, provenance, and pinned revision rollouts across Antigravity, Gemini CLI, and ADK agents.

---

## 09. Enterprise Customizations & `agents-cli` Spec-to-Eval Workflows {#s9}

Production IDD separates **always-on workspace invariants (Rules)**, **on-demand procedural playbooks (Skills)**, **zero-exception deterministic guardrails (Hooks)**, and **automated CI evaluation gates (`agents-cli`)**.

### Rules vs. Skills vs. Hooks Across Antigravity & Claude Code

| Mechanism | Google Antigravity | Claude Code | Enforcement & When to Use |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Always-On / Path-Scoped Rules** | `AGENTS.md` / `GEMINI.md` + `.agents/rules/*.md` with **strict snake_case `trigger:`** (`always_on`, `model_decision`, `glob`, `manual`; max ~24 KB/file, ~20k-token total budget) | `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/CLAUDE.md`, `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` (`@path` imports) + `.claude/rules/*.md` with YAML `paths:` globs | **Advisory LLM context** for repo architecture, naming, and style conventions. *(Gotcha: camelCase `alwaysOn` in Antigravity YAML is silently discarded!)* |
| **Modular Skills (`SKILL.md`)** | `.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` + `~/.config/agents/skills/` + `GCPSkillRegistry` | `.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` + `~/.claude/skills/` | **On-demand procedural workflows** (<5k tokens) loaded via 3-level progressive disclosure to avoid context bloat. |
| **Deterministic Lifecycle Hooks** | `hooks.json` lifecycle scripts | `settings.json` hooks (`PreToolUse`, `PostToolUse`, `Stop`, `UserPromptSubmit`) | **100% deterministic OS enforcement:** `PreToolUse` exit code `2` blocks forbidden commands/secret writes; `PostToolUse` runs `ruff`/`tsc`; `Stop` verifies tests pass. |
| **Interactive Spec Alignment** | `/plan` (executable Plan Artifact) & `/grill-me` (structured design interview before coding) | Plan Mode (`Shift+Tab` read-only exploration & plan approval) | **Pre-code human alignment** during IDD Phase 1–2 (`Define → Review`) to resolve ambiguities before touching files. |

### End-to-End Spec-to-Eval Automation with `agents-cli` (PAA Sec 2.1 & 4.1)

Google's **`google-agents-cli` (`agents-cli`)** bridges IDD specifications directly into scaffolded ADK code, automated evaluation gates, and managed cloud deployment:

```bash
# 1. Install official Google Cloud agent skills into Antigravity, Claude Code & Gemini CLI
uvx google-agents-cli setup

# 2. Scaffold an ADK agent from the approved IDD spec (headless: pass --prototype --yes)
agents-cli create refund-agent --prototype --yes
agents-cli install

# 3. Gate PRs in CI against golden scenarios & rubrics (evalsets configured in eval_config.json)
agents-cli eval run --config tests/eval/eval_config.json

# 4. Deploy to managed runtime (Agent Runtime, Cloud Run, or GKE) & publish to Gemini Enterprise
agents-cli deploy --deployment-target agent_runtime --no-confirm-project
agents-cli publish gemini-enterprise --agent-runtime-id <RUNTIME_ID>
```

> **Exam Gotcha — Headless Coding Agents & CI Runners (`--yes`):** Humans running `agents-cli` interactively in a terminal can answer wizard prompts, but **coding agents (Antigravity, Claude Code) and CI/CD pipelines MUST invoke `agents-cli` with `--yes` and explicit CLI flags** so non-TTY subprocesses never hang waiting on `stdin`.

---

## 10. Key Takeaways & Self-Assessment {#s10}

### Key Takeaways

- **IDD/SDD** writes structured instruction contracts *before* code generation (`Define → Review → Execute → Validate → Refine → Archive`).
- Every complete IDD spec covers **Context, Functional Requirements, Non-Functional Requirements, Technical Constraints, File Structure, and Acceptance Criteria**.
- **Agent Skills (`SKILL.md`)** eliminate context/tool bloat via **3-Level Progressive Disclosure**: Level 1 YAML `description` (~100 tokens) at startup, Level 2 `SKILL.md` (<5,000 tokens) on match, and Level 3 non-interactive `scripts/` & `references/` on demand — governed org-wide via **`GCPSkillRegistry`**.
- Separate **Rules** (advisory conventions; Antigravity `.agents/rules/*.md` requires snake_case `trigger: always_on | glob | model_decision | manual`), **Skills** (on-demand workflows), and **Hooks** (`PreToolUse` exit `2` / `PostToolUse` formatters for zero-exception deterministic enforcement).
- Use **`/plan`** and **`/grill-me`** (or Claude Code Plan Mode) to lock design decisions before code generation, then automate scaffolding, trajectory/rubric CI gating (`agents-cli eval run`), deployment, and Gemini Enterprise publishing with **`agents-cli` (`--yes` in headless mode)**.

### Self-Assessment Questions

1. **Q1.** What are the three main problems with ad-hoc AI prompting that IDD solves?
   - *Answer:* **Inconsistency**, **Context Loss**, and **No Collaboration** (avoiding the *"death by a thousand prompts"* spiral).
2. **Q2.** Name the 6 sections of a well-structured IDD instruction document.
   - *Answer:* 1) Context, 2) Functional Requirements, 3) Non-Functional Requirements, 4) Technical Constraints, 5) File Structure, and 6) Acceptance Criteria.
3. **Q3.** How does `SKILL.md` 3-Level Progressive Disclosure prevent context bloat compared to pasting runbooks into `AGENTS.md` or loading dozens of raw MCP servers?
   - *Answer:* Level 1 loads only YAML frontmatter (`name` + required `description`, ~100 tokens/skill) at session start; Level 2 loads the `<5,000`-token `SKILL.md` body *only* when the task matches `description`; Level 3 executes non-interactive `scripts/` or reads `references/` strictly on demand.
4. **Q4.** Why must security-critical guardrails (such as blocking `rm -rf` or `.env` commits) live in `PreToolUse` hooks rather than `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md` rules?
   - *Answer:* Rules are advisory prompt tokens that an LLM can misinterpret or override under context pressure, whereas a `PreToolUse` hook returning exit code `2` deterministically blocks the tool call at the OS/harness layer 100% of the time.
5. **Q5.** How does `agents-cli` operationalize an IDD spec from developer IDE setup through CI gating and enterprise release?
   - *Answer:* `uvx google-agents-cli setup` installs official skills into the IDE; `agents-cli create --prototype --yes` + `install` scaffolds the ADK agent headlessly; `agents-cli eval run` gates PRs against `*.evalset.json` + `eval_config.json`; `agents-cli deploy` ships to Agent Runtime/Cloud Run/GKE; and `agents-cli publish gemini-enterprise` registers the agent for end users.
