# Agent Platform: Build, Retrieve & Run — Study Guide

> **Author:** Michaël Bettan  
> **Version:** 2.0  
> **Updated:** October 2026

---

## 00. Overview & Mental Model

**Definition:** **Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform** is the evolution of Vertex AI for building, scaling, governing, and optimizing agents on Google Cloud. This guide covers the *build, retrieve, run, and optimize* lifecycle: choosing among the three build paths (**Agent Studio**, **Managed Agents API**, and code-first **ADK / open frameworks** with **`agent-starter-pack`** and **`agents-cli`**), hosting agents on **Agent Runtime** (formerly Agent Engine), managed **Sessions**, **Memory Bank**, **Example Store**, and the **Code Execution** sandbox, choosing between Agent Runtime, Cloud Run, and GKE, grounding and retrieval services, caching and external state, the **Agent Evaluation** suite (2-step user simulation, environment simulation, adaptive rubrics, trajectory metrics, online monitors, and golden-dataset flywheels), **Agent Observability** (Agent Registry telemetry views, dual-attribution audit logs, failure cluster analysis, and programmatic prompt optimization), and cost/quota management.

**Out of scope here:** cryptographic identity, IAM, Principal Access Boundary (PAB), VPC Service Controls, Model Armor, Sensitive Data Protection, Agent Gateway, and governance policies are covered under **Agent Platform: Identity, Security & Governance**; ADK code-level patterns, vendor-neutral RAG design, Gemini model selection, and A2A wire mechanics are covered in their dedicated topic guides.

> **Mental model (5-part anatomy mapped to Google Cloud):**  
> The **model** (Gemini 4 Argon, Gemini 3.8 Flash…) is the reasoning brain; the **orchestration layer** (ADK, LangGraph, Managed Agents harness, or Agent Studio) wires the Think → Act → Observe loop; **Agent Runtime** is the managed body that keeps long-running tasks alive; **Sessions** are short-term working memory for one conversation while **Memory Bank** is consolidated long-term memory across conversations; **MCP servers, retrieval services, and the Code Execution sandbox** are the hands and library; **Evaluation + Observability + Optimizer** form the continuous AgentOps quality flywheel.

> **Rule 0 (managed by default):**  
> Choose the most managed component that meets the requirement. Move down the stack (**Managed Agents API / Agent Studio** → **Agent Runtime** → **Cloud Run** → **GKE**) only for a concrete engineering need: custom orchestration code, non-Python stacks, hosting stateless Streamable HTTP MCP servers, GPUs/self-hosted open weights, or fine-grained kernel/network control.

> [!NOTE]
> Product names, preview status, quotas, and regions evolve continuously. Items marked **Preview** are Pre-GA and do not carry GA SLAs. Always verify launch stage, regional availability, and pricing against current Google Cloud documentation before production commitment.

---

## 01. Platform Map: Naming, Pillars & Build Paths

### The four pillars

| Pillar | What it covers | Key components |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Build** | Create agents, attach skills/tools, and connect to enterprise data | **ADK** (Python, Go, Java, TypeScript), **Agent Studio** (low-code visual builder), **Managed Agents API** + **Interactions API** (**Preview**), **Skill Registry**, **Agent Garden** (samples/templates), **Model Garden** (200+ models), **RAG Engine**, **Agent Search**, **Agent Retrieval**, **`agent-starter-pack`**, **`agents-cli`** |
| **Scale** | Run stateful, multi-step agents reliably in production | **Agent Runtime** (`reasoningEngines`), **Sessions**, **Memory Bank**, **Example Store** (**Preview**), **Code Execution** sandbox, **A2A Agent Hosting** |
| **Govern** | Control identity, discovery, egress, and security policy | **Agent Registry**, **Agent Identity** (SPIFFE), **Agent Gateway**, **Model Armor**, governance policies → see **Security guide** |
| **Optimize** | Simulate, evaluate, observe, and continuously improve quality | **Gen AI Evaluation Service** (2-step user simulation, environment simulation, adaptive rubrics, trajectory metrics, **Online Monitors**), **Agent Registry Observability**, **Failure Cluster Analysis**, **Prompt Optimization / Agent Optimizer** |

**Billing model:** Agent Platform is **pay-as-you-go** consumption (tokens, vCPU/GiB-seconds on runtimes, storage/queries on indexes) with optional **Provisioned Throughput** (GSUs) for developers; the **Gemini Enterprise app** (formerly Agentspace) is a separate per-seat subscription workspace where business users discover and invoke published agents.

### Three build paths on Agent Platform

| Build path | Target builder & control level | How the loop & state work | Best fit |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **1. Agent Studio** (low-code) | Citizen developers, domain experts, rapid prototypers | Visual canvas to configure instructions, Gemini model, grounding data stores, MCP tools, and sub-agents; test in-console and publish 1-click to **Agent Runtime** or **Gemini Enterprise Workflow Builder** | Internal knowledge assistants, departmental workflows, rapid validation before pro-code handoff |
| **2. Managed Agents API** (**Preview**) | Developers wanting a declarative, harness-managed agent via REST/SDK | Combines the **Agents API** (reusable agent definition + mounted **Skill Registry** skills) with the stateful **Interactions API** (`client.interactions.create`, server-side `previous_interaction_id`, `background=true`). Google owns the Think-Act-Observe loop, automatic restarts, artifacts, and an isolated Linux sandbox (**no network egress by default**). Powers managed endpoints like **Antigravity Agent** and **Deep Research**. | Autonomous coding, file analysis, research, and document-producing tasks where you want zero harness maintenance |
| **3. Code-first ADK & Open Frameworks** | Software & AI engineers needing deterministic control over control flow, callbacks, and CI/CD | You author orchestration code in **ADK**, **LangGraph**, **CrewAI**, **AG2**, or **LlamaIndex**, scaffold production CI/CD + Terraform via **`agent-starter-pack`** / **`agents-cli`**, and deploy to **Agent Runtime**, **Cloud Run**, or **GKE** | Complex multi-agent topologies, strict compliance callbacks, custom deterministic guardrails, hybrid A2A meshes |

### Name changes you must recognize

| Current name | Former name | Exam / API note |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform** | Vertex AI | Evolution of the same platform; IAM permissions still use `aiplatform.*` |
| **Gemini Enterprise** (end-user app) | Google Agentspace | Unified enterprise search + multi-agent workspace supporting A2A and **A2UI** |
| **Agent Runtime** | Vertex AI Agent Engine / Reasoning Engine | Underlying REST/gRPC resource remains `projects/…/locations/…/reasoningEngines/<id>` |
| **Agent Search** | Vertex AI Search | Turnkey managed search/RAG (`discoveryengine.googleapis.com`) with connectors and native ACLs |
| **Agent Retrieval** | Vector Search 2.0 | Collections-based, self-tuning vector store with schema and auto-embeddings |
| **Vector Search 1.0** | Matching Engine | High-scale ScaNN ANN index-as-a-service |
| **Workflow Builder** (Gemini Enterprise) | Agent Designer | No-code builder for end-user chat agents and scheduled/triggered workflows in Gemini Enterprise |
| **Gemini 4 Argon / Gemini 3.x** | Gemini 1.5 / PaLM 2 | Active frontier (`gemini-4-argon`) and workhorse (`gemini-3.8-flash`) generations |

> **Model Garden pointer:** Model Garden catalogs Google first-party (Gemini 4 Argon, Gemini 3.8 Flash, Nano Banana 2.1, Gemini Omni 1.1 Flash, Veo 3.1, Lyria 3.5, Chirp 3), partner MaaS (Anthropic Claude, Mistral, DeepSeek), and open-weight models (Gemma 4, Gemma 3n, Llama). **Gemini itself is served only through managed Google endpoints** — you cannot self-host Gemini weights on Cloud Run or GKE; open models such as Gemma 4 can be self-hosted there.

---

## 02. Agent Runtime: Deploying & Scaling Stateful Agents

**Agent Runtime** is Google Cloud's fully managed, opinionated compute runtime purpose-built for stateful agents: sub-second cold starts, optional `min_instances` to keep instances warm, long-running and multi-day asynchronous execution, IAM and **VPC Service Controls** perimeter enforcement, private egress to on-prem/VPC resources via **Private Service Connect (PSC) interface** network attachments, cryptographic **Agent Identity** (`spiffe://…`), and zero-plumbing integration with **Sessions**, **Memory Bank**, **Example Store**, **Code Execution**, **A2A**, and OpenTelemetry observability.

### Framework & protocol support

| Support level | Frameworks & protocols |
| :--- | :--- |
| **First-class native integration** | **ADK** (Python via `adk deploy agent_engine` or `agents-cli`; Go via `adkgo`; Java & TypeScript via container deployment) |
| **Built-in SDK templates** | **LangChain**, **LangGraph**, **AG2**, **LlamaIndex** (**Preview**) |
| **Custom Python class** | **CrewAI** or any custom Python class implementing `query` / `async_query` / `stream_query` |
| **Agent2Agent (A2A) hosting** | Native **`A2aAgent`** wrapper (**Preview**) exposing an `AgentCard`, task store, and A2A task endpoints directly on Agent Runtime |
| **Any language / runtime** | Custom **Dockerfile** or pre-built **Artifact Registry container image** conforming to the Agent Runtime HTTP contract |

### Five deployment methods

| Method | Languages | Best for |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Developer Connect** (Git repository) | Python | GitOps CI/CD — automatically builds and deploys directly from a connected Git repo without managing local build artifacts |
| **Source files** (inline directory) | Python | Automated CI/CD pipelines and Terraform; packages local source directly with no Cloud Storage staging bucket required |
| **Dockerfile** | Any | Non-Python agents (Go, Java, TypeScript/Node) or Python agents needing OS-level system packages |
| **Container image** (Artifact Registry) | Any | Pre-built, vulnerability-scanned immutable images promoted from staging to prod; **lowest deployment latency** |
| **SDK object** (in-memory pickle) | Python | Rapid notebook/Colab prototyping (`client.runtimes.create(agent=my_agent)`); object must be serializable |

### SDK, `agent-starter-pack` & `agents-cli` production workflow

- **Agent Platform SDK (`google-cloud-agentplatform`):** Exposes `agentplatform.Client(project=…, location=…)` with `client.runtimes`, `client.sessions`, `client.sandboxes`, and `client.memory_banks` (superseding the legacy `vertexai.agent_engines` namespace).
- **`agent-starter-pack` & `agents-cli`:** Production scaffolding toolkit that generates standardized repo layouts:
  - Infrastructure-as-Code (**Terraform**) for staging/prod projects, least-privilege IAM, Artifact Registry, and VPC-SC/PSC wiring.
  - **Cloud Build** or GitHub Actions CI/CD pipelines with **evaluation gates** (`agents-cli eval` runs golden + trajectory evalsets on every PR and blocks promotion if scores regress).
  - Pre-wired **OpenTelemetry** tracing, BigQuery log sinks, and feedback collection for the post-deployment data flywheel.
- **Managed Agents API (`Agents API` + `Interactions API`, Preview):** Instead of deploying container code to `reasoningEngines`, you register an Agent config + **Skill Registry** bundles (`SKILL.md` + helper scripts/assets) and invoke it via `Interactions API`. Server-side state (`previous_interaction_id`) and `background=true` allow multi-hour execution without client polling loops, inside an isolated Linux container with **network egress disabled by default**.

> **Common trap — reserved environment variables:** Never override platform-managed environment variables such as `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT` or `PORT` in your deployment spec, and never use the reserved `GOOGLE_CLOUD_AGENT_ENGINE*` prefix for custom application variables (other than documented flags like `GOOGLE_CLOUD_AGENT_ENGINE_ENABLE_TELEMETRY=true`).

> **Exam tip:** **Agent Runtime hosts stateful agents, NOT standalone MCP tool servers.** Deploy custom **Streamable HTTP MCP servers** on **Cloud Run** (for serverless scale-to-zero) or **GKE**, register them in **Agent Registry**, and invoke them from your Agent Runtime agent.

---

## 03. Choosing a Runtime: Agent Runtime vs. Cloud Run vs. GKE

| Criterion | **Agent Runtime** | **Cloud Run** | **GKE (Standard / Autopilot)** |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Primary workload** | Stateful single- or multi-agent orchestrators (ADK, LangGraph, A2A) | Stateless A2UI/APIs, webhook handlers, **Streamable HTTP MCP servers** (`--functional-type=mcp-server`), async Jobs | Self-hosted open-weight models (Gemma 4 via vLLM/TGI), GPU/TPU workloads, dense multi-service meshes |
| **Ops overhead** | Lowest (fully managed agent harness) | Low (serverless containers) | Highest (cluster, node-pool, and networking lifecycle) |
| **State & memory** | Native **Sessions**, **Memory Bank**, **Example Store**, **Code Execution** & **Computer Use** (`Preview`) | Ephemeral local disk/RAM; externalize state to Agent Platform Sessions, Memorystore, Firestore, Spanner, or Cloud SQL | StatefulSets, local SSDs, or external managed databases |
| **Scaling, revisions & duration** | Autoscales up to **`1,000` instances** (**`100` in VPC-SC**); `min_instances` & `container_concurrency` (`Preview`); up to **`6,000` revisions** with `traffic-split` (*bypassed if Agent Gateway routes*); multi-day async workflows | Scales to zero (`$0` idle) up to `1,000` instances (`80–1,000` concurrency); HTTP timeout up to **60 min** (Services) / **24h** (Jobs); `--to-revisions` canary splits | Full control over HPA/VPA, custom metrics, GPU time-slicing, Istio/Gateway API L7 splits, and spot nodes |
| **Isolation & security** | IAM, VPC-SC, PSC interface (`AgentConnectivityTemplate`), Agent Identity, isolated Code Execution sandbox | IAM, Direct VPC egress, VPC-SC, built-in Agent Identity (`--functional-type=agent`) & Agent Registry integration | Workload Identity Federation, **GKE Sandbox (`RuntimeClassName: gvisor` / Kata)** kernel isolation, NetworkPolicies |
| **Hosts MCP servers?** | **No** | **Yes** (ideal for Streamable HTTP MCP servers) | **Yes** (high-density or stateful MCP fleets) |
| **Main trade-off** | **No custom GPUs/TPUs inside the runtime container**; non-Python stacks require custom containers | In-process memory vanishes on scale-in or instance recycle (optional L4 / RTX PRO 6000 GPUs for bursts) | Highest operational and Kubernetes platform engineering cost (full H100/H200/B200 & TPU control) |

**Architectural decision rules:**

1. **Python/ADK/LangGraph agent + minimal ops + managed Sessions & Memory Bank** → **Agent Runtime**.
2. **Custom remote MCP server (Streamable HTTP), polyglot TypeScript/Java/Go webhook agent, or spiky scale-to-zero workload** → **Cloud Run**.
3. **Self-hosting Gemma 4 / Llama on GPUs/TPUs, strict kernel-level multi-tenant sandboxing (`gVisor`), or existing enterprise K8s platform** → **GKE**.
4. **Zero-infrastructure autonomous coding/file/research agent where Google manages the loop and Linux sandbox** → **Managed Agents API (Preview)**.
5. **Hybrid regulated GPU topology (stateful ADK orchestrator + private self-hosted Gemma 4 SLM):** Host the orchestrator on **Agent Runtime** (for turnkey Sessions, Memory Bank, and SPIFFE Agent Identity) and invoke a private **GKE** GPU `vLLM` worker (or **Model Garden `PrivateEndpoint`**) over a **PSC interface** (`AgentConnectivityTemplate` with `vpcEgress: ALL_TRAFFIC` and `restricted.googleapis.com` `199.36.153.4/30`) inside **VPC-SC**—never attempt to attach GPUs directly to an Agent Runtime container.

> **Common trap — keeping conversation history in Cloud Run RAM:** Cloud Run instances scale to zero or recycle unpredictably, wiping in-process dictionaries and local SQLite files. Always externalize conversational state to **Agent Platform Sessions** (`--session_service_uri agentengine://<id>`), **Memorystore**, **Firestore**, **Spanner**, or **Cloud SQL**.

---

## 04. Context Engineering: Sessions, Memory Bank & Example Store

Effective agents practice **context engineering** — dynamically assembling only the task-relevant history, user facts, and few-shot demonstrations needed for the current turn rather than stuffing entire raw logs into the prompt window (which causes **context rot**, latency spikes, and quadratic attention cost).

### Core state vocabulary

| Abstraction | Scope | Lifetime | Typical contents |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Session** | Chronological append-only log of **Events** (user messages, model thoughts, tool calls, tool outputs) | Single conversation thread | Turn-by-turn dialogue and tool trace |
| **State** | Mutable key-value scratchpad (`session.state`, `user:`, `app:`, `temp:` prefixes in ADK) | Current turn (`temp:`) or current session | Cart IDs, workflow step flags, extracted slot values |
| **Memory Bank** | LLM-extracted, consolidated semantic facts & preferences | Persistent across sessions (with configurable TTL & revisions) | User role, preferred coding language, dietary/travel rules, recurring project context |
| **Example Store** (**Preview**) | Dynamically retrieved input→trajectory/output few-shot pairs | Persistent per agent/task corpus | Edge-case tool routing demonstrations, strict formatting exemplars |

**Managed Sessions, Context Compaction & Prefix Caching (Tier 1 + Tier 2):** ADK agents on Agent Runtime automatically persist sessions (`VertexAiSessionService`), while Cloud Run, GKE, or local dev workstations attach via `--session_service_uri agentengine://<id>` (or `DatabaseSessionService` on Spanner, AlloyDB, or Cloud SQL). Configure ADK **`EventsCompactionConfig(token_threshold=..., event_retention_size=...)`** to summarize older tool trajectories before hitting token limits, and pair with **`ContextCacheConfig`** (or implicit prefix caching). **Prefix-cache trap:** placing dynamic timestamps or per-turn user IDs at the **top** of the system prompt invalidates prefix caching on every turn—keep static instructions and tool schemas first.

### Memory Bank (long-term semantic & episodic memory)

- **Asynchronous LLM extraction & consolidation (`GenerateMemories`):** Extracts durable facts from session events in the background (zero hot-path latency penalty) and **consolidates** them with existing memories — merging duplicates, updating stale preferences, and resolving contradictions while keeping **memory revisions** for audit/rollback.
- **Explicit agent-triggered writes (`CreateMemory`):** Exposed as a tool ("memory-as-a-tool") when the user explicitly says *"Always format my SQL queries in GoogleSQL"* and immediate persistence is desired.
- **Scoped retrieval (`RetrieveMemories`):** Retrieves by exact scope or **semantic similarity search** against the active user turn.
- **Strict tenant isolation:** Every memory is keyed by an explicit identity scope such as `{user_id, app_name}` — never share an unscoped memory namespace across users.
- **Enterprise governance:** Custom **Memory Topics** (defining *what* is worth remembering and *what* PII must be ignored), multimodal event ingestion, **TTL** policies (default or per-memory expiration for GDPR/retention compliance), IAM Conditions, `roles/aiplatform.memoryViewer` / `roles/aiplatform.memoryEditor`, CMEK, and regional data residency (`gcp.resourceLocations`).
- **ADK integration:** `VertexAiMemoryBankService`; trigger incremental extraction from an `after_agent_callback` via `add_events_to_memory` (preferred over full-session `add_session_to_memory` to avoid redundant token processing).

> **Common trap — memory poisoning:** If untrusted external content (e.g., an email or web page fetched by a tool) tricks the extraction LLM into storing a malicious instruction in Memory Bank, that instruction is injected into *future* sessions (**persistent cross-session prompt injection**). Screen untrusted inputs with **Model Armor**, constrain extraction with strict **Memory Topics**, and audit memory revisions (**Security guide**).

### Example Store (Preview)

Stores curated few-shot demonstrations and dynamically injects only the top-$k$ semantically similar examples at inference time — improving edge-case accuracy without inflating every prompt.
- **Immutable embedding binding:** The embedding model (e.g., `text-embedding-005`, `text-multilingual-embedding-002`, or `gemini-embedding-001`) is **locked when the Example Store instance is created**; switching embedding models requires creating a new instance and re-indexing.
- **Quota awareness:** Up to 50 Example Store instances per project per region (verify current limits).

| Requirement | Right component |
| :--- | :--- |
| Recall what *this user* asked three turns ago | **Session** events / scratchpad `state` |
| Remember *this user's* preferred timezone and reporting style next month | **Memory Bank** |
| Show the model 3 similar complex SQL/tool trajectories at runtime | **Example Store** (**Preview**) |
| Answer questions grounded in 50,000 corporate policy PDFs with ACLs | **Agent Search** (Section 06) |

---

## 05. Code Execution Sandbox

The **Code Execution** sandbox executes untrusted, model-generated Python code inside a hardened micro-container completely separate from the agent's own runtime process:
- **Sub-second provisioning & stateful sessions:** Spins up and executes in `<1s`, supports file I/O up to **100 MB**, and preserves stateful sandbox files/variables across turns for up to **14 days** (configurable TTL).
- **ADK integration:** `AgentEngineSandboxCodeExecutor` binds **one isolated sandbox per session**, enabling multi-turn data science, chart generation, CSV reconciliation, and deterministic math verification. Callable even if the agent orchestrator itself runs on Cloud Run or GKE.
- **Managed Agents sandbox:** In the **Managed Agents API**, the built-in Linux execution environment runs with **no outbound network access by default** and mounts approved **Skill Registry** scripts/files cleanly into the workspace.

> **Mental model — runtime vs. sandbox:** **Agent Runtime** runs *trusted* orchestration code written and reviewed by engineers (and holds IAM/MCP credentials). The **Code Execution sandbox** runs *untrusted* code synthesized on the fly by an LLM. Running `exec()` inside the agent's own container exposes service-account tokens, environment variables, and VPC network paths.

---

## 06. Grounding, Retrieval & Enterprise Tooling

### Retrieval service decision matrix

| Service | Architecture | Choose when | Key limits & watch-outs |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Agent Search** (formerly Vertex AI Search) | Turnkey managed search & RAG (`discoveryengine`) | Enterprise documents across SharePoint, Drive, Confluence, Jira, GCS, or BigQuery needing built-in layout parsing, hybrid search, reranking, citations, and **document-level source ACL enforcement** | Less low-level control over custom chunking or bespoke embedding pipelines; max **10 data stores** per grounding request |
| **RAG Engine** | Code-first modular RAG orchestration over **corpora** (`RagCorpus` / `RagFile`) | Engineers need explicit control over chunk size/overlap, parser choice (default, LLM parser, **Document AI Layout Parser**), embedding model, and backing store (**RagManagedDb**, Agent Retrieval, Vector Search 1.0, Pinecone, Weaviate) | `ImportRagFiles` Layout Parser caps PDFs at **20 MB / 500 pages**; **Serverless mode** lacks CMEK while **Spanner mode** supports CMEK (**one-way mode lock-in**: corpora cannot migrate in place without re-indexing); Agent Retrieval corpora require `COSINE` distance |
| **Agent Retrieval** (formerly Vector Search 2.0) | Self-tuning, schema-aware collection store | Storing structured + unstructured **Data Objects** with automatic managed embeddings (`vertex_embedding_config`) or BYO vectors without cluster sizing | Exact brute-force KNN up to ~100k objects; create an ANN **Collection Index** beyond ~100k objects; CMEK (`--kms-key`) must be set at collection creation |
| **Vector Search 1.0** | High-scale ScaNN ANN index-as-a-service | 100k to billions of BYO dense/sparse vectors at sub-10ms latency with fine-grained ScaNN tree/hashing tuning and `STREAM_UPDATE` or `BATCH_UPDATE` pipelines | `IndexEndpoint` bills **24/7 VM node-hours even at 0 QPS**; `dimensions` and `distanceMeasureType` are immutable; stores IDs + vectors + restricts only (hydrate payload text externally) |
| **AlloyDB AI / Cloud SQL (`pgvector` / ScaNN)** | Transactional operational DB vectors | Low-latency hybrid SQL filters (`WHERE tenant_id = $1 AND status = 'OPEN'`) joined directly with live ACID rows (`scann` on AlloyDB; HNSW/IVFFlat on Cloud SQL) | Pin an **explicit embedding model version** in `google_ml_integration` `embedding()` calls so model updates never cause silent vector drift; size connection pools via `MCP Toolbox` |
| **BigQuery (`VECTOR_SEARCH`)** | In-warehouse SQL vector search (`IVF` `< 10M` rows; `TREE_AH` up to `200M` rows) | Batch enrichment, analytical SQL joins over petabyte warehouse tables, and offline evaluation pipelines | Hundreds of milliseconds to seconds cold analytical startup latency; wrong fit for sub-50ms online chat QPS |
| **Firestore Vector Search** | Serverless operational NoSQL document + flat/KNN vector store | Mobile/web or operational agent documents already stored in Firestore needing integrated metadata + vector lookups | Max **2,048 dimensions** (truncate 3,072d embeddings via `output_dimensionality <= 2048` + L2 re-normalize), max **1,000 results** per query, and **no real-time snapshot listeners** on vector queries |
| **Grounding with Google Search / Maps / Web** | Managed live public-index grounding | Fresh public facts, news, places/geospatial context, or third-party enterprise web grounding (Parallel, Exa) | Must render required **Search Suggestions** / attribution chips from `groundingMetadata` |

> **Common trap: `DOT_PRODUCT` metric failure under RAG Engine:** When backing a **RAG Engine** corpus with an **Agent Retrieval** or Vector Search index, configure the index distance metric as **`COSINE`**. RAG Engine issues cosine-distance queries, so leaving the index at `DOT_PRODUCT` fails at runtime with `FAILED_PRECONDITION`.

### Embedding models, normalization & distance metric maths

| Model | Modalities & language scope | Max dimensions & input cap | `task_type` & Matryoshka support | Key operational trap |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **`text-embedding-005`** (`GA`) | English text and source code | Up to **768** dims; **2,048-token** max input | Supports **8 `task_type` values** (`RETRIEVAL_DOCUMENT`, `RETRIEVAL_QUERY`, `QUESTION_ANSWERING`, `FACT_VERIFICATION`, `CLASSIFICATION`, `CLUSTERING`, `SEMANTIC_SIMILARITY`, `CODE_RETRIEVAL_QUERY`) and Matryoshka `output_dimensionality`; unit L2-normalized at 768d | Accuracy degrades on non-English corpora; switch to `text-multilingual-embedding-002` or `gemini-embedding-001` for multilingual text |
| **`gemini-embedding-001`** (`GA`) | Multilingual text (100+ languages) and code | Up to **3,072** dims; **2,048-token** max input | Asymmetric **`RETRIEVAL_DOCUMENT`** (corpus indexing) vs. **`RETRIEVAL_QUERY`** (user query); Matryoshka output slicing (`768`, `1,536`, `3,072`) | Exceeds Firestore's 2,048-dimension ceiling at default 3,072d; set `output_dimensionality <= 2048` (e.g., `768` or `1536`) and **L2 re-normalize** the truncated slice before indexing |
| **`gemini-embedding-2`** (`GA` / rolling multimodal) | Unified omni-modal space: text, images, audio, video, and PDFs | Up to **3,072** dims; **8,192-token** max input | Cross-modal retrieval in one shared vector space; supports managed auto-embeddings in Agent Retrieval (`global`, `us`, `eu`) | Long recordings or PDFs exceeding 8,192 tokens must be segmented into timestamped or page-bounded clips (`start_offset` / `end_offset` metadata per `DataObject`) |

* **L2 normalization and distance metric equivalence:** When vectors are unit L2-normalized (`‖u‖₂ = ‖v‖₂ = 1`), cosine similarity equals the inner dot product (`u · v`) and produces the exact same monotonic neighbor ordering as squared Euclidean distance (`‖u − v‖₂² = 2 − 2(u · v)`). Under unit normalization, **`DOT_PRODUCT_DISTANCE`** is the fastest hardware SIMD execution path in ScaNN.
* **Un-normalized and Matryoshka-sliced vectors:** Truncating a Matryoshka vector via `output_dimensionality` (or importing third-party encoders) breaks unit length (`‖u‖₂ < 1`). Using raw `DOT_PRODUCT_DISTANCE` on un-normalized vectors biases top-`k` toward high-magnitude vectors; either L2 re-normalize vectors before upsert, configure `featureNormType: "UNIT_L2_NORM"` on the Vector Search index, or select `COSINE_DISTANCE`.

### Vector Search 1.0 index & endpoint tuning

| Knob / configuration | Purpose & mechanics | Architectural guidance & exam traps |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **`treeAhConfig` vs. `bruteForceConfig`** | `treeAhConfig` combines two-level ScaNN Tree partitioning with Asymmetric Hashing for fast ANN; `bruteForceConfig` runs exact exhaustive linear scan | Use `treeAhConfig` for `100k` to billions of vectors at sub-10ms latency; reserve `bruteForceConfig` for small datasets (`< ~50k` vectors) or `100%`-recall ground-truth benchmarking |
| **`leafNodeEmbeddingCount`** | Target number of vectors per ScaNN tree leaf partition (default ~`1000`) | Smaller leaf sizes build finer-grained partitions and raise recall at the cost of higher index build time and memory footprint |
| **`leafNodesToSearchPercent`** | Percentage of tree leaf partitions probed per query (e.g., `5`–`10`%) | Primary runtime latency-vs-recall dial; doubling the searched leaf percentage increases vCPU consumption roughly linearly |
| **`approximateNeighborsCount`** | Pre-reordering candidate pool scored via fast asymmetric hashing before exact full-precision rescoring | Always set strictly greater than requested `neighbor_count` (`> k`, e.g., `100`–`200` for top-`10`) so quantization noise does not drop true nearest neighbors |
| **`restricts`, `numeric_restricts` & crowding** | Categorical token filters (`namespace` with `allow` / `deny` lists), typed numeric range predicates, and `per_crowding_attribute_num_neighbors` | Enforce tenant/metadata pre-filtering inside the ANN scan; set **crowding** (e.g., max `2` neighbors per `document_id` or `brand_id`) so one verbose document never monopolizes top-`k` |
| **`STREAM_UPDATE` vs. `BATCH_UPDATE`** | `STREAM_UPDATE` accepts real-time `UpsertDatapoints` / deletes within seconds with background compaction; `BATCH_UPDATE` rebuilds immutable shards from GCS | `STREAM_UPDATE` carries higher hourly node cost for live freshness; `BATCH_UPDATE` lowers serving cost when minutes-to-hours refresh lag is acceptable |
| **`IndexEndpoint` deployment & networking** | Hosts deployed index shards on dedicated machine types (`minReplicaCount` to `maxReplicaCount`) via public endpoint, VPC Peering, or **Private Service Connect** | **Four classic traps:** (1) `IndexEndpoint` bills **24/7 VM node-hours even at `0` QPS** (`minReplicaCount >= 1`); (2) `dimensions` and `distanceMeasureType` are **immutable** after creation; (3) prefer **PSC (`pscAutomationConfigs`)** over VPC Peering to avoid `/26+` subnet CIDR exhaustion; (4) stores IDs + vectors + restricts only (fetch chunk text from GCS, Firestore, AlloyDB, or BigQuery) |

### Vector Search 1.0 vs. Agent Retrieval vs. RAG Engine

When the matrix above leaves two vector options close, compare them on these dimensions.

* **Object model:** Vector Search 1.0 holds datapoints (an ID, the embedding, optional filter metadata) in an index deployed to an endpoint, so the source text or record lives in a separate store. Agent Retrieval keeps JSON **Data Objects** (payload fields plus one or more vector fields) inside a schema-validated **Collection**. RAG Engine exposes `RagCorpus` and `RagFile` resources and hands the vectors to a backing vector database.
* **Embedding pipeline:** Vector Search 1.0 is bring-your-own: you compute dense (and, for hybrid, sparse) vectors before upserting. Agent Retrieval accepts your own vectors or fills a vector field automatically from a `vertex_embedding_config` (model ID, text template built from payload fields, task type) whenever a Data Object arrives without that vector. RAG Engine parses, chunks, and embeds files for you at import time (`ImportRagFiles` with Document AI Layout Parser supports up to **20 MB / 500 pages** per PDF).
* **Hybrid search and reranking:** Vector Search 1.0 fuses a dense and a sparse index with Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF), weighted by `rrf_ranking_alpha`, and you build the sparse vectors (for example SPLADE or TF-IDF) yourself. Agent Retrieval combines semantic search with built-in keyword text search through RRF and can rerank results with the Ranking API. RAG Engine sets reranking in `RagRetrievalConfig` (`rank_service` for a semantic ranker model or `llm_ranker` for a Gemini model); its `hybrid_search.alpha` setting applies only when Weaviate is the backing store.
* **Agent and MCP integration:** Vector Search 1.0 needs a custom function tool or your own MCP server. Agent Retrieval has a Google-managed stateless remote MCP server (Preview, read-only tools; see the MCP catalogue below). RAG Engine attaches a corpus to Gemini requests as a `vertex_rag_store` retrieval tool.
* **Scaling and cost:** Vector Search 1.0 bills deployed index endpoints by node-hour, even when idle. Agent Retrieval serves brute-force KNN with no index; add a Collection Index once a collection nears 100,000 Data Objects or KNN latency is too high for your query rate. Its pricing is usage-based for small workloads or resource-based for tuned performance.
* **CMEK on Agent Retrieval:** set the Cloud KMS key (same region as the collection) when you create the Collection (`--kms-key`). An existing collection cannot be switched to CMEK, so export its Data Objects to Cloud Storage and import them into a new CMEK collection.
* **RAG Engine deployment modes (one-way lock-in):** one RAG API routes to whichever mode the project has active; corpora created under the other mode stay stored but hidden until you switch back, and modes **cannot be migrated in place** without re-indexing.
   * **Serverless mode** needs no tier management, autoscales, and by default provisions an Agent Retrieval collection in your project as the vector database (Pinecone and Weaviate are alternatives; RagManagedDb is not offered). Storage is not isolated and **CMEK is not supported**.
   * **Spanner mode** is the default when no mode is chosen. It runs a dedicated Spanner instance at the **Basic** tier (default, fixed low compute) or the **Scaled** tier (autoscaling, production data volumes); the **Unprovisioned** tier deletes the instance and its data. It isolates storage and performance, **supports CMEK**, and offers RagManagedDb (default), Agent Retrieval, Vector Search 1.0, Pinecone, and Weaviate as vector stores.
   * **Both modes** support VPC Service Controls.
* **When to choose:** **Vector Search 1.0** for existing pipelines with your own embedders and tuned, always-on ANN endpoints; **Agent Retrieval** for a new custom agent store that keeps payload and vectors together with auto-embeddings, keyword plus semantic search, and an MCP server; **RAG Engine Serverless mode** for the fastest managed document RAG when CMEK is not required; **RAG Engine Spanner mode** (or a CMEK-enabled Agent Retrieval collection) when policy demands CMEK or isolated storage and performance.
* **Anti-pattern (Serverless mode under a CMEK mandate):** the mode has no CMEK option, so a key-management policy rules it out. Pick Spanner mode before importing data, because corpora do not carry over between modes.

### Reranking, hybrid RRF & citation verification

| Mechanism | Latency & candidate scale | How it works | Key trap & operational guidance |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Agent Platform Ranking API** (`semantic-ranker-*`, e.g., `semantic-ranker-default@latest`) | **`< 100 ms`** over up to ~200 candidate chunks | Stateless cross-encoder jointly attends to the query and each candidate passage, narrowing noisy recall down to high-precision top-`k` | Requires **`discoveryengine.googleapis.com`** enabled (`roles/discoveryengine.viewer` / ranking permission) even when called from custom RAG pipelines, or requests fail with **`403 PERMISSION_DENIED`** |
| **Agent Search built-in ranking (`BoostSpec`)** | Zero extra network hop (inline in `discoveryengine`) | Combines managed semantic + keyword retrieval with declarative condition-based score multipliers (freshness decay, authoritative source boosts) | Applies only inside Agent Search queries; configure bounded positive/negative boost weights so boosted low-relevance docs do not crowd out exact answers |
| **LLM reranker** (`llm_ranker` in RAG Engine / Gemini listwise reranking) | **`1–2+ s` TTFT**; high input-token cost | Prompts a generative Gemini model to reason across candidate passages for complex multi-constraint relevance | Prohibitive latency and token spend on high-QPS chat or large `top_k` pools; reserve for low-QPS research synthesis or cascade after cross-encoder pruning |
| **Hybrid sparse + dense + RRF** (`rrf_ranking_alpha`) | Single-digit ms fusion overhead | Reciprocal Rank Fusion merges lexical sparse rank (exact SKUs, part numbers, error codes, acronyms) with dense semantic rank on a rank-order scale | `rrf_ranking_alpha` spans `[0.0, 1.0]`: **`0.5`** weights dense and sparse rankings equally, whereas **`1.0` weights dense vectors `100%` and silently ignores sparse keyword matches** (`0.0` uses sparse keywords only) |

* **Check Grounding API:** Evaluates each claim in a candidate answer against supplied source facts, returning a support score and per-sentence citations to block ungrounded hallucinations.
* **Grounding metadata:** Inspect `groundingChunks`, `groundingSupports`, `webSearchQueries`, and `searchEntryPoint` to render verifiable inline citations.
* **Agent Search grounding limits:** Attach up to **10 data stores** per request; callers require `roles/discoveryengine.viewer` (and user identity propagation via Workforce Identity or OAuth when enforcing source document ACLs).

### Google Cloud MCP servers & enterprise integration layers

Google Cloud provides both **first-party remote `StreamableHTTP` MCP servers** (`https://<service>.googleapis.com/mcp` or regional `.rep.googleapis.com/mcp`, auto-registered in `global` **Agent Registry** when the underlying API is enabled, supporting stateless MCP spec **`2026-07-28`** without `initialize` or `Mcp-Session-Id` state) and four complementary enterprise tool integration layers for databases, SaaS/ERPs, OpenAPI microservices, and custom logic.

#### First-party Google Cloud & database MCP servers catalogue

| MCP server / project | Capabilities | Hosting & discovery mode | Required IAM / auth | Operational traps |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **`bigquery.googleapis.com/mcp`** | Dataset/table discovery, schema inspection, dry-run validation, and SQL execution | Google-hosted remote `StreamableHTTP` (`global` Agent Registry) | `roles/mcp.toolUser` + `roles/bigquery.jobUser` + `roles/bigquery.dataViewer` (row/column ACLs apply) | Unbounded analytical scans spike slot/byte bills; enforce `maximumBytesBilled` or expose curated authorized views |
| **`container.googleapis.com/mcp`** | GKE cluster, node-pool, workload, and pod diagnostics | Google-hosted remote `StreamableHTTP` (`global` Agent Registry) | `roles/mcp.toolUser` + `roles/container.viewer` (or `roles/container.developer` for mutations) | Scope troubleshooting agents to `container.viewer` so prompt injection cannot mutate live cluster specs |
| **`compute.googleapis.com/mcp`** | Compute Engine VM inventory, metadata inspection, and instance lifecycle actions | Google-hosted remote `StreamableHTTP` (`global` Agent Registry) | `roles/mcp.toolUser` + `roles/compute.viewer` / `roles/compute.instanceAdmin.v1` | Gate stop/reset/delete tools with IAM UAP `iap.googleapis.com/mcp.tool.isReadOnly` CEL predicates or HITL approval |
| **`run.googleapis.com/mcp`** | Inspect and deploy Cloud Run services, revisions, and traffic splits | Google-hosted remote `StreamableHTTP` (`global` Agent Registry) | `roles/mcp.toolUser` + `roles/run.viewer` / `roles/run.developer` | Manages Cloud Run itself; *custom* MCP servers hosted *on* Cloud Run deploy as Services with `--functional-type=mcp-server` + `--no-allow-unauthenticated` + IAP |
| **`logging.googleapis.com/mcp`** (plus Monitoring / Trace MCP) | Query Cloud Logging entries, metrics, and trace spans during incident triage | Google-hosted remote `StreamableHTTP` (`global` Agent Registry) | `roles/mcp.toolUser` + `roles/logging.viewer` / `roles/logging.viewAccessor` | Require bounded `timestamp` filters on every query to prevent full-bucket scans and context-window overflow |
| **Cloud SQL / AlloyDB / Spanner / Firestore / Cloud Storage MCP** | Instance management, `execute_sql` / `execute_sql_readonly`, NoSQL ops, and `storage.googleapis.com/storage/mcp` object R/W | Google-hosted remote `StreamableHTTP` (`global` Agent Registry; AlloyDB regional Preview) | `roles/mcp.toolUser` + underlying DB/bucket IAM roles | Prefer `execute_sql_readonly` or parameterized **MCP Toolbox** tools over unrestricted SQL write endpoints |
| **`developerknowledge.googleapis.com/mcp`** (plus Maps Grounding Lite) | Search public English Google developer documentation (and live place/geospatial facts) | Google-hosted non-Cloud remote `StreamableHTTP` | API key or OAuth (no `roles/mcp.toolUser`; not governed by Cloud IAM policies) | **VPC-SC trap:** indexes public English docs only and does **not** support the `restricted.googleapis.com` VIP inside VPC-SC; route egress via **`private.googleapis.com`** |
| **Agent Retrieval MCP** (`vectorsearch.googleapis.com/mcp`, `Preview`) | Nine read-only tools for collection/index inspection plus vector, semantic, hybrid, and keyword search (no write tools) | Google-hosted stateless `StreamableHTTP` (MCP spec `2026-07-28`) | `roles/mcp.toolUser` + `roles/vectorsearch.viewer` + `roles/agentregistry.viewer` | Client must attach target project/routing headers on every `tools/call`; strictly read-only |
| **MCP Toolbox for Databases** (`googleapis/genai-toolbox` / `mcp-toolbox`, `GA`) | Prebuilt (`--prebuilt=<db>`) and declarative `tools.yaml` parameterized SQL/Cypher/NoSQL with connection pooling and OTel across **30+ DBs** | Self-hosted on Cloud Run / GKE (`StreamableHTTP`) or local `stdio` (`ToolboxToolset` / `McpToolset`) | IAM DB auth + Cloud Run Invoker / IAP + optional per-tool OAuth/OIDC | Never expose a generic raw `run_any_sql` string parameter; bind typed parameters in `tools.yaml` to prevent SQL injection |

> [!NOTE]
> Additional Google-managed remote MCP servers also cover Bigtable, Memorystore, Pub/Sub, Apigee API Hub, and Knowledge Catalog. Verify per-service launch stage and supported regions in the Google Cloud MCP documentation before production rollout.

#### Four-way enterprise tool integration matrix

When connecting beyond native first-party Google Cloud MCP endpoints, select the integration layer matching your backend protocol and governance boundary:

| Integration layer | ADK toolset class | Target systems & strengths | Latency, auth & operational traps |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Integration Connectors + Application Integration** (`GA`) | `ApplicationIntegrationToolset` | **100+ SaaS, ERP, and CRM platforms** (Salesforce, ServiceNow, SAP, Workday, Jira) with visual schema mapping, payload transformation, and **Auth Manager 3LO** user-delegated consent | Higher per-invocation hop latency and connector execution cost than direct database or REST calls |
| **MCP Toolbox for Databases** (`GA`) | `ToolboxToolset` / `McpToolset` | **Sub-50ms pooled database queries** across 30+ relational, graph, and analytical engines (AlloyDB, Cloud SQL, Spanner, BigQuery, Postgres, Neo4j, Snowflake) via declarative `tools.yaml` and OTel tracing | Database-centric only; provides no prebuilt SaaS/ERP business-object adapters |
| **Apigee + API Hub** (`GA`) | `ApiHubToolset` (or `OpenAPIToolset` for small direct specs) | **Cataloged OpenAPI REST microservices** fronted by enterprise rate limits, LLM token quotas, mTLS, semantic caching, and inline Model Armor | **Tool-bloat trap:** always filter specific OpenAPI operations rather than importing 200 raw REST endpoints into one agent's prompt context |
| **Custom Remote MCP on Cloud Run** (`GA`) | `McpToolset` (`StreamableHTTPConnectionParams`) | **Bespoke polyglot domain logic** and multi-API composition deployed with `--functional-type=mcp-server`, `--no-allow-unauthenticated`, and **Cloud IAP + Agent Gateway** | **Header-split trap:** Cloud Run consumes `Authorization` to verify the caller's OIDC token; pass Cloud Run OIDC in **`X-Serverless-Authorization`** when forwarding a user OAuth token in `Authorization`, or delegate token brokering to **Agent Gateway + Auth Manager** |

* **Transport & principal rule:** Use `stdio` only for local IDE/CLI subprocesses; production remote tools require **`StreamableHTTP`** over HTTPS authenticated via cryptographic **SPIFFE Agent Identity** (for agent-scoped cloud/DB actions) or **Auth Manager 3LO OAuth** (when downstream SaaS/workspace tools must enforce per-user ACLs).

### Agent Registry end-to-end governance workflow

**Agent Registry** serves as the centralized control-plane catalog for agents (`AgentCard`), MCP servers (`McpServer`), and standalone skills across your organization:

| Governance dimension | Platform behavior & workflow | Key IAM roles & exam traps |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Auto-discovery vs. manual registration** | **Auto-discovered:** Agent Runtime (`reasoningEngines`), Cloud Run Services deployed with `--functional-type=mcp-server` (Cloud Run Jobs cannot be MCP servers), GKE workloads labeled `registry.gke.io/functional-type: "MCP_SERVER"` with `modelcontextprotocol.info/*` annotations, and 1P Google Cloud MCP servers (registered only in `--location=global`, with regional URLs inside `interfaces`). **Manual (`gcloud agent-registry`):** external, on-prem, cross-project (outside management boundary), or regional-residency endpoints; MCP registration requires uploading a **`toolspec.json`** (`<= 10 KB`, declaring tool schemas plus `readOnlyHint` / `destructiveHint`) because the registry does not crawl external servers | Querying 1P Google Cloud MCP servers with `--location=us-central1` returns `NOT_FOUND` (use `--location=global`). Manual registration requires `roles/agentregistry.editor` or `roles/agentregistry.admin` |
| **Discovery vs. invocation authorization** | Catalog visibility and live network invocation are strictly separated | **`roles/agentregistry.viewer` grants catalog discovery and metadata read only**; it never permits calling the live A2A or MCP endpoint. Runtime invocation requires **`roles/iap.egressor`** (evaluated with IAM UAP CEL predicates at Agent Gateway / IAP) plus target endpoint IAM (`roles/run.invoker` or `roles/mcp.toolUser`) |
| **Gemini Enterprise Agent Gallery alignment** | Match the Agent Registry location (`global`, `us`, `eu`, or specific region) to your **Gemini Enterprise** app location so published enterprise agents populate the workforce **Agent Gallery** | Business users discover governed organizational agents via *Agent Gallery -> Request access -> "From your organization"* and invoke them inline with `@agent_name`; mismatched registry/app regions hide the agent from the gallery |
| **CI/CD gating & version cutovers** | Built-in pre-registration CI approval workflows and a formal `DEPRECATED` lifecycle flag on MCP/agent endpoints are **not publicly documented** in Agent Registry itself | Gate catalog writes by restricting `roles/agentregistry.admin` / `editor` to your **Cloud Build** CI service account (unlocked only after `agents-cli eval` regression gates pass), and perform zero-downtime version cutovers or retirements via semantic **`AgentCard.version`** fields paired with **Agent Gateway** routing |
| **ADK runtime resolution & `.clone()`** | Resolve `AgentRegistry.get_remote_a2a_agent()` and `get_mcp_toolset()` **once at process startup** rather than inside per-turn request handlers | Avoids per-turn control-plane discovery latency and quota burn; always call **`.clone()`** when attaching the same resolved remote A2A agent across multiple ADK workflow branches so parent-pointer tree state does not collide |

### Skill Registry lifecycle

**Skill Registry** (Preview) is the Agent Platform repository for agent skills in the open Agent Skills layout: a `SKILL.md` file plus optional `scripts/`, `references/`, and `assets/` folders. Agents load a skill only when the task calls for it, instead of carrying every instruction in the prompt. **Agent Registry** can also hold the same packages as *standalone skills*, alongside agents and MCP servers. That second path has its own API, roles, and tighter payload limits, so keep the two apart.

| Stage | Skill Registry (Agent Platform API) | Agent Registry standalone skills |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Author** | `SKILL.md` front matter: `name` (required, max 64 characters, lowercase letters, digits, and hyphens, no leading or trailing hyphen), `description` (required, max 1,024 characters), optional `license` (max 1,024). Instructions body max 500,000 characters. The skill ID (1 to 63 characters, starts with a letter) stays reserved even after deletion, and the `gcp-` prefix is reserved for built-in skills | Same `SKILL.md`, placed at the zip root with valid front matter per the Agent Skills specification |
| **Publish and validate** | `CreateSkill` long-running operation (REST `v1beta1`, or `client.skills.create` in the `agentplatform` SDK) with a base64 zip. Asynchronous validation rejects a zip over **10 MB**, over 500 MB unzipped, over **10,000** entries, nested deeper than 8 folders, compression ratio over 100, any **symbolic link**, duplicate names, `..` or absolute paths, or a missing `SKILL.md` | `gcloud alpha agent-registry skills create` with `--payload` (local zip) or `--gcs-source-uri`. Limits: **500 KB** compressed, 10 MB uncompressed, 1 MB per file, 8 folder levels. The ID gets a `private-` prefix, and a Cloud Storage import needs the Agent Registry service agent to hold `storage.objects.get` |
| **Revisions** | Every create or update stores an immutable **skill revision**; `GetSkill` returns the latest one, and `ListSkillRevisions` / `GetSkillRevision` expose history | New skills start `DISABLED`; set the default revision and switch the target state to Active before agents can discover it |
| **Discover** | `ListSkills` returns name, display name, and description; `RetrieveSkills` runs semantic search over display name and description. The built-in **`gcp-skill-registry`** skill (Google-managed) lets an agent create, search, and manage skills itself; it appears after the first API call | Agent Registry search across agents, MCP servers, and skills |
| **Authorize** | Inherits project IAM: `roles/aiplatform.user` to manage skills, `roles/aiplatform.viewer` for read-only access | `roles/agentregistry.viewer` (discover and read), `roles/agentregistry.user` (read plus create, update, delete skills and revisions), `roles/agentregistry.editor` (skills plus agents, MCP servers, endpoints), `roles/agentregistry.admin` (everything plus bindings and skill IAM policies) |
| **Govern at runtime** | **Semantic governance policies** (Preview) intercept the ADK skill tools and judge each call against natural language constraints (NLCs) | Same policies apply, because loading a skill is itself a tool call |

Progressive disclosure at runtime runs through four ADK skill tools, and each one is a point where a policy can return a verdict:

1. **`list_skills`** shows the model only the catalog of skill names and descriptions.
2. **`load_skill`** pulls one skill's full instructions and tools into context.
3. **`load_skill_resource`** fetches a referenced file or asset on demand.
4. **`run_skill_script`** executes the skill's bundled code.

```yaml
---
name: invoice-triage
description: Sorts supplier invoices by urgency and flags missing PO numbers. Use when a user shares or asks about an invoice.
license: Apache-2.0
---
# Invoice triage
1. Extract the PO number, amount, and due date.
2. Run `scripts/check_po.py` to confirm the PO exists before routing.
```

* **Compliance (Skill Registry):** Access Transparency and US/EU data residency are supported; CMEK, VPC Service Controls, and HIPAA are not. Regions: `us-central1`, `europe-west4`, `us-east5`.
* **Tainted-session control:** an NLC can deny `load_skill` for any skill that sends messages or writes externally once the history contains web, email, or uploaded content, so the outbound tools never enter context.
* **Supply-chain control:** an NLC can inspect the arguments of an install tool triggered by skill instructions and deny packages outside an allowlist.
* **Caveat:** semantic governance uses an LLM, so verdicts are probabilistic. Keep IAM and network egress controls as the deterministic layer.
* **Anti-pattern (registry admin roles on agents):** granting `roles/agentregistry.admin` or `roles/agentregistry.editor` to an agent identity lets a compromised agent alter tool definitions or enroll a malicious agent. On the Agent Registry standalone-skills path, give consuming agents `roles/agentregistry.viewer` and publishers or CI pipelines `roles/agentregistry.user`; on the Skill Registry path, use `roles/aiplatform.viewer` for consumers and `roles/aiplatform.user` for publishers.
* **Anti-pattern (IAM as the only skill control):** IAM decides who may publish or read a package, but an authorized agent can still be steered by injected content into loading a powerful skill. Pair IAM with semantic governance policies.

---

## 07. Caching & External State

| Backing store | Primary role in an agentic architecture |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Gemini Context Caching** | **Implicit caching** (on by default, zero storage fee; **the only context cache mode on `gemini-4-argon`**) and **Explicit caching** (`cachedContents` with TTL + storage fee on supported Gemini 2.5/3.x models) for massive repeated system instructions, tool schemas, or static corpora |
| **Memorystore for Redis / Valkey** | Sub-millisecond (`< 1 ms`) hot state, sliding-window rate-limit/budget counters, Pub/Sub `messageId` idempotency locks, and **semantic response caching** via Redis HNSW/FLAT vector search |
| **Firestore** | Serverless multi-region (`99.999%`) strong-consistency document store for real-time UI state sync, HITL approval queues, and subcollection turn logs |
| **Cloud SQL / AlloyDB** | ACID relational workflow checkpoints; backs ADK's `DatabaseSessionService` (with PgBouncer / AlloyDB connection pooling) when custom SQL querying over sessions is required |
| **Agent Platform Sessions** | Zero-ops managed event & scratchpad persistence (`VertexAiSessionService`, default 365-day TTL, regional CMEK) for ADK and Agent Runtime |
| **Cloud Storage (`GcsArtifactService`)** | Versioned binary blob store (`{app}/{user}/{session}/{filename}/{version}` and `user:` scope) for large PDFs, audio, images, and sandbox outputs outside `session.state` |
| **BigQuery** | Long-term telemetry sink, offline evaluation datasets, failure-cluster analytics, and FinOps token attribution; **never hot-path turn state** |

> **Common trap: cross-tenant semantic cache leakage:** If User A asks *"What is the Q4 executive bonus pool?"* and the semantic cache keys only on the query embedding, User B asking a similar question can receive User A's restricted answer. **Always partition semantic cache keys by tenant/role/ACL scope** (or bypass semantic caching entirely for user-authorized data).

### Choosing data services by agent data need

Split agent data by access pattern rather than putting everything in one database. Each row names the default pick and the usual fallback.

| Data need | Default service | Common alternative | Why the default fits |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Conversation sessions** (events + state) | **Agent Platform Sessions** via `VertexAiSessionService` | Cloud SQL or AlloyDB via `DatabaseSessionService` | No schema to own; same store reachable from Agent Runtime, Cloud Run, GKE, or a laptop; feeds Memory Bank generation |
| **Long-term user memory** | **Memory Bank** (`VertexAiMemoryBankService`, Section 04) | Your own facts table with vectors in AlloyDB/Cloud SQL (`pgvector`) or Firestore vector search | Managed LLM extraction, consolidation, identity-scoped similarity retrieval, TTL, and revisions |
| **Semantic cache** | **Memorystore for Redis** vector search (Redis 7.2; HNSW approximate or FLAT exact) | AlloyDB vector index | Sub-millisecond in-memory lookups with native key expiry, so repeated or paraphrased prompts skip the model call |
| **Rate-limit, budget & idempotency locks** | **Memorystore** (Redis/Valkey atomic increments & `SET NX` TTL keys) | Firestore transactional documents (higher latency, ~1 write/s/doc limit) | Sub-millisecond atomic operations suit per-user throttling and Pub/Sub `messageId` deduplication on the hot path |
| **Transactional data that tools read and write** | **Cloud SQL** or **AlloyDB** | **Spanner** (global scale) or **Firestore** (document model) | ACID transactions, joins, and vector columns next to live rows; reachable through managed MCP servers or MCP Toolbox |
| **Analytics and agent telemetry** | **BigQuery** | Cloud Logging Log Analytics | Serverless SQL over prompt/response logs, traces, eval results, and token cost; never the per-turn state store |
| **Documents, media, and artifacts** | **Cloud Storage** (ADK `GcsArtifactService` for agent outputs) | BigQuery object tables (SQL metadata over Cloud Storage objects) | Durable object storage (including Zonal Rapid buckets) that also feeds Agent Search, RAG Engine, and Agent Retrieval ingestion |
| **Vector embeddings** | **Agent Retrieval** or **Vector Search 1.0** (Section 06 matrix) | AlloyDB/Cloud SQL `pgvector`, Firestore vector search, BigQuery `VECTOR_SEARCH` | Purpose-built ANN and hybrid search; pick the operational database when vectors must be filtered with live transactional rows |

### ADK state services (`SessionService`, `MemoryService`, `ArtifactService`) & backing stores

| ADK interface / backing store | Persistence scope & features | Production limits & architectural traps |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **`VertexAiSessionService`** (Agent Platform Sessions, `GA`) | Managed chronological `Event` log + `session.state` (`--session_service_uri agentengine://<id>`); **365-day default TTL** (configurable), regional data residency, and **CMEK** | Default on Agent Runtime and callable from Cloud Run or GKE; never stuff OAuth tokens, secrets, unredacted PII, or multi-MB blobs into `session.state` |
| **`VertexAiMemoryBankService`** (Agent Platform Memory Bank, `GA`) | Asynchronous `GenerateMemories` consolidation (`add_events_to_memory` in `after_agent_callback`) and explicit `CreateMemory` tool writes with revisions, Memory Topics, TTL, and CMEK | Always scope by `{user_id, app_name}` to prevent cross-tenant leakage; screen external inputs with Model Armor to block memory poisoning |
| **`DatabaseSessionService`** (AlloyDB / Cloud SQL / Spanner, `GA`) | Relational ACID persistence in customer-operated PostgreSQL/MySQL/Spanner (or local SQLite for dev) when SQL reporting, row-level security, or custom VPC residency is required | **Connection-exhaustion trap:** autoscaling Cloud Run containers quickly exhaust PostgreSQL `max_connections` unless fronted by **PgBouncer**, **AlloyDB Auth Proxy pooling**, or bounded SQLAlchemy pools |
| **`InMemorySessionService`** (Process RAM) | Ephemeral in-process dictionary for unit tests and local `adk web` | Wiped on container restart, scale-to-zero, or horizontal load-balancing across replicas; never use in production |
| **Firestore** (Custom / serverless state, `GA`) | `99.999%` multi-region strong consistency, real-time client listeners for UI streaming/HITL queues, and automatic document TTL policies | Hard **1 MiB max document size** and **~1 sustained write/sec per document** hotspot limit; **store turn events in subcollections** (`sessions/{id}/events/{eventId}`) rather than appending unbounded arrays inside one root document |
| **Memorystore for Redis / Valkey** (`GA`) | **`< 1 ms`** HNSW/FLAT vector semantic cache, sliding-window RPM/TPM rate limiters, and Pub/Sub `messageId` idempotency keys; scales up to **250 nodes / 25+ TB** | **Compliance audit trap:** relies on **asynchronous replication** and optional mutually exclusive **RDB snapshots or AOF (`appendfsync`) persistence** (legacy standalone Redis tiers are RDB-only); replica failover or key eviction can still lose recent in-flight writes, so never use Memorystore as the sole system of record or immutable audit ledger |
| **`GcsArtifactService`** (Cloud Storage, `GA`) | Versioned binary object hierarchy (`{app}/{user}/{session}/{filename}/{version}`), `user:` prefix for cross-session persistence, and **Zonal Rapid Storage buckets** for low-latency streaming | **Initialization trap:** leaving `Runner(artifact_service=None)` raises **`ValueError`** at runtime whenever a tool calls `ctx.save_artifact()`. Pass `gs://` URIs across A2A rather than multi-MB base64 A2A `Part` blobs that choke Agent Gateway `CONTENT_AUTHZ` |

### Service trade-offs

| Service | Latency profile | Consistency | Cost model | Ops burden |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Agent Platform Sessions + Memory Bank** | API calls on the hot path; memory generation runs asynchronously | Session reads/writes are immediate; memories converge after background consolidation | Managed usage-based pricing | Lowest |
| **Firestore** | Low (serverless document reads/writes) | Strong (`99.999%` multi-region), with ACID transactions | Per operation + storage | Very low (scales to zero) |
| **Memorystore** | Sub-millisecond (`< 1 ms`) in-memory | Strong on the primary; replicas are asynchronous (mutually exclusive RDB or AOF on Cluster/Valkey; RDB-only on legacy standalone Redis) | Provisioned capacity per hour | Low to medium (capacity sizing) |
| **Cloud SQL** | Low within the VPC | Strong relational ACID | Provisioned vCPU/RAM + storage | Medium (instances, pooling, indexes) |
| **AlloyDB** | Low, with `scann` vector and columnar analytical acceleration | Strong relational ACID | Provisioned primary and read pool nodes | Low to medium |
| **BigQuery** | Hundreds of ms to seconds per query | Strong after commit | Per data scanned or reserved slots + storage | Very low |
| **Cloud Storage** | Tens of ms to first byte (lower on Zonal Rapid buckets) | Strong read-after-write | Per GB-month by class + operations + egress | Lowest |
| **Agent Retrieval / Vector Search** | Single-digit to tens of ms ANN | Near real time for streaming updates | Usage-based (Agent Retrieval) or 24/7 node-hours (Vector Search 1.0) | Low |

> [!NOTE]
> Latency labels are directional. Benchmark with your own payload sizes and regions before committing to an SLO.

### Communication protocols & event-driven triggers

Match the transport or event broker to directionality, barge-in latency, delivery guarantees, and duration ceilings:

| Protocol or trigger | Direction & concurrency model | Timeout / duration ceiling | Primary fit & operational traps |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **SSE (`Server-Sent Events`)** (`StreamingMode.SSE`, A2A `/message:stream`) | Unidirectional `Server -> Client` stream over HTTP/1.1 or HTTP/2 for incremental text tokens, tool status, and chunked A2A artifacts | Up to **60 minutes** on Cloud Run / HTTP gateways | Ideal for chat UIs and short-to-medium A2A `SendStreamingMessage` progress (`SubscribeToTask` on reconnect); **cannot** support real-time voice barge-in (half-duplex) or multi-hour background jobs |
| **MCP `StreamableHTTP`** (`2026-07-28` stateless spec) | Stateless HTTP `POST` per request (`Mcp-Method`, `Mcp-Name`, `Mcp-Param-Region` headers) replying with JSON or a per-call SSE stream | Request-scoped tool RPC (seconds to minutes) | Standard remote MCP transport scaling horizontally behind load balancers with **no sticky `Mcp-Session-Id`**; legacy standalone `HTTP+SSE` dual-endpoint transport is deprecated |
| **Bidirectional Streaming (`Gemini Live API`)** (`gemini-3.8-live` over WebSockets / gRPC) | Full-duplex audio + video frame streaming (`runner.run_live`) with server-side VAD **barge-in** (`event.interrupted == True`) | Stateful streaming connection; persist **session resumption handles** to reconnect cleanly across WebSocket drops | Mandatory for sub-second voice/video front-doors on Agent Runtime or Cloud Run; **`gemini-4-argon` does not support Live WebSockets**, so delegate deep reasoning from `3.8-live` via `AgentTool` |
| **Pub/Sub Push & Eventarc** (`--trigger_sources pubsub,eventarc` -> Cloud Run or Agent Runtime) | Decoupled 1-to-N event fan-out with **at-least-once delivery**; tune Cloud Run `container_concurrency` (e.g., multiples of 9 such as `36` for async I/O-bound agent loops) | **600s (10-minute)** max Pub/Sub ack deadline (Cloud Run HTTP timeout up to 60 min) | **Duplicate-mutation trap:** slow multi-step turns exceeding the 600s ack deadline trigger redelivery and duplicate tool side effects. Enforce atomic **`messageId` idempotency checks** in Memorystore/Spanner/Firestore and attach a **Dead-Letter Topic (`maxDeliveryAttempts >= 5`)** |
| **Cloud Tasks** | Point-to-point queue with explicit **`maxDispatchesPerSecond`**, `maxConcurrentDispatches`, `scheduleTime` delayed execution, and OIDC token injection | Up to **30 minutes** per HTTP target attempt | Best for **rate-limiting / shock-absorbing** agent bursts so fragile legacy ERPs and project Gemini TPM/RPM quotas are never overwhelmed; **no 1-to-N pub-sub fan-out** |
| **Cloud Workflows & Cloud Run Jobs** | Deterministic serverless saga state machine (**Workflows**, `$0` idle wait + HTTP callbacks) vs. non-HTTP batch shards (**Cloud Run Jobs**, up to `10,000` parallel tasks) | Up to **1 year** (**Workflows**) / **24 hours** per shard (**Cloud Run Jobs**) | Use **Workflows** for multi-day human approval sleeps and deterministic compensation sagas invoking ADK / Agent Runtime for reasoning sub-steps; use **Cloud Run Jobs** for offline batch enrichment or eval suites (exposes no HTTP/SSE endpoint) |

### Reference architectures

| Component | Customer support agent | Data analysis agent | High-QPS public FAQ agent | Regulated-industry agent |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Runtime** | Agent Runtime | Agent Runtime | Cloud Run (autoscaled) | Agent Runtime (`AgentConnectivityTemplate`) + private GKE GPU / Model Garden `PrivateEndpoint` in VPC-SC |
| **Sessions** | `VertexAiSessionService` | `VertexAiSessionService` | Firestore subcollections or Memorystore (short-lived state) | `DatabaseSessionService` on AlloyDB/Spanner with PgBouncer, CMEK, and PSC |
| **Memory** | Memory Bank (device history, preferences) | Memory Bank (analyst preferences) | None (anonymous traffic) | Memory Bank with strict topics, SDP surrogates, and TTL, or none |
| **Knowledge and vectors** | Policy PDFs in Cloud Storage indexed by Agent Search or Agent Retrieval | BigQuery tables through `bigquery.googleapis.com/mcp` | Agent Retrieval behind a Memorystore semantic cache | AlloyDB `scann` vectors with row-level security next to transactional rows |
| **Tools and transactions** | Order/refund lookups via `ToolboxToolset` + CRM via `ApplicationIntegrationToolset` | Code Execution sandbox for Python; charts saved with `GcsArtifactService` | Memorystore sliding-window rate limits per IP or API key | Custom Cloud Run MCP (`--functional-type=mcp-server`) behind Cloud IAP + Agent Gateway |
| **Telemetry** | Cloud Trace + BigQuery eval sink | BigQuery cost and eval analytics | Cloud Monitoring cache hit rate + BigQuery logs | Dual-attribution Audit Logs to BigQuery; locked Cloud Storage retention bucket |

> **Common trap: Memorystore as the system of record.** Because Memorystore uses asynchronous replication (with optional mutually exclusive RDB snapshots or AOF on Redis Cluster/Valkey, and RDB-only on legacy standalone Redis), replica failover or key eviction can still drop recent in-flight writes. Keep authoritative orders, approvals, and audit records in Cloud SQL, AlloyDB, Spanner, or Firestore, and treat Memorystore entries as rebuildable.
