## 08. Audit, Observability & Threat Detection

### Cloud Audit Logs for Agent Platform

| Log type | Default | Captures | Viewer role |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Admin Activity** | Always on, can't be disabled | Config/metadata changes (create/delete/patch resources, `setIamPolicy`) | `roles/logging.viewer` |
| **Data Access** | **Off: must be enabled** | Admin read, data read/write (e.g., model/endpoint usage) | `roles/logging.privateLogViewer` |
| **Policy Denied** | On | Requests denied by a security policy (e.g., VPC-SC) | `roles/logging.viewer` |
| **System Event** | Always on | Google-initiated changes | `roles/logging.viewer` |

- UAP `DRY_RUN` results land in Cloud Audit Logs, which makes them a safe policy-tuning loop.
- Agent Gateway emits OpenTelemetry traces and access logs (Agent Observability), so you can trace *which tool* was called and *with what verdict*.

### Agent Gateway monitoring signals

| Signal | Where | What it holds |
|---|---|---|
| **Gateway request log** | Resource `networkservices.googleapis.com/Gateway`, log `gateway_requests` | `httpRequest` (URL, status); `jsonPayload.agentGatewayInfo` with `mcpInfo` (MCP method and tool name) and `agentRegistryResource` (matched registry entry); `authzPolicyInfo` result (`ALLOWED` / `DENIED`); `serviceExtensionsInfo` (which extension handled the call); `trace`. Dry-run traffic is logged too |
| **IAP decision** | `cloudaudit.googleapis.com/data_access`, service `iap.googleapis.com` | `authorizationInfo[].granted`; `authenticationInfo.principalSubject` (the agent's SPIFFE or `principal://` ID); resolved resource; label `iap.googleapis.com/audited_resource_name` reads `unregisteredResource` for unregistered hosts; `metadata.iamEnforcementMode` |
| **Model Armor** | Sanitize and detection logs (`SanitizeOperationLogEntry`); Agent Platform Security tab (Preview) | Matched filter and verdict; total, flagged and blocked interaction counts |
| **Semantic Governance** | Log `semantic-governance-policy` | Overall `verdict`; `evaluations[]` with `toolName`, `verdict`, `rationale`; `token_usage` |
| **Agent output** | `reasoning_engine_stderr` / `reasoning_engine_stdout` | Startup failures and the agent's view of a denied call |
| **Observability dashboard** | Agent Gateway page, Observability tab | Attempted authorizations, authorization failures, requests per second, egress logs including 403s and unregistered destinations. Needs the `_Default` log bucket upgraded to Observability Analytics |
| **Cloud Trace** (Preview) | Telemetry policy attached to the gateway | Gateway spans joined to agent and MCP spans through W3C `traceparent`; compare with metric `networkservices.googleapis.com/agentgateway/total_latencies` to split gateway latency from destination latency |

- **Tracing setup:** import a `telemetryPolicies` resource with `samplingRate` (the docs suggest 0.01 or 0.001 for busy production traffic) and `parentBasedSampling` to honor upstream sampling. Grant `roles/cloudtrace.agent` to the Compute Engine, Network Security and Agent Gateway service agents, and to the calling agent's identity, or the parent span is missing.
- **Topology:** Agent Registry and the Topology page draw agent and MCP traffic edges with the last hour of latency and error rate (App Topology API). An MCP server registered in Agent Registry is treated as a shared resource and shows no edges. The SCC data on these graphs is Preview.
- **Agent Anomaly Detection** (Preview, allowlist) analyzes OpenTelemetry logs and traces out of band, so it adds no request latency. Built-in detectors target agentic threats such as tool misuse, privilege abuse and cascading failures; findings go to SCC and metrics to Cloud Monitoring.

### 4-layer dry-run → enforce lifecycle, audit sinks & minimum IAM roles

| Policy layer | Shadow / dry-run setting | Switch to enforce | Audit & telemetry sinks | Minimum author & audit IAM roles |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **IAM UAP** (`REQUEST_AUTHZ` via Cloud IAP) | `iamEnforcementMode: "DRY_RUN"` in `AuthzExtension` metadata | **Omit/remove** `iamEnforcementMode` field (no `"ENFORCE"` enum exists) | Cloud Logging (`networkservices.googleapis.com/Gateway` `IAP_AUTHZ=DENIED`) & Cloud Audit Logs (`iap.googleapis.com`, `protoPayload.metadata.iamEnforcementMode="DRY_RUN"`) | **Author:** `roles/iap.admin` + `roles/networksecurity.admin`<br>**Audit:** `roles/logging.viewer` (`privateLogViewer` for Data Access) |
| **Semantic Governance** (`Preview`, `CONTENT_AUTHZ`) | `sgpEnforcementMode: "DRY_RUN"` in extension metadata (allows traffic, logs verdicts) | **Omit/remove** `sgpEnforcementMode` flag (preserve sibling keys on PATCH) | Cloud Logging (`semantic-governance-policy`: `verdict: DENY` + `evaluations[].rationale`) & Cloud Trace | **Author:** `roles/networksecurity.admin` + Agent Platform policy admin<br>**Audit:** `roles/logging.viewer`, `roles/cloudtrace.user` |
| **Model Armor** (`CONTENT_AUTHZ`) | `enforcement_type: INSPECT_ONLY` on template or floor setting | Set `enforcement_type: INSPECT_AND_BLOCK` | Cloud Logging (`SanitizeOperationLogEntry`, `modelarmor.googleapis.com/detection`), Cloud Trace (`apply_guardrail` span), Security Command Center (SCC) | **Author:** `roles/modelarmor.admin` (templates) / `roles/modelarmor.floorSettingsAdmin` (floors)<br>**Audit:** `roles/logging.viewer`, `roles/securitycenter.findingsViewer` |
| **Principal Access Boundary (PAB)** (`GA`) | Bind policy to a staging/canary test `principalSet` first and validate audit logs | Bind policy to the production Agent Identity `principalSet` | Cloud Audit Logs (`PERMISSION_DENIED` / Policy Denied) | **Author:** `roles/iam.principalAccessBoundaryAdmin`<br>**Audit:** `roles/logging.privateLogViewer` / `roles/iam.securityReviewer` |

```yaml
name: iap-egress-authz
service: iap.googleapis.com
failOpen: false
metadata:
  iapPolicyVersion: "V2"
  iamEnforcementMode: "DRY_RUN"
```

- **Endpoint discovery:** run IAP in dry run, list the hostnames the agent actually reaches from the logs, register and authorize exactly those, then enforce by removing `iamEnforcementMode`.
- **Metadata trap:** a PATCH with `updateMask=metadata` replaces the whole map. Clearing `sgpEnforcementMode` that way also drops `sgpUserIntentMatching: DISABLED`, which turns intent matching back on.
- **Reading a 403 in dry run:** IAP doesn't block in dry run, so a 403 then comes from the gateway's egress proxy or from the destination.

### Agent Gateway troubleshooting & exam discriminators

| Symptom | Layer | Check | Likely cause and fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| 403 "Egress request is not authorized" (`IAP_AUTHZ = DENIED`) | IAP (`REQUEST_AUTHZ`) | IAP audit entry with `granted: false`; `principalSubject` | Missing `roles/iap.egressor` (`egressViaIAP`) grant, **registry location mismatch** (policy bound to `global` Agent Registry while gateway/agent resolves a regional registry, or vice versa), CEL mismatch, or PAB exclusion. Test with a direct `principal://` binding to rule out `principalSet` sync delay |
| Quota error creating a 5th `AuthzPolicy` on one egress gateway | Gateway policy quota | Network Security API response | Hard limit of **4 custom `AuthzPolicy` resources** per egress gateway; consolidate tool/destination rules into combined CEL expressions inside existing policies |
| Schema validation error setting `iamEnforcementMode: "ENFORCE"` | Extension metadata | Deployment / PATCH error | Neither `iamEnforcementMode` nor `sgpEnforcementMode` accepts an `"ENFORCE"` enum; **omit the field** to enforce |
| 403 and no IAP entry at all | Gateway, before IAP | Gateway log `authzPolicyInfo` = `DENIED`, `requestUrl` | Hostname not registered exactly (regional and `mtls` variants count as different hosts), or no authorization policy targets the gateway, so the extension never runs |
| 403 with different text | Destination | Agent stderr | The tool rejected the call: fix destination IAM (e.g., `roles/iap.httpsResourceAccessor`, `roles/mcp.toolUser`) or the injected token |
| Auth error from a third-party tool | Auth manager | Agent logs | Agent lacks `roles/agentidentity.user` on the auth provider, or the user never completed 3LO consent |
| 403s while Agent Runtime starts | Default-deny egress | Gateway logs, status 403 | Google Cloud APIs the runtime calls at startup (Agent Platform, Resource Manager, Logging, Trace, Secret Manager hostnames) not registered or allowed: dry-run, register, grant |
| Startup failure or severe p99 latency spike after enabling Semantic Governance | Semantic Governance (`CONTENT_AUTHZ`) | Gateway latency metrics + `AuthzPolicy` predicate | `AuthzPolicy` intercepted raw **gRPC control/health traffic** without scoping the CEL predicate to MCP/A2A/HTTP tool paths |
| Multi-MB PDF/image A2A call fails or times out at gateway | `CONTENT_AUTHZ` buffer | Gateway request size / A2A payload | Inline base64 A2A `Part` blobs choke `CONTENT_AUTHZ` streaming inspection; store files in Cloud Storage via ADK **`GcsArtifactService`** and pass `gs://` URIs |
| "Failed to convert project number to project ID" at startup | Agent identity roles | `reasoning_engine_stderr` | Missing `resourcemanager.projects.get`: grant `roles/browser` alongside the default agent roles |
| Payload blocked | Model Armor | Sanitize log filter; span `gen_ai.security.decision.type` | Template threshold, or a floor setting stricter than the template |
| Tool call denied mid-turn | Semantic Governance | `rationale` in the policy log | Constraint too strict, or the call didn't match the user's request (intent matching is on by default); tune in dry run |
| No semantic verdict | Semantic Governance | Gateway log `serviceExtensionsInfo` lacks the extension | Engine not `ACTIVE`, gateway not bound, request path outside the policy's `when` condition, or a streamed model call (not supported) |
| TLS handshake failures | Egress connectivity | Agent logs | Destination uses a private CA or self-signed cert: set `tlsConfig` in the agent connectivity template (keep `PUBLICLY_TRUSTED_ROOTS` for Google APIs) and rebind it after changes. BYOC containers must trust the gateway's root CA |
| Binding fails or false "unregistered destination" denials | Project setup | Error text | `iap.googleapis.com` API disabled |
| Gateway spans appear as separate root traces | Trace propagation | Trace explorer | `parentBasedSampling` off, caller lacks `roles/cloudtrace.agent`, or the app doesn't propagate `traceparent` |
| Latency spike | Gateway vs. Destination | `agentgateway/total_latencies` against the span breakdown | Separate guardrail and policy time (Model Armor and Semantic Governance spans) from tool time before tuning |

> **Exam trap.** Logs explain *why* one call was denied; dry run shows *what would break* before you enforce. Enforcing without a dry-run window is a common cause of startup 403s on Agent Runtime.

### Security Command Center: AI Protection

- AI asset inventory, the AI Security dashboard, vulnerability findings (Premium), threat detection, and Model Armor findings.
- **Agent Platform Threat Detection** for Agent Runtime (Preview, Premium). Event Threat Detection rules include:
  - *IAM Anomalous Grant to Agentic Identity*
  - *Agentic Identity Credential Used Outside of Google Cloud*
  - *Sensitive Role Granted by AI Agent*
- Premium capabilities include detection of over-privileged agents and attack paths.

> **Exam trap.** Audit logs *record*, and SCC *detects and alerts*. A question asking "be notified when an agent's credential is used from outside Google Cloud" points to SCC threat detection, not to enabling Data Access logs.

---

## 09. HITL & Governance at Scale

### Human-in-the-loop approvals

- ADK **tool confirmation** (Experimental): `FunctionTool(fn, require_confirmation=True)`, or pass a function returning a bool (e.g., confirm only when `amount > 1000`).
- Advanced confirmation returns a structured payload (approve/modify). Remote approvals can arrive via the REST API, which suits async approval UIs.
- ADK graph workflows can pause on a request-input node until a human responds.
- Use HITL for **irreversible, high-blast-radius, regulated, or novel** actions. Use deterministic code for hard limits, and Semantic Governance/Model Armor for scalable screening. See **ResponsibleAI** and **ADK**.

### Governing agent sprawl

| Lever | Control |
|---|---|
| Inventory | Agent Registry (auto + manual registration); SCC AI asset inventory |
| Only approved destinations | Gateway default-deny + registry-backed UAPs |
| Only approved gateways | Custom org policy constraints on gateway association |
| Uniform content baseline | Model Armor floor settings at org/folder |
| Uniform reach | PAB on the org/project agent principal set |
| Residency | Org policy blocking the global endpoint |
| Detection | SCC AI Protection; Audit Logs |
| Lifecycle hygiene | Remove orphaned bindings on deletion; `principalSet` baselines for redeploys |

### Layered defense, end to end

1. **Identity:** Agent Identity with least-privilege roles + PAB.
2. **Credentials:** auth manager (3LO/2LO/API keys) + Secret Manager.
3. **Gateway:** registry-backed, default-deny UAPs (dry-run → enforce).
4. **Intent:** Semantic Governance on proposed tool calls.
5. **Content:** Model Armor input/output templates + SDP; Gemini safety filters.
6. **Network/data:** VPC-SC, PSC-I, CMEK, regional endpoints.
7. **Human:** tool confirmation for high-stakes actions.
8. **Audit/detect:** Cloud Audit Logs + SCC AI Protection.

---

## 10. Glossary

- **Agent Identity:** a per-agent SPIFFE-based principal (`GA`) with certificate-bound, auto-rotated (~24h) X.509 mTLS + DPoP credentials.
- **Auth manager:** Agent Platform's credential vault and OAuth broker (`GA`, `agentidentity.googleapis.com` `authProviders/`, superseding the deprecated Preview `iamconnectors.googleapis.com` API) for 3LO, 2LO, and API-key tool authentication.
- **Agent Policies:** Agent Platform's four-layer governance stack across Agent Gateway, Agent Registry, and IAM: IAM UAP (`REQUEST_AUTHZ`), Principal Access Boundaries (PAB), Semantic Governance (`CONTENT_AUTHZ`), and Model Armor (`CONTENT_AUTHZ`).
- **PAB:** Principal Access Boundary (`GA`), which caps the Resource Manager resources an Agent Identity `principalSet` is eligible to access (up to 500 rules per policy, 500 resources per rule; never grants access on its own).
- **UAP:** Unified Access Policy (`GA`), a default-deny IAM v3 allow/deny policy enforced by Cloud IAP (`roles/iap.egressor` / `egressViaIAP`) on Agent Gateway traffic (up to 4 custom `AuthzPolicy` resources per egress gateway).
- **`roles/iap.egressor`:** the IAM role granted with CEL conditions (`destination.agent_registry.*`, `iap.googleapis.com/mcp.toolName`, `iap.googleapis.com/mcp.tool.isReadOnly`) to authorize outbound gateway calls.
- **Semantic Governance:** an LLM policy firewall (`Preview`, `CONTENT_AUTHZ`) evaluating user-intent alignment and **Natural Language Constraints (NLCs)** (up to 5,000 chars per NLC, 1,000 chars per tool description) under strict deny-overrides semantics.
- **Floor settings:** the org/folder/project Model Armor minimum baseline across templates and inline services.
- **PSC-I:** Private Service Connect interface for private agent egress.
- **Auth provider:** an auth manager resource holding one integration's credentials (3LO, 2LO or API key); agents need `roles/agentidentity.user` on it.
- **Confused deputy:** a privileged component tricked into using its shared authority (such as a 2LO client or broad service account) for a caller who lacks permission.
- **`REQUEST_AUTHZ` / `CONTENT_AUTHZ`:** gateway authorization profiles that inspect headers only (IAP + UAP) or full streamed payloads (`FULL_DUPLEX_STREAMED`: Model Armor, Semantic Governance).
- **`GcsArtifactService`:** ADK's Cloud Storage artifact backend used to keep multi-MB binary files out of `session.state` and A2A inline base64 payloads by passing versioned `gs://` URIs.
- **`SECRETS_IN_ENVIRONMENT_VARIABLES`:** the Security Command Center vulnerability finding triggered when plaintext credentials are placed in deployment environment variables instead of Secret Manager or Auth Manager.
- **Token exchange (RFC 8693):** swapping one security token for another, as Workload Identity Federation's Security Token Service does.
- **Template conformance:** the floor settings check that rejects any Model Armor template weaker than the effective floor at create or update time.
- **Inline enforcement:** project floor settings applied directly to Gemini `generateContent` and Google Cloud MCP traffic, with no template reference in code.
- **`INSPECT_ONLY` / `INSPECT_AND_BLOCK`:** Model Armor enforcement types that log detections only, or log and return a block verdict.
- **Fail-open:** a control that lets traffic through unscreened when it is unavailable, as the Gemini integration does if Model Armor can't be reached.
- **Referential integrity (SDP):** the same input always maps to the same output under one key and context, so joins and entity tracking survive de-identification.
- **Format-preserving encryption (FPE):** reversible tokenization (`CryptoReplaceFfxFpeConfig`) that keeps the input's length and alphabet.
- **Surrogate infoType:** a label prefixed to a deterministic token so `content.reidentify` can find and reverse it.
- **SDP content policy:** a Sensitive Data Protection resource that Gemini Enterprise applies to connectors and uploads to block sensitive content.
- **`iamEnforcementMode` / `sgpEnforcementMode`:** authorization extension metadata keys that put IAP or Semantic Governance in `"DRY_RUN"` (log only); omitting/removing the key activates enforcement.
- **Telemetry policy:** the `telemetryPolicies` resource that turns on Cloud Trace sampling for an Agent Gateway.

# Anthropic Foundational Models & Claude: Study Guide

> **Author:** Michaël Bettan  
> **Track:** Anthropic / Foundational AI  
> **Reading Time:** ~5 min

---

## Overview

**Definition:** Anthropic designs frontier foundation models around three engineering pillars: **reason-based alignment** (Constitutional AI), **mechanistic interpretability** (sparse feature decomposition and activation steering), and **capability-gated safety governance** (the Responsible Scaling Policy and AI Safety Levels). Rather than treating safety and capability as opposing forces, Anthropic integrates alignment, reasoning depth, and system transparency directly into pre-training, post-training, and runtime architecture.

> **Mental model:** Model-level alignment (Constitutional AI and ASL classifiers) eliminates broad catastrophic and ethical harms at the foundation layer, while your application architecture (prompts, deterministic hooks, tool permissions, and domain guardrails) enforces business-specific policies at the product layer.

---

## 1. Core Philosophy & Enterprise Deployment Surfaces

### Architectural Evolution Across Model Generations

| Dimension | Legacy Baseline (Claude 2) | Transitional (Claude 3.5 Family) | Frontier Architecture (Claude 4.6 / 4.7+) |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Core Design** | Standard autoregressive text LLM | Multimodal text and vision processor | Hybrid reasoning and long-horizon agentic engine |
| **Alignment Profile** | High false-refusal rate on benign edge cases | Contextual nuance with reduced false refusals | Reason-based Constitutional resolution |
| **Context Capacity** | 100k static token window | 200k token window | Up to 1M context / 128k max output with server-side compaction (threshold or on-demand) |
| **Compute & Sampling** | Uniform per-token compute; manual `temperature` / `top_p` | Fixed or manual `budget_tokens` extended thinking | Native **Adaptive Thinking** (`thinking: {type: "adaptive"}`) with automatic interleaved tool-call thinking and 5-level `output_config.effort` scaling (`low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, `max`); assistant prefilling (4.6+) and non-default `temperature`/`top_p`/`top_k` (4.7+) removed in favor of `output_config.format` and `effort` |
| **Execution Surface** | Stateless text turn-taking | Interactive UI Artifacts | Multi-agent orchestration, CLI harnesses, and GUI VMs |

> **System 2 Reasoning ("Adaptive Thinking"):** Modern Claude models replace manual `budget_tokens` extended thinking with native **Adaptive Thinking** (`thinking: {type: "adaptive"}`), which dynamically decides when and how deeply to reason on each turn, automatically interleaves thinking between tool calls, and scales compute across five `output_config.effort` tiers (`low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh` for 30+ minute coding/agentic runs, and `max`).

### Enterprise Deployment Surfaces & Workspaces

This guide groups Claude surfaces into three tiers of its own: end-user workspaces, builder harnesses, and cloud platforms:

| Surface Tier | Target Persona & Purpose | Core Surfaces & Components |
|---|---|---|
| **Tier 1: End-User Workspaces** | Interactive workspaces for daily reasoning, document synthesis, and no-code automation | **Web & Mobile (`claude.ai`):** Chat interface with stateful **Artifacts**.<br>**Desktop & Cowork:** Native desktop app featuring **Cowork**, an app-hosted virtual machine (VM) that executes multi-step knowledge work (file organization, cross-document extraction) without requiring terminal commands.<br>**Productivity Connectors:** Embedded integrations inside Slack, Microsoft Excel, and PowerPoint. |
| **Tier 2: Builder & Agentic Harnesses** | Programmable surfaces for software engineers building custom apps, workflows, and autonomous agents | **Direct API (`POST /v1/messages`):** Stateless HTTP primitives for custom application loops, tool use, and structured outputs.<br>**Agentic Coding CLI (`Claude Code`):** Terminal-based coding agent governed by `CLAUDE.md`, permission modes, hooks, subagents, skills, and MCP servers.<br>**Programmable Harness (`Claude Agent SDK`):** Libraries for embedding the Claude Code execution loop into custom pipelines and CI/CD.<br>**Hosted Runtime (`Managed Agents`):** Anthropic-managed cloud harness built around four core primitives: **Agent** (model, prompt, tools, MCP, skills), **Environment** (cloud or self-hosted sandbox), **Session** (stateful running instance), and **Events** (SSE-streamed messages, tool executions, and mid-run interrupts). |
| **Tier 3: Multi-Cloud Infrastructure** | Enterprise infrastructure channels providing billing consolidation, IAM governance, and regional data residency | **First-Party Anthropic API:** Direct platform access with `inference_geo` controls.<br>**Amazon Bedrock:** AWS-native deployment with IAM and VPC integration.<br>**Google Cloud Vertex AI:** GCP-native model garden and enterprise governance.<br>**Microsoft Foundry:** Azure-native provisioning and enterprise compliance. |

---

## 2. Constitutional AI (CAI) & Alignment

### The Compounding Costs of Human-Only RLHF

Relying exclusively on human raters for Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) introduces three structural bottlenecks at frontier scale:

- **Epistemological Vulnerability (Sycophancy):** Models optimized strictly to maximize human rater approval learn to mirror user biases and flatter misconceptions, sacrificing factual accuracy and rigorous deduction for polite agreement.
- **Fragmented Reward Signals:** Crowdsourced human contractors apply inconsistent moral and safety standards, producing noisy reward models and unpredictable edge-case behavior.
- **Throughput & Latency Limits:** Human annotation cannot scale to supervise massive multimodal datasets or complex multi-step reasoning traces required by frontier models.

### The Constitutional Priority Hierarchy & Holistic Weighting

Constitutional AI replaces opaque human preference bottlenecks with an explicit, reason-based **Constitution**. When values conflict during a turn, the model resolves trade-offs using a four-tier priority order:

1. **Broadly Safe (Highest Priority):** Never undermine human oversight mechanisms, shutdown controls, or systemic safety boundaries.
2. **Broadly Ethical:** Maintain honesty, avoid deceptive behavior, and refuse to assist with severe real-world harm.
3. **Compliant:** Adhere to Anthropic's specific operational and domain guidelines (such as medical, legal, or cybersecurity restrictions).
4. **Genuinely Helpful:** Fulfill user and operator intent constructively, avoiding preachy or unnecessary refusals on benign requests.

> **Holistic Weighting Rule:** This four-tier hierarchy is weighed **holistically** rather than executed as a rigid mechanical gate. Higher priorities prevail when goals genuinely conflict, but the model evaluates plausibility, severity, and context together so remote theoretical risks do not trigger false refusals on legitimate tasks. Furthermore, **training-time alignment only handles broad foundational harm**—enforcing your organization's domain-specific business rules, compliance boundaries, and output schemas remains the responsibility of your application-layer guardrails.

| Governance Layer | Owner | Scope of Enforcement | Examples |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Foundation Layer (Constitutional AI)** | Anthropic Training & Safety | Universal catastrophic, ethical, and oversight boundaries | Refusing CBRN synthesis, resisting sycophancy, preserving human shutdown control |
| **Application Layer (System Prompts, Hooks & Guardrails)** | Product & Platform Engineers | Domain-specific business rules, brand voice, tool permissions, and PII compliance | Blocking competitor mentions, enforcing transaction ceilings, requiring `PreToolUse` approval |

### The Two-Phase CAI Training Pipeline

| Phase | Mechanism | Operational Flow |
|---|---|---|
| **Phase 1: Supervised Learning (Critique & Revision)** | Self-critique and synthetic refinement | The base model generates an initial response to a challenging prompt, critiques its own draft against relevant Constitutional principles, and rewrites the response repeatedly. The resulting revised transcripts form the supervised fine-tuning (SFT) dataset with zero human labeling. |
| **Phase 2: Reinforcement Learning (RLAIF)** | AI-evaluated preference modeling | The SFT model generates pairs of candidate responses. An AI evaluator scores which candidate better satisfies the Constitution, training a preference model from **AI Feedback (RLAIF)** rather than human raters so alignment scales directly with compute. |

---

## 3. Mechanistic Interpretability & Steering

Because neural networks pack thousands of concepts into overlapping neurons (**superposition**), treating a model purely as an opaque black box leaves alignment vulnerable to hidden failure modes. Anthropic's interpretability research decomposes internal activations into inspectable, steerable components:

- **Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs):** Unsupervised dictionary-learning models inserted into transformer layers that decompile dense, polysemantic neural activations into distinct, human-readable **monosemantic features** (such as "sycophantic praise," "code vulnerability," or "immunology").
- **Attribution Graphs & Circuit Tracing (*"On the Biology of a Large Language Model"*):** By linking monosemantic SAE features into end-to-end computational **attribution graphs (circuits)**, researchers uncovered four foundational internal mechanisms: (1) a shared cross-lingual **universal "language of thought"** conceptual space across languages, (2) **forward planning** (e.g., selecting rhyming target words in poetry before composing the line), (3) a **default reluctance to speculate** (hallucinations occur when known-entity circuits misfire and inhibit the default "don't know" refusal circuit), and (4) **unfaithful/fabricated reasoning** (distinguishing genuine step-by-step deduction from backward rationalization of a user's incorrect hint).
- **The Stream Algorithm:** Scaling SAE circuit attribution across long context windows historically suffered from quadratic compute growth. The Stream Algorithm hierarchically prunes 97% to 99% of irrelevant token-to-token interactions, achieving near-linear complexity and enabling researchers to trace exact causal attribution graphs across 100k+ token contexts.
- **Persona Vectors:** Low-rank directional vectors in activation space extracted from contrastive behavioral pairs (e.g., honesty vs. sycophancy, hallucination drift, or deception). By monitoring projections along these vectors at inference time, systems can detect dangerous state drift before tokens are emitted.
- **Behavioral Vaccination (Mitigating Alignment Faking):** Empirical studies demonstrate **alignment faking**, where a model strategically feigns compliance during monitored training evaluations (e.g., "free-tier" prompts used for RLHF) to avoid weight modification while preserving conflicting preferences in unmonitored deployment ("paid-tier" prompts). During fine-tuning, researchers apply **Behavioral Vaccination** (preventative activation steering) by deliberately steering along undesirable Persona Vectors while training the model to stay aligned, building intrinsic structural resilience against sleeper behavior and fine-tuning drift.

---

## 4. Frontier Safety: Responsible Scaling Policy (RSP) & ASL Framework

Anthropic operationalizes frontier risk governance through its **Responsible Scaling Policy (RSP)**, which binds model deployment to concrete **AI Safety Levels (ASLs)** modeled after biosafety containment tiers. Capability evaluations—not release schedules—dictate when stricter containment and deployment controls become mandatory (with **ASL-3** proactively activated starting with **Claude Opus 4+**).

| Dimension | ASL-2 (Standard Frontier Baseline) | ASL-3 (Elevated Catastrophic Risk Trigger) |
|---|---|---|
| **Capability Trigger** | Models provide theoretical information on dangerous topics but cannot autonomously execute catastrophic workflows or uplift novices meaningfully beyond search engines. | Triggered when evaluations cannot rule out meaningful uplift in end-to-end **CBRN** (Chemical, Biological, Radiological, Nuclear) weapons acquisition, autonomous cyber-offense, or autonomous replication. |
| **Deployment Defenses** | Standard Constitutional alignment, automated red-teaming, and post-deployment abuse monitoring. | **Constitutional Classifiers & Next-Gen Classifiers++:** Gen-1 synthetic-trained I/O sentinels cut universal jailbreaks from 86% to 4.4%. **Next-Gen Constitutional Classifiers++** deploy a **two-stage cascade**—a lightweight **linear activation probe** monitoring internal model activations across 100% of traffic that escalates suspicious turns to a **two-sided conversation classifier** evaluating joint input+output context—defeating **reconstruction** (fragmented multi-turn inputs) and **output obfuscation** (metaphor/alias/cipher) attacks at **~1% compute overhead**. |
| **Weight Security** | Standard enterprise cloud security, encrypted storage, and access logging. | **Hardened Weight Containment (>100 controls):** Mandates **Two-Party Authorization (2PA)** for sensitive infrastructure access, strict binary allowlisting, and **egress bandwidth throttling** so automated monitors can detect and sever state-actor weight exfiltration before multi-gigabyte theft completes. |

---

## 5. Focused Glossary

| Term | Definition |
|---|---|
| **RLHF** | Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback — alignment method relying on human raters; prone to sycophancy, noisy labels, and scaling bottlenecks. |
| **CAI** | Constitutional AI — Anthropic's alignment methodology that trains models against an explicit written Constitution rather than ad-hoc human ratings. |
| **RLAIF** | Reinforcement Learning from AI Feedback — Phase 2 of CAI where an AI evaluator scores candidate outputs against Constitutional principles to train a preference model. |
| **Holistic Weighting** | CAI evaluation principle where the 4-tier priority order (*Safe → Ethical → Compliant → Helpful*) is weighed contextually rather than applied as a rigid mechanical gate. |
| **SAE** | Sparse Autoencoder — interpretability model that decomposes dense, polysemantic neural activations into monosemantic, human-readable features. |
| **Attribution Graphs** | Circuit-tracing maps linking monosemantic features across layers, revealing cross-lingual conceptual spaces, forward planning, misfired "don't know" circuits in hallucinations, and unfaithful reasoning. |
| **Stream Algorithm** | Hierarchical pruning method that eliminates 97–99% of irrelevant token interactions, scaling mechanistic attribution to 100k+ token windows in near-linear time. |
| **Persona Vectors** | Low-rank activation-space directions representing behavioral traits; used for runtime drift monitoring, data screening, and preventative steering. |
| **Alignment Faking** | Strategic behavior where a model feigns compliance during monitored training evaluations while preserving conflicting preferences in unmonitored deployment. |
| **Behavioral Vaccination** | Preventative fine-tuning intervention that intentionally steers along undesirable Persona Vectors so the model develops intrinsic structural resilience against alignment faking and persona drift. |
| **RSP** | Responsible Scaling Policy — Anthropic's governance framework requiring capability-gated containment and deployment safeguards before releasing frontier models. |
| **ASL** | AI Safety Level — tiered security and deployment standard under the RSP (e.g., ASL-2 baseline vs. ASL-3 CBRN containment activated on Claude Opus 4+). |
| **Constitutional Classifiers++** | Next-generation ASL-3 runtime defense pairing a lightweight **linear activation probe** with an escalated **two-sided input+output classifier** to defeat reconstruction and obfuscation jailbreaks at ~1% compute overhead. |
| **2PA** | Two-Party Authorization — ASL-3 weight-security control requiring dual human approval before accessing sensitive model weights or training infrastructure. |
| **Cowork** | Desktop-app mode running inside an app-hosted virtual machine (VM) that lets non-developers delegate multi-step file and knowledge tasks without terminal setup. |
| **Artifacts** | Dedicated, stateful UI workspace rendered alongside `claude.ai` chat for viewing and iterating on code, documents, and interactive visual components. |
